description: Yakami Orchards grow their yuzu in the Miyazaki Prefecture of Japan, a region renowned for the quality of its citrus. This Japanese sauce combines the brightness of yuzu with savory notes of bonito and kombu seaweed. Salty, savory, and citrusy, combine it with soy sauce or tamari for an easy-yet-complex dipping sauce, or use it as a marinade.

name: Yoka Miso Garbanzo, 8oz
description:
The first and only Seattle-Based Miso company. Woman-owned and family operated, they are dedicated at Yoka Miso to producing the highest quality miso paste in the PNW. Their garbanzo bean (chickpea) miso paste offers a lighter, sweeter flavor, compared to their traditional soybean miso while still holding the deep umami flavor that miso has to offer. It is a Sugiyama Family favorite and is regularly used in their household.

The garbanzo miso is also a great alternative to those who cannot consume soy. Fermented for a minimum of 7 months--each batch varies in color depending on fermentation time. This miso is also ALIVE. They do not kill off our rice yeast, so it will continue to ferment if you do not stick it in the refrigerator.

name: Yoka Miso Traditional, 8oz
description:

The traditional soybean miso is the staple product and the reason for Yoka Miso. Our traditional miso can be described as a rich, authentic Japanese miso paste crafted using time-honored fermentation methods. The texture of our miso has a more rustic feel-it is "chunky" in that we do not blend our miso into a fine paste. Our miso is one of the best emulsifiers out there.

Yoka miso is fermented for a minimum of 7 months and each batch varies in color depending on fermentation time. The miso is also ALIVE. We do not kill off our rice yeast, so it will continue to ferment if you do not stick it in the refrigerator.

description:

name: CiCi's Italian Birthday Cake Cookies, 8oz

description: La Florentine candied chestnuts a sweet/savory treat that will for sure go well with that glass of port or gelato after dinner.

name: Baratti & Milano Caramella Di Torino Classica, 200g
description: The most historic candy produced by Baratti & Milano, was once one of the most famous. This elegant hard candy is made from real fruit. This elegant candy, "Classica Caramella", Classic candy, was created for the first time at Baratti & Milano in 1911, during the International Fair of Turin. A matchless recipe of fresh and delicate flavors natural fruits, gives it it's rich taste. These candies have a classic shape, and unmistakable butterfly "farfalla" wrappings. Their flavors include: strawberry, lemon, mint and bilberry (a European style blueberry).

name: Bonomi Lady Fingers, 500g
description: The Bonomi family has been baking delicious breads and confections since 1850. Often used as an accompaniment to ice-cream, custards and coffee, lady fingers are long, thin cookies designed to turn spongy when soaked in liquor or covered with ice cream. Most notably, they are the critical ingredient in tiramisu - the famous italian dessert consisting of ladyfingers soaked in espresso, mascarpone, liquor and cocoa powder.

name: Confectionately Yours English Toffee, 8oz
description: Made with loving care right here in Seattle by our great friend Sweet Sue - this recipe dates back over 50 years. If you don't believe us, ask anyone who has been lucky enough to be at DeLaurenti when Sweet Sue is kind enough to come down and sample her amazing toffee!! Made by hand using only the finest ingredients, it is easily the best toffee you will ever eat!!

name: Coufidou Prunes, 450g
tagline: Agen Prunes Stuffed with Prunes Mousse
description: The stuffed Prunes of Agen (Pruneaux d’Agen Fourrés) are a classic holiday delicacy, ranking as one of the most prestigious gifts in France. Splendid, full-bodied Agen Prunes are pitted, dried, gently rehydrated, and—delight of delights—filled generously with a smooth purée of their own fruit, delicately flavored with lemon peel and vanilla. name: Bonomi Amaretti, 200g
description: The Bonomi family has been baking delicious breads and confections since 1850. With a flavor that is reminiscent of childhood, these amaretti cookies are crisp and crunchy on the outside with a soft center. They are excellent eaten as is, with coffee, or dessert wines. They are also perfect crumbled on vanilla ice cream, or into the crust of a delicious amaretti cake.

name: Antonio Mattei Almond Biscotti, 250g
description: Since 1858, Antonio Mattei has been producing Italian biscotti and confections in their historical bakery and shop located on Via Ricasoli, in the heart of the old city of Prato, Tuscany. The bakery has been run by the Pandolfini family for 3 generations. Throughout Tuscany, these biscotti are considered the standard-bearer. Their size, texture and taste are synonymous with quality and tradition. Made only with flour, farm fresh eggs which impart a golden yellow color, sugar, almonds, and pine nuts. Traditionally enjoyed at the end of a meal with a glass of Vin Santo, they are also perfect with coffee, gelato or panna cotta.

name: Dandelion Hot Chocolate Mix, 5.6oz
tagline: Built to withstand foggy cold mornings in SF & Seattle!
description:
Dandelion Chocolate's classic Hot Chocolate is rich, subtly sweet, and deeply chocolatey. Inside each bottle includes the hot chocolate mix made from the 70% Camino Verde, Ecuador single-origin chocolate they use for their house hot chocolate drinks, and, of course, a basic recipe for the home hot chocolate enthusiast.

Each bottle makes four servings.

name: Jonboy Fleur de Sel Caramel Sauce, 8oz
tagline: A local Seattle favorite since 2009!
description: Jonboy Caramels started as a side gig for close friends Jonathan Sue and Jason Alm in 2008. Working on a four-burner stove in a small Ballard room, the two friends developed recipes for their unforgettable small batch caramels. They worked with the finest Northwest and organic ingredients available. They knew they were onto something, but few others did. Enter the Ballard Farmers Market, which offered them a stand in 2009. Fast forward a decade and change and their now-famous caramels can be found throughout the region. We’re especially fond of their velvety caramel sauce with just the right touch of French sea salt. Enjoy it with sliced apples, chocolate, and over ice cream!

tagline: A local Seattle favorite since 2009!

Finally each individual bonbon is sealed in a foil envelope so that it will always taste as fresh as the day they were made. They make an amazing gift, to someone you love, or to yourself!

tea.

name: Bonne Maman Raspberry Tartlet, 135g

fruit in their products. Their Tartelettes Framboise may not rival your French

wrapped tartelettes make great tea cookies, a light dessert, or a mid-afternoon pick-me-

up.

name: DeLaurenti Candied French Lemon Strips, 4oz

description: You don't need to get ready, because you stay ready. These crunchy little wafer cookies piped with creamy nutella are the same way. 6 individual cookies, individually wrapped for readiness!

name: Fogliani Anise Pizzelle, 5oz
description: Never had a pizzelle cookie you say? Time to change that. These classic anise cookies from Abruzzo are made by pouring batter in a pizzelle iron and cooking them like a waffle. They are one of Nate's all time favorites...soon to be yours too!

name: Fogliani Vanilla Pizzelle, 5oz

name: Gavottes Crepe Dentelle Dark Chocolate, 90g
description: We aren't sure how you make a cookie this light, crisp and delicious. The answer to this mystery has been a closely held secret by the folks at Gavottes in Brittany since 1920. As legend goes, these cookies are the result of a pancake left too long on the stove by Marie-Catherine Cornic in Quimper, in 1893. When she folded it, rolled it up and popped it in her mouth, the crispy Brittany crepe was born! Enrobed in dark chocolate, these crispy Crepe Dentelles are perfect right out of the box, or as an accompaniment to vanilla ice cream.

name: Gavottes Crispy Crepe Biscuits Milk Chocolate, 90g
description: Gavottes, so the story goes, began with a mistake—an overcooked crepe. But when the crepe was rolled and cool, it was delightfully crispy. So popular was the biscuit that emerged, it has been a French favorite for a century. Still made by the same company in Brittany, the buttery biscuits are light and golden. Chocolate lovers will rejoice at the combination of flaky biscuit and milk chocolate. Perfect with champagne, tea, coffee and ice cream. Or live on the edge and steal one midday.

name: Gavottes Crispy Crepes, 125g
description: Gavottes, so the story goes, began with a mistake—an overcooked crepe. But when the crepe was rolled and cool, it was delightfully crispy. So popular was the biscuit that emerged, it has been a French favorite for a century. Still made by the same company in Brittany, the buttery biscuits are light and golden and flaky. Wrapped by twos in gold foil, Gavottes add a refined touch to ice cream or make a great accompaniment to coffee, tea, or champagne.

name: Little Belgians Speculoos Cookies, 136g
description: These buttery speculoos cookies are thin, crunchy, and not too sweet. Little Belgians Original Speculoos pair perfectly with chilled Riesling, Prosecco, Chardonnay, and Rose. Of course, they are also an ideal snack all on their own! Each gabled box contains a heat sealed bag with 16 cookies.

Likewise, fresh baked bread that is still warm is equally hard to come by. Even slicing, oiling and grilling a nice baguette takes effort. Piadina is the cure. Build pizzas and fire them at home...oil up both sides and brown in a skillet until crunchy/chewy and top with a pinch of sea salt...pair with meats cheeses & antipasti...you can even store them in the freezer until you are ready to use them! There is literally no downside. Buy these, you won't regret it.

Enjoy the classic blend of sesame, poppy seed, black pepper, garlic, and onion—a nostalgic nod to your favorite breakfast, now with a satisfying crunch. Perfect for snacking, pairing with dips, or adding to your next charcuterie board.

Historically, it was a staple of shepherds who needed a shelf-stable bread to last through the long winters and transhumance. This variation, paper-thin with a drizzle of olive oil & rosemary, is known as pane guttiau in Sardinian. It is enjoyed as a delicate and savory cracker that can pair with anything from olives to cheese and charcuterie. The poetic name of Pane di Musica evokes sheets of parchment used for notating music.

name: Storye Classic Rye Bread
description: Storye (Stor-eye) is made in Riga by the Laci Bakery, a traditional maker of dense, dark Latvian rye breads made with just a few ingredients. Everything is done by hand, using wooden tools and baked slowly in wood-fired brick ovens. Using only locally-grown rye—and no wheat—the dough is naturally fermented with a starter handed down from the bakery founder’s grandmother, which gives it a malty tang. Their Classic Rye is moist and rich with a full, zesty flavor. Latvians use it for open-faced sandwiches, sometimes just with a simple smear of butter. Or layer it with pastrami, sauerkraut, Swiss cheese, and Russian dressing for the perfect Reuben sandwich.

name: Storye Fine Rye Bread
description: Storye (Stor-eye) is made in Riga by the Laci Bakery, a traditional maker of dense, dark Latvian rye breads made with just a few ingredients. Everything is done by hand, using wooden tools and baked slowly in wood-fired brick ovens. Using only locally-grown rye—and no wheat—the dough is naturally fermented with a starter handed down from the bakery founder’s grandmother, which gives it a malty tang. Their Fine Rye is lighter in texture than their Classic Rye because they remove the hard exterior of the rye berry before milling, which creates a more refined rye flour. The addition of caraway seeds gives the Fine Rye extra zing. Slices of this loaf will remind you of the best Jewish deli rye you’ve ever sampled.

name: St. Jude Mediterranean Tuna, 6oz
description: The Malleys are a family business based in Seattle. Joe Malley started out salmon trolling in Sitka, Alaska in 1978. The result is an amazing quality tuna packed in it's own juice and nothing else. Perfect for sandwiches, pasta, antipasti, or right out of the can!

name: Ekone Smoked Habanero Hots Oysters, 85g
description:
Since 1980, the shellfish farmers behind Ekone have been smoking local oysters in one of the country's few independent canneries, on the shores of Willapa Bay, Washington.

In their Habanero Hots tin, each oyster is immersed in two distinct, flavorful Habanero sauces, infusing them with the perfect level of heat. The oysters are then carefully placed on stainless steel racks and gently cold-smoked, preserving their natural umami flavor while adding a smoky depth. These smoked oysters are a must-try for anyone craving a bold, spicy, and smoky treat!

name: Ekone Smoked Lemon Pepper Oysters, 85g

We take it a step further by infusing these oysters with a subtle yet enticing lemon pepper spice blend, adding a zesty kick that perfectly complements the smoky undertones. A great choice for seafood lovers looking for a flavorful snack with a balance of smokiness and citrusy tang.

name: Ekone Smoked Original Oysters, 85g

description:
Ati Manel, originally formed in 1922 by its namesake, exemplified the Portuguese tradition of freshly canned seafood through the late 1950s. When Luís Mendonça, already a successful artist, discovered his great-grandfather’s weathered canning relics more than 60 years after the business passed with Manel into family lore, he was inspired to resurrect the legacy. While researching notes from fishermen and international purveyors, it became clear that close, personal relationships were just as important to Manel as sourcing high quality, local, and raw materials in his tins. Luís has re-captured uniquely distinct flavors and feelings that have set the table again, inviting us all to join the Manel family’s tradition in a tin.

This tin of Ati Manel Garfish are more spicy (plus chilli pepper) than spiced (there’s no clove, bay, or pickled vegetables).

name: Bokksu Japanese Mackerel, 85g
tagline: Saba in Olive Oil
description:
Sourced from the coastal waters of Nagasaki and Saga, Japan, this Bokksu Original saba (mackerel) is gently prepared in smooth olive oil to preserve its natural tenderness and full-bodied flavor. A staple in Japanese kitchens, saba is prized for its flaky texture and satisfying richness.

What Makes This Saba Special?

Saba (Japanese mackerel) is known for its hearty flavor and high nutritional value. Unlike milder white fish, it brings a richer bite that stands up well in bold or simple preparations alike. Packed in olive oil, it stays moist and ready to use whenever inspiration strikes.

name: Bokksu Spicy Japanese Sardines, 85g
tagline: Iwahi In Olive Oil And Togarashi Pepper
description:
Bold yet balanced, this Bokksu Original iwashi (Japanese sardines) from Miyazaki, Japan is prepared in olive oil and finished with togarashi pepper. The olive oil preserves the fish’s tender texture and clean, savory flavor, while the togarashi adds gentle warmth and layered spice from the first bite.

What Makes This Iwashi Special?

Iwashi are prized in Japanese cooking for their soft flake and approachable flavor. Compared to heavier fish, they offer a lighter texture that absorbs seasoning beautifully. The addition of togarashi, a classic Japanese chili blend, brings mild heat and subtle complexity without overpowering the fish.

name: Bokksu Young Japanese Anchovies, Shirasu with Mentaiko, 80g
tagline: Shirasu With Mentaiko
description:
Bokksu's tinned fish line primarily focuses on shirasu (tiny young anchovies or whitebait) freshly caught in Japan's Miyazaki Port and packed in premium cottonseed oil. Rather than standard fillets, these are tiny, delicate whole fish that provide a buttery texture and intense umami flavor, making them ideal as a gourmet garnish.

These delicate shirasu (anchovies) are freshly caught from Miyazaki Port and preserved in cottonseed oil blended with savory mentaiko (cod roe)—a prized Japanese delicacy. The result is a briny, buttery-rich seafood flavor that’s as versatile as it is delicious.

Sprinkle them over omelets, rice balls, pasta, or appetizers for a bold seafood twist. The infused oil doubles as a flavor booster for sushi rolls or dipping sauces!

name: Bokksu Young Japanese Anchovies,Shirasu with Pepper 80g
tagline: Shirasu With Black pepper & Basil-Infused
description:
Bokksu's tinned fish line primarily focuses on shirasu (tiny young anchovies or whitebait) freshly caught in Japan's Miyazaki Port and packed in premium cottonseed oil. Rather than standard fillets, these are tiny, delicate whole fish that provide a buttery texture and intense umami flavor, making them ideal as a gourmet garnish.

Simple, buttery, and rich in umami, these shirasu (anchovies) are caught fresh in Miyazaki Port and preserved in cottonseed oil infused with basil and black pepper for a refined, savory experience.

Versatile and nutrient-packed, they’re perfect for adding depth to pasta sauces, stir-fries, onigiri, white rice, salads, or even as a garnish for pizza. Use the leftover anchovy oil as a delicious base for salad dressings or marinades!

name: Cambados Sea Urchin Caviar
description: The sea urchin coming exclusively from the Galician Rias is an increasingly coveted delicacy. Its laborious production consists of extracting the whole roe (caviar) and cleaning them extremely delicately. It can be enjoyed on its own without any condiments to not alter its exquisite taste, smell, or texture.

name: Colatura Di Gambero Rosso, 200ml
description: Colatura di Gambero Rosso from Mazara del Vallo is a unique food product, obtained by extracting the precious juices and eggs contained in the shells and heads of the Mazara red prawn. It is ideal for stirring into first courses, soups, enhancing bruschetta, or gourmet pizzas. Originating from centuries-old maritime tradition, Colatura di Gambero Rosso was used by fishermen to enrich soups and fish-based dishes. Today, this condiment has been reinvented to bring the unique flavor of the Mazara red prawn directly to your kitchen.

name: Conservas de Cambados Octopus in Galacian Sauce, 111g
Conservas de Cambados Octopus in Olive Oil, 111g
Conservas de Cambados Sterilized Cuttlefish ink, 90g
description: Discover the key to crafting exquisite Spanish dishes with Conservas De Cambados Cuttlefish ink. Sourced from the unspoiled Spanish coastline, this luscious ink boasts a deep, robust taste and vibrant hue that is revered in Mediterranean cooking. An essential ingredient in classic paellas, risottos, pastas, and seafood sauces, Cuttlefish Ink adds a dash of versatility and allure to your kitchen repertoire.

name: Donostia Cod Fish in Biscayne Sauce, 111g
description:
Cod fish (bacalao) in this style is synonymous with Basque Country. The tinned version is a take on the traditional dish that allows maximum enjoyment of the flavorful offering found at tapas bars across the country in convenient fashion.

The preparation for each tin is simple: the cod is cut, dusted in rice flour and lightly (very lightly, tenderly, gently) fried in olive oil then tinned, with a touch of heat finishing the process.

name: Fratelli Polli Italian Antipasto, 7.4oz
description: Fratelli Polli is an Italian food company from Milan formed in 1872. They produce a range of preserved vegetables and sauces sold in glass jars. Their Italian Antipasto is a mix of vegetables and tuna in a tomato sauce. It’s excellent served as an appetizer, as a flavorful spread for sandwiches, or add it to a basic marinara sauce and use it as a pasta sauce.

name: Iasa Grilled Branzino, 145g
description: Branzino can be hard to come by, even if you have a great fish guy. Keep it at the ready safely tucked away in your cupboard until the need arises! This fish is sustainably caught, lightly grilled and hand-packed in olive oil. It's great on grilled bread with a drizzle of good olive oil and a pinch of sea salt, served aloft a pile of fresh greens, or eaten right out of the tin with a fork!

name: IASA Spicy Anchovies, 200g
description:
Ittica Alimentare Salerno (IASA) packs anchovies caught off the Amalfi Coast, doing most of the work by hand in traditional fashion. They layer the anchovies in drums with sea salt before hand-packing the anchovies in jars. Their Spicy Anchovies are marinated in olive oil and smoky chile paste. The sharp brininess of the fish gets a kick from the pepper yet isn’t overwhelmed by the spiciness. They add zip to dishes like

puttanesca sauce or Caesar dressing, but also make a great appetizer on a piece of crusty bread.

name: Les Mouettes d'Arvor Mackerel Fillets in Escabeche Sauce, 169g
description: Les Mouettes d’Arvor hails from the old port town of Concarneau in Brittany. The third-generation cannery is run by the Gonidec family. All their canned fish are fresh, never frozen, caught in a sustainable fashion, and prepared by traditional methods with natural ingredients. Escabeche Sauce is a sweet and sour tomato sauce seasoned with paprika, vinegar, and wine. The delicate mackerel fillets are excellent straight from the tin, over a salad, or as part of a picnic with bread, cheese, and fruit.

Their production is completely artisanal, inspired by the simple but precise rules of the local anchovy traditions. Colatura di Alici is produced by drawing off the liquid given off by curing anchovies under salt, and is an easy way to add concentrated umami flavor to a dish without having to rinse, filet and chop the little fish. Mix a teaspoon of colatura with a few tablespoons of olive oil and some crushed garlic, and you’ve got an instant flavorful sauce for spaghetti, potatoes, or sauteed greens. Sprinkle a few drops on roasted vegetables, fresh tomatoes, avocado slices, roasted meat, scallops, Caesar salad, and any other dish that could use a quick umami kick! This is the famous Amalfi anchovy sauce.

tagline: This is an important sauce...seriously.
description: Simply put, these Bachan sauces are amazing. A staff favorite, it is the product of Justin Gill's Japanese family heritage, distilled and contained in an easy to use, delicious bottle of homemade sauce. Bachan means 'granny' in Japanese and this sauce tastes like your granny made it. The gluten free version is made with tamari rather than traditional soy sauce, and you wouldn't know the difference. It is what you want to drizzle over your rice bowl with grilled vegetables, whatever meat you had the night before & and a fried egg. Add some chopped scallions & some toasted sesame seeds and you're set. Not as salty as soy sauce & loaded with fresh scallions, garlic & ginger! Great as a condiment & fantastic as a quick marinade! Did we mention it's one of the coolest labels ever as well? That part is free of charge.

name: Galbusera Gluten Free Zero Grano Crackers, 8 x 40g
description: Can't have wheat and looking for a great platform for your favorite cheeses? Look no further. Imported from Italy, Galbusera Gluten-Free crackers are made with corn, rice, and just a touch of salt. Pleasant on their own, but mild enough to allow you to enjoy tasting whatever you put on them! These crackers come in convenient 8 individual packs!

name: Natural Nectar GF Cracklebred, 100g
description: These gluten free blank slates of awesomeness are ready to do exactly what they are told. No delusions about being the lead singer in the band. They live to serve. So...pile them with your favorite cheese, charcuterie, dips or spreads and call it good!

name: Momofuku Restaurant Grade Tamari, 8oz
description: Meet Momofuku Tamari. If you’re used to grocery store tamari, you’ve never had anything like this. Their restaurant-grade version is made from organic ingredients and steeped with kombu to unlock a world of depth and flavor. It's built on 10 years of flavor research at the Momofuku Culinary Lab and now they are making them available to home cooks for the first time! Naturally gluten free and packed with flavor!

name: Caputo Fioreglut Gluten Free Flour, 1000g
description:
The Antimo Caputo line of flours is one of Italy’s premium brands for authentic

Neapolitan pizza, bread, and desserts. Their Fioreglut Gluten Free Flour is a great all-

natural alternative for those allergic to or avoiding gluten. You’ll be pleasantly surprised

at how pizza crust and bread made with this flour achieve a texture and taste that

resembles traditional loaves and crusts.

name: Primo Pan GF Drolo, 12oz
tagline: Gluten Free Dark Chocolate Hazelnut Cookies!
description: In the village of Battifollo on the Cuneo side of the Ligurian Alps, the Biga family bakes small lots of wonderful cookies according to local recipes. These gluten-free cookies are made with 40% Piedmont hazelnuts, egg white, sugar, cocoa and vanilla. Crunchy and light, this is a flourless cookie that tastes like a chocolate brownie on a cloud. Perfect with a glass of cold or steamed milk or with a caffe latte.

name: Primo Pan GF Volo, 12oz
tagline: Gluten Free Dark Chocolate Almond Cookies!
description: In the village of Battifollo on the Cuneo side of the Ligurian Alps, the Biga family bakes small lots of wonderful cookies according to local recipes. Inspired by Primo Pan's best-selling Drolo Cookies, their new Volo cookies are made with almonds, egg white, sugar, cocoa and vanilla. Crunchy, light, and gluten-free. Pairs well with milk and caffè lattes.

name: Good Honey Creamed Clover, 16oz
description:
The Ashusrt Family are 5th generation bee keepers, home harvesting honey in the USA since 1919.

Their Montana Creamed Clover honey is their raw and pure, using their unique creaming method. Good Honey’s creamed clover is whipped and chilled to perfection, creating a luxuriously smooth and spreadable texture. Crafted from only the finest clover blossoms, their creamed honey boasts a rich and delicate sweetness with a perfect velvety finish. It’s great for spreading over warm toast, stirring into tea, or enjoying by the spoonful!

name: Good Honey Montana Clover, 16oz
description:
The Ashusrt Family are 5th generation bee keepers, home harvesting honey in the USA since 1919.

Their Montana Clover Honey is the Olympic gold medal of honeys. When Montana Clover blooms in the summer months, Beekeepers and bees alike spend countless hours looking for this liquid gold. Although there are over 300 varieties of clover flowers, Montana Sweet Clover (Melilotus officinalis) is prized for its superior taste. They harvest it as a pure Montana clover, meaning it is not blended with other varieties, and is among some of the lightest colored honeys produced. Our favorite quality is its candied sweetness. If you’re looking for the most premium & tasty honey, look no further!

Delicate and sweet with clean floral notes. (A finishing honey)

name: Good Honey San Diego Citrus, 16oz
description:
The Ashusrt Family are 5th generation bee keepers, home harvesting honey in the USA since 1919.

San Diego Orange groves have a variety of Citrus fruits that come together to create the unique & signature taste of Southern California.

This delectable nectar leaves as quick as it comes, creating a small window to collect this prized honey. San Diego citrus is like sunshine in a jar, enjoy!

Juicy, jammy, bright and balanced

name: OroLiquido Marcona Almond Butter, 160g
tagline: fresh roasted marcona almonds & sea salt!
description: OroLiquido is a crunchy, creamy nut butter made with only two ingredients: Roasted Marcona almonds and sea salt. this "liquid gold" is delicious as an ice cream topping, on freshly baked bread with honey, or eaten by the spoonful!

name: Ayako Apricot Jam, 6oz
description:
In the summer of 2010, Ayako Gordon founded Ayako & Family Jams. Partnering with Japanese Organic farmer Katsumi Taki, they sought to bring the rarest of European and Asiatic plum varieties to the pantries of preserves lovers around the globe. 100% of the fruit for this artisan jam is grown on Taki's organic Japanese farm near Yakima.

This jam has a true apricot flavor balanced by notes of lemon zest and honeysuckle. Great on your morning toast with coffee, or fantastic with aged sheep's milk cheeses.

name: Ayako Damson Plum Jam, 6oz
description:
In the summer of 2010, Ayako Gordon founded Ayako & Family Jams. Partnering with Japanese Organic farmer Katsumi Taki, they sought to bring the rarest of European and Asiatic plum varieties to the pantries of preserves lovers around the globe. 100% of the fruit for this artisan jam is grown on Taki's organic Japanese farm near Yakima.

Damson Plum is a small, pear shaped heirloom fruit distinctive for its violet hues and punchy skins.

name: Ayako Greengage Plum Jam, 6oz
description:
In the summer of 2010, Ayako Gordon founded Ayako & Family Jams. Partnering with Japanese Organic farmer Katsumi Taki, they sought to bring the rarest of European and Asiatic plum varieties to the pantries of preserves lovers around the globe. 100% of the fruit for this artisan jam is grown on Taki's organic Japanese farm near Yakima.

Greengage Plums are a queen of plums, visually distinctive for their ethereal, ashy pink and chartreuse skins. Best known for their confectionary flavors, this jam provides intense, almost dried fruit concentration, think ripe apricot, with complex aromas of lemon verbena and orange blossom.

name: Ayako Italian Plum Jam, 6oz
description:
In the summer of 2010, Ayako Gordon founded Ayako & Family Jams. Partnering with Japanese Organic farmer Katsumi Taki, they sought to bring the rarest of European and Asiatic plum varieties to the pantries of preserves lovers around the globe. 100% of the fruit for this artisan jam is grown on Taki's organic Japanese farm near Yakima.

The Italian Plums are a ubiquitous variety here in the Pacific Northwest and known worldwide for its distinctive confectionary quality, both fresh and cooked. This European variety boasts a large oval sillhouette with dark violet skins and bright yellow flesh. When cooked, it offers the flavors of fresh mission fig with such a hint of honeysuckle on the finish.

name: Ayako Mirabelle Plum Jam, 6oz
description:
In the summer of 2010, Ayako Gordon founded Ayako & Family Jams. Partnering with Japanese Organic farmer Katsumi Taki, they sought to bring the rarest of European and Asiatic plum varieties to the pantries of preserves lovers around the globe. 100% of the fruit for this artisan jam is grown on Taki's organic Japanese farm near Yakima.

Mirabelle Plum is a European plum species known for its flecked golden skin in palm sized spheres. This jam offers intense, almost dried fruit concentration reminiscent of meyer lemon marmalade with honey.

name: La Trinquelinette Apricot Jam, 370g
description: This apricot jam is made in a small batches by a small family business in the village of Saint-Léger-Vauban in the Burgundy region. This area of France is known for its fertile soil and vineyards. All their jams are made with local fruit and brown unrefined sugar. Some of the jams are thicken with pectinei and some use rhubarb.Not too sweet, but sweet enough - perfect for your toasted baguette, French butter & coffee!

name: Pojer e Sandri Quince Syrup, 150g
description:
Pojer e Sandri Cold Pressed Quince Syrup is made from 100% cold concentrated quince juice, and nothing else.

Their estate’s orchard is located at 700 meters and is surrounded by forest, an ideal location for organically cultivating two varieties of quince, Ronda and Silver. Every fall, they cold press carefully selected fruit into juice. Using a unique vacuum processing, Pojer e Sandri are able to concentrate the quince juice to a thick, maple syrup consistency without adding any sugar. Thus, the intrinsic characteristics of the quince remain intact in the final product.

Pojer e Sandri has truly captured the essence of quince. Unlike most sugary syrups, this Quince Syrup bursts with a tannic tartness balanced by just enough natural sweetness. The quince fruit’s distinct aromas and notes of plum, molasses, and pine are concentrated. One spoonful packs a flavorful punch that evokes the mountainous region from which it originates.

name: Fabbri Amarena Cherries in Syrup, 120g
tagline: The Classic Amarena Cherry in Syrup!
description: The Fabbri Company of Bologna has been making uniquely delicious cherries in amarena syrup for over a century. Only the best wild cherries are carefully selected and candied in amarena syrup according to Gennaro Fabbri's original recipe, created in 1905. Eat them straight out of the crock, add them to cobblers and cakes, or top a perfect bowl of vanilla ice cream.

name: Bees Knees Meyer Lemon Honey, 10oz
description: Made by Bushwick Kitchens in Brooklyn, USA. Combining sweet honey from the Hudson Valley with a bright squeeze of citrus, Bees Knees Meyer Lemon Honey is great on anything from a fresh baked scone to a bowl of berries to a plate of fried chicken.

name: Bees Knees Salted Honey, 10oz
description: Made by Bushwick Kitchens in Brooklyn, USA. Fragrant wildflower honey from the Hudson Valley is infused with sea salt, creating a honey with the perfect balance of sweet and salty. It is great on anything from soft goat cheese to a piece of freshly buttered toast to a scoop of warm fruit cobbler.

name: Bees Knees Spicy Honey, 10oz
description: Made by Bushwick Kitchens in Brooklyn, USA. This wildflower honey from the Hudson Valley is infused with a custom spicy mix of chile peppers, delivering the perfect balance of sweet heat. It is great on anything from a warm buttered biscuit to a cold bowl of ice cream, to the perfect vinaigrette.

name: Girl Meets Dirt Ginny Jam, 7.75oz
description:
In an orchard by the sea (Warm Valley Orchard) lies a grove of old Italian Plum trees, harvested by long time islanders Bob & Maria Nutt. These beautiful plums have been crated off to Seattle the past few years to be soaked with botanicals in gin by Copperworks Distilling for their lauded & award winning Plum Gin (side note, Bob is brothers with Copperworks Founder Micah and Audra bought her first Shiro Plums aside from the farmette tree, from the Nutt family).

A few years back we fielded a call from Copperworks- basically- hey- we’ve got these boozy plums we normally compost but maybe you want them? HECK YA we do.

So in true full circle fashion we picked up a truckload of buckets of the inaugural 2021 season island Italian plums that had spent most of 2022 on the lash in a gin bath and brought them back home. We rolled up our sleeves and hand pitted each and every one of them, added some sugar and a squeeze of lemon to the party and have an exquisite new limited edition preserve!

name: Girl Meets Dirt Hot Damn Pepper Jam Spoon Preserves, 7.75oz
description:
The Girl Meets Dirt crew is really into fruit, but their farmers grow great vegetables too! Time to fire up the peppers. The result is a not so usual pepper jelly. They gave it the old GMD spin and maxxed out the spiciness but added lots of local fruit and a bit of punchy organic vinegar (made from WA apples) for balance. The quince and apple add body to the set allowing GMD to stay committed to their ‘no pectin’ policy. It’s legit hot (yes!). It’s legit amazing. And it’s all natural.

This is one of those jars you need in your refrigerator to spice up lackluster meals (visualize dipping coconut shrimp or topping grilled salmon) and serve as an instant cheese pairing by slathering on cream cheese and crackers at a moment’s notice. They're a game-changer for any charcuterie board or cheeseboard!

name: Girl Meets Dirt Orcas Pear, 7.75oz
description: At the height of ripeness Girl Meets Dirt picks Orcas Island pears and cooks them into a rosy preserve, with notes of ginger from their fresh kitchen garden grown bay leaves. Highly versatile, this preserve is a gorgeous topping to pannacotta and cheesecake.

name: Girl Meets Dirt Pear Balsamic. 7.75oz
description: This jam is always a star on a cheeseboard or grazing board with taleggio, asiago and blues. Truly an all-purpose condiment – try it over ice cream. Or play around – add a few glugs of balsamic to a teaspoonful, extra virgin olive oil, salt, and minced shallots and puree it together for a quick, rich vinaigrette for a salad (topped with blue cheese, fresh pear slices, and crispy shallots). Spoon it over a wedge of Rogue River Blue with wafer thin crackers or fresh pear slices for an intensely satisfying cheese pairing.

name: Girl Meets Dirt Rhuberry Preserves, 220g
description:
The Girl Meets Dirt crew is really into fruit, but their farmers grow great vegetables too! Time to fire up the peppers. The result is a not so usual pepper jelly. They gave it the old GMD spin and maxxed out the spiciness but added lots of local fruit and a bit of punchy organic vinegar (made from WA apples) for balance. The quince and apple add body to the set allowing GMD to stay committed to their ‘no pectin’ policy. It’s legit hot (yes!). It’s legit amazing. And it’s all natural.

This bright ruby small batch Reserve folds grassy red rhubarb from Ralph's Greenhouse in the Skagit Valley and from JBS Farm in Crow Valley on Orcas (where John and Susan Fleischer tend crowns that have been in the ground for fifty years) with tart, plump Northwest raspberries — classically preserved in just six copper pots, the way they always have.

name: Tree Knees Cinnamon Maple Syrup, 13.5oz
description: Rich maple syrup from the Catskill Mountains is infused with cassia cinnamon from Indonesia, creating the ultimate tag team of flavors. Trees Knees Cinnamon Maple is great in iced coffee, drizzled over baked fruit, or poured over hot waffles.

name: Villa Jerada Buckwheat Honey, 16oz
description:
Yakima Valley buckwheat honey showcasing the bounty and diversity of plants and source of pollen for the bees. Often compared to the (overhyped) Manuka honey, many clinical studies have shown that buckwheat honey is as healthy and nutritious.

Villa Jerada buckwheat honey is unfiltered, raw, full of complex flavors such as molasses and caramel. It pairs well with raw milk cheeses, fruits, teas and in a simple baguette slice with olive oil and a generous drizzle on top.

name: Runamok Bourbon Barrel-Aged Pure Maple Syrup, 12.7 oz
description: Founded in 2009 by husband-and-wife team Eric and Laura Sorkin, Runamok combines high quality ingredients, innovative flavors, and eye-catching packaging to create excellent maple syrups. This syrup is aged in recently-emptied bourbon barrels, allowing the essence of bourbon to shine through.

name: Runamok Sugar Maker's Cut Pure Maple Syrup, 12.7 oz
tagline: The Season's Best Pure Maple Syrup!
description: Founded in 2009 by husband-and-wife team Eric and Laura Sorkin, Runamok combines high quality ingredients and innovative flavors to create excellent maple syrups. This Grade A Vermont maple syrup is a beautiful amber hue, with a rich flavor to complement any pancake breakfast.

name: Runamok Whiskey Barrel Aged Pure Maple Syrup, 12.7 oz
description: Founded in 2009 by husband-and-wife team Eric and Laura Sorkin, Runamok combines high quality ingredients, innovative flavors, and eye-catching packaging to create excellent maple syrups. This syrup is aged in recently-emptied whiskey barrels, allowing the essence of whiskey to shine through.

name: Casina Rossa Saffron & Acacia Honey, 140g
description: Casina Rossa is a brand of artisan food products from the Abruzzo region of Italy created by Nicola and Paola DeLaurentiis. Their Saffron & Acacia Honey is complements aged cheeses, ice cream, or even roasted chicken or scallops.

name: Faugier Creme de Marrons, 17oz
tagline: Classic sweet chestnut cream
description: Clement Faugier created the recipe for his famous chestnut spread in 1885. Not 1985, 1885. It has stood the test of time and is still perfect to spread on your morning toast, a fresh baguette or crepes. It's sweet & creamy with a hint of vanilla - making it a staple in French cooking & baking.

name: Inna Jam Meyer Lemon
description: Inna Jam, located in the Bay Area, sources all its organic produce from within 150 miles of their Emeryville kitchen. Their single-varietal jams rely on the best possible fruit and are intended to showcase the natural subtleties and bright flavors of the fruit. There is no mixing of fruit or added flavorings. Each jar is a time capsule of single-sourced fruit. Their Meyer Lemon has the floral, lemony bite of Meyer lemons, the bitter tinge distinctive of citrus marmalades, and the sweet-but-not-too-sweet balance typical of Inna jams.

name: Inna Jam Plenty Spicy Jalapeno Jam, 10oz
description: Pronounced like "I'm in a jam" - inn-ah. No matter how you say it, Inna's makes amazing seasonal jams from fresh, organic, seasonal fruit sourced from within 150 miles of their Emeryville, CA kitchen. The Spicy Jalapeño, Inna's signature jam, has more kick than other pepper jellies because they use the entire pepper, seeds and all! This results in a spicy-sweet and completely addictive jam with distinct jalapeño flavors. Go old school with your favorite cracker, cream cheese, smoked salmon & Inna's Spicy Jalapeno!

name: Marchesi di San Giulano Mandarin Orange Marmalade, 460g
description: The San Giuliano estate is in the foothills of Mount Etna and boasts some of the most fertile soil in Sicily. Some of the finest citrus fruits in Italy grow there. All their jam production is done on the San Giuliano estate by hand in small batches with simple, family recipes. Freshly picked organic fruit is hand-sliced and cooked down slowly with only cane sugar. They never use thickeners or preservatives. Their Sicilian Mandarin Marmalade gets its burnt orange color from the sweet, juicy mandarins that hang ripe from the trees like ornaments in late December, leading some to call it the Christmas Orange. The marmalade is sweet and fragrant with enough acidity to give it complexity. Fabulous on crusty toast with butter, but also a sophisticated addition to almost any dessert.

name: Marchesi di San Giuliano Clementine Orange Marmalade, 460g
description: The San Giuliano estate is in the foothills of Mount Etna and boasts some of the most fertile soil in Sicily. Some of the finest citrus fruits in Italy grow there. All their jam production is done on the San Giuliano estate by hand in small batches with simple, family recipes. Freshly picked organic fruit is hand-sliced and cooked down slowly with only cane sugar. They never use thickeners or preservatives. Their Sicilian Clementine Marmalade is made with a juicy varietal of mandarin. The high proportion of fruit picked at peak ripeness and prepared simply with natural ingredients give this jam an incomparable flavor. Great on toast and pairs well with cheeses such as ricotta.

name: Marchesi di San Giuliano Lemon Marmalade, 460g
description: The San Giuliano estate is in the foothills of Mount Etna and boasts some of the most fertile soil in Sicily. Some of the finest citrus fruits in Italy grow there. All their jam production is done on the San Giuliano estate by hand in small batches with simple, family recipes. Freshly picked organic fruit is hand-sliced and cooked down slowly with only cane sugar. They never use thickeners or preservatives. Bright and tangy, with the sweet bitterness of caramelized fruit, their Sicilian Lemon Marmalade bursts with the flavor of Sicily’s treasured lemons. Great on toast and croissants, but also makes a lovely filling for tarts.

name: Marchesi di San Giuliano Red Grapefruit Marmalade, 460g
description: The San Giuliano estate is in the foothills of Mount Etna and boasts some of the most fertile soil in Sicily. Some of the finest citrus fruits in Italy grow there. All their jam production is done on the San Giuliano estate by hand in small batches with simple, family recipes. Freshly picked organic fruit is hand-sliced and cooked down slowly with only cane sugar. They never use thickeners or preservatives. Their Sicilian Red Grapefruit Marmalade is sweet and tangy with a clean, bright flavor. Tender slices of aromatic grapefruit add to the texture and give the marmalade a pleasant bitterness. Excellent on toast with creamy butter, as a topping for ice cream, or swirled into yogurt.

name: Marchesi di San Giuliano Sicilian Bitter Orange Marmalade, 460g
description: The San Giuliano estate is in the foothills of Mount Etna and boasts some of the most fertile soil in Sicily. Some of the finest citrus fruits in Italy grow there. All their jam production is done on the San Giuliano estate by hand in small batches with simple, family recipes. Freshly picked organic fruit is hand-sliced and cooked down slowly with only cane sugar. They never use thickeners or preservatives. Their Sicilian Bitter Orange Marmalade is made with the Arancia Rossa di Sicilia, the blood orange of Sicily. Its bright crimson flesh is both tart and sweet. Excellent on bread or with baked brie.

name: Marchesi di San Giuliano Sicilian Orange Marmalade, 460g
description: The San Giuliano estate is in the foothills of Mount Etna and boasts some of the most fertile soil in Sicily. Some of the finest citrus fruits in Italy grow there. All their jam production is done on the San Giuliano estate by hand in small batches with simple, family recipes. Freshly picked organic fruit is hand-sliced and cooked down slowly with only cane sugar. They never use thickeners or preservatives. Their Sicilian Orange Marmalade is made with Arancia Rossa di Sicilia, the blood orange of Sicily. Its bright crimson flesh is both tart and fruity. The marmalade has a well-crafted balance of fragrant citrus and gentle sweetness. Lovely on a slice of toasted, crusty bread or dollop a spoonful on vanilla ice cream.

name: Mike's Hot Honey, 12oz
description: Michael Kurtz, inspired by the chili infused honey he discovered while living in Brazil, set out to make his own version upon his return to the US. He ended up creating the perfect accompaniment for his favorite food - pizza. After an apprenticeship at one of New York's hottest pizzarias and doing a lot of experimenting, Mike's Hot Honey was ready for the public. At first, it was just for restaurant use. It didn't take long for customers to start requesting to-go orders of the honey, and he discovered there might actully be a larger market for his honey. This is truly an incredibly versatile condiment - try on pizza, chicken, ribs, biscuits, fruits, cheese, even in cocktails.

name: Ritrovo Selections Organic Rosemary Honey, 8.8oz
description: Ritrovo Selections is a premium importer of foods that represent Italy’s traditions and quality. Ritrovo means to rediscover in Italian. Over the last 20 years, the Seattle-based company has vastly expanded its line of products and won numerous international awards for quality. Their Organic Rosemary Honey is made in Southern Italy by beekeeper Fabio Lacovanelli who reserves his harvest exclusively for Ritrovo. The bees forage on organic rosemary blossoms, which gives the pale amber honey a piney aroma and full-bodied sweetness. Toast is an obvious choice and always excellent but consider adding some to cheese plates. Just a little honey complements the salty nature of cheese. You can drizzle it over a wedge or put it in a ramekin and let your guests spoon it out on their own. Especially good with goat cheese, brie, aged pecorino and camembert.

name: Ritrovo Selections Sicilian Pistachio Cream, 8oz
description: Ritrovo Selections is a premium importer of foods that represent Italy’s traditions and quality. Ritrovo means to rediscover in Italian. Over the last 20 years, the Seattle-based company has vastly expanded its line of products and won numerous international awards for quality. Their Pistachio Cream is obsession worthy. It’s made with just two ingredients: cane sugar and organic Sicilian pistachios from the foothills of Mount Etna, where the best pistachios in the world are grown. This pure, sweet spread is used in Italy for pastries, cake fillings, and gelati. But you’ll probably find yourself spreading it on toast or just eating it straight from the jar.

name: Apicoltura Dr. Pescia Chestnut Honey, 250g
description: Paolo Pescia, a passionate second-generation honey maker, practices “nomadic” beekeeping. He transports his beehives to seasonally flowering zones and protected national parks located in the Tuscan coastal hills, producing monofloral honeys of stunning flavor. All production is done by hand, including the scraping of honey from the combs. All of Pescia's honeys are raw, unpasteurized, unfiltered, and contain no artificial colors or sweeteners. This bronze-colored honey comes from a chestnut forest near Pescia's farm in the Tuscan hills. With an intense molasses-like bouquet and flavor, it is ideal as a condiment for both aged cheeses and fresh ricotta. It is also great with roasted squash and meats.

name: Ayako Suyematsu Raspberry Jam, 6oz
description: In the summer of 2010, Ayako Gordon founded Ayako & Family Jams. Partnering with Japanese Organic farmer Katsumi Taki, they sought to bring the rarest of European and Asiatic plum varieties to the pantries of preserves lovers around the globe. 100% of the fruit for this artisan jam is grown on Taki's organic Japanese farm near Yakima. This jam is a limited edition flavor, produced with Raspberries grown and harvested at Suyematsu Organic Farm on Bainbridge Island, WA in honor of Japanese Farmer Akio Suyematsu.

name: Casa Forcella Crab Apple Mostarda, 5oz
description: Mostarda is a classic Italian condiment that combines the sweet-tart notes of candied fruit with the spiciness of mustard. This apple mostarda is a perfect complement to pecorinos such as Pecorino Toscano or Piccolo Canestrato, and adds an adventurous zing to any charcuterie board. Casa Forcello founder Paola Calciolari utilizes locally-sourced fruit and her grandmother’s traditional recipes to create a truly exceptional mostarda.

name: Casa Forcella Pear Mostarda, 5oz
description: Mostarda is a classic Italian condiment that combines the sweet-tart notes of candied fruit with the spiciness of mustard. Casa Forcello founder Paola Calciolari utilizes locally-sourced fruit and her grandmother’s traditional recipes to create a truly exceptional mostarda.

name: Casa Forcella Plum Mostarda, 5oz
description: Mostarda is a classic Italian condiment that combines the sweet-tart notes of candied fruit with the spiciness of mustard. Casa Forcello founder Paola Calciolari utilizes locally-sourced fruit and her grandmother’s traditional recipes to create a truly exceptional mostarda.

name: Chateau Miraval Lavendar Honey, 500g
description: Château Miraval Lavender Honey is a rare, limited-edition, raw honey produced directly on the Provence property, often harvested in the summer or fall by resident beekeeper Noel Patterson. It is known for its delicate floral taste and creamy texture, reflecting the aromatic lavender fields surrounding the estate.

name: Dalmatia Fig & Orange Spread, 240g
description: Dalmatia combines the sweetness of Croatian figs with the zesty pop of coastal oranges. Made with care using hand-selected fruits, this is the perfect accompaniment to your charcuterie or cheese board. It pairs nicely with blue cheeses such as Bleu des Basque or Mitibleu, bloomy rind cheeses such as Brie du Pommier or Fromage de Meaux, or with fresh ricotta and walnuts over toasted bread. It’s not limited to cheese, however. It’s the perfect complement to your morning coffee when spread liberally on toast with butter.

name: Dalmatia Fig Spread, 240g
description: As good on toast as it is with aged sheep's milk cheese, this spread is made with figs from the Croatian coast. After we tried it for the first time, we knew it had to be on our shelves. This spread pairs well with almost any cheese - from rich and creamy to dry and sharp. Love figs, but not with cheese? No problem. Spread liberally on toast with butter and enjoy with your morning coffee!

name: Dalmatia Sour Cherry Spread, 240g
description: Dalmatia uses perfectly-ripened Croatian sour cherries to make this delightful spread. A popular charcuterie board recommendation from our deli staff, this spread pairs especially well with tangy goat cheeses such as Florette, Humboldt Fog, or Bocconcino di Langa. It also makes an excellent filling for chocolate cake or cookies!

name: Girl Meets Dirt Bluebarb Preserves, 220g
description:
The Girl Meets Dirt crew is really into fruit, but their farmers grow great vegetables too! Time to fire up the peppers. The result is a not so usual pepper jelly. They gave it the old GMD spin and maxxed out the spiciness but added lots of local fruit and a bit of punchy organic vinegar (made from WA apples) for balance. The quince and apple add body to the set allowing GMD to stay committed to their ‘no pectin’ policy. It’s legit hot (yes!). It’s legit amazing. And it’s all natural.

In their Bluebarb Preserve, rhubarb, the harbinger of their season, with Cascadia blueberries and their classic French-inspired flair. This one is the PNW at her best.

name: Hotaru Matcha Milk Jam, 250g
description: Milk jam, a popular treat in Japan, is in the same family as long-simmered reductions of milk and sugar like dulce de leche, though without the caramelization. Creamy and thick enough to spread, this artisanal milk jam is slow-cooked with matcha green tea powder. The vibrant green jam has an earthy nuttiness, just a touch of caramelly-bitterness, and a pleasant modest sweetness. Excellent on brioche toast, drizzled over desserts, or served with sharp, aged cheeses.

name: Luxardo Maraschino Cherries, 400g
description: These cherries are the real deal. Produced the same way since 1905, they have no thickening agents or preservatives. Deep burgundy red in color, small, sweet and sour, they are a far cry from the electric red, processed maraschinos you found in your Shirley Temple as a kid. Without these cherries, no Manhattan is complete. Although ideal for cocktails, they are equally delicious right out of the jar, or spooned over ice cream and desserts.

name: Momofuku Chili Crunch Hot Honey, 220g
description:
Momofuku Chili Crunch Hot Honey is the sweet side of spicy. They combined their cult-favorite spicy-crunchy chili oil with premium wildflower honey to create the ultimate union of heat and sweet.

Developed by David Chang and the Momofuku Goods team, Chili Crunch Hot Honey is packed with the same chef-approved ingredients they use in their restaurants.

name: Ronnie's Blackstraw Jam, 240g
tagline: Washington Blackberries, Strawberries & Currants
description:
BlackStraw Jam™ is a low sugar jam made of Washington Blackberries, Marionberries, Strawberries & Black Currants!

Still sweet, but with 33% less sugar than most jams, this is a delight on toast, muffins, pancakes and more...

Imagine a summer morning in the misty valleys of Washington State. The air is crisp, and the berries are ripe, their colors so vivid they could stop a painter mid-stroke. This is no ordinary jam. It’s an ode to nature’s wild elegance—a perfect storm of blackberry bramble, the deep, wine-dark allure of marionberries, the sun-kissed brightness of strawberries, and the brooding richness of black currants.

name: The French Beekeeper Wild Alfalfa Honey, 3oz
description: This is a raw wild flower honey produced in King County, Washington, by The French Beekeeper. It is a light hue, colored pale gold with a clean and uniform texture. The taste recalls fresh cut grass and hay. Plant notes are present but delicate, evoking freshly worked farmland rather than flowers.

name: Toschi Amarena Cherries
description: These iconic cherries need no introduction, but we’ll give them one anyway! Each elegantly designed jar is filled with carefully selected black sour cherries, suspended in a sweet syrup. If you’re garnishing something sweet, making a cake, or serving ice cream sundaes, these cherries are a must-have. Even the syrup is worth keeping once the fruit is gone – use it to flavor sodas, milkshakes, or popsicles.

name: Yakami Orchards Passion Fruit Marmalade, 290g
description: Made with traditional South Korean techniques using passion fruit, honey, and sugar. Elevate your cheese plate, excite your English muffin, or entice your senses in hot tea. Try it now and experience a burst of deliciousness.

name: Zab's Hot Honey, 12oz
description:
A sweet, slow burning drizzle for your cheese boards, marinades, pizza, and anything in between.

A new (but old) ingredient you most likely didn’t know you were missing. A rare and mysterious pepper from st. Augustine, Florida. Known for its signature “slow burn” and naturally sweet heat, it provides a subtle blend of fruity, tangy flavor with a gradual, tingly and lingering heat.

Despite mysterious origins, it has been a culinary staple and centerpiece of old Florida cuisine for 200+ years. We suspect the datil originated in the caribbean, and was brought to Florida in the late 1700’s/early 1800’s, where it became a local treasure, and evolved over time into the unique pepper it is today. Our datil peppers are grown with care on a small (but growing) farm just outside St. Augustine.

name: Emile Vergeois Lemonade, 8.5oz
description: Emile Vergeois has been a beacon of quality and tradition in the fruit juice industry since 1993. Situated in the lush countryside near Lyon, France, this family-operated workshop specializes in producing exquisite fruit juices and nectars that celebrate the richness of French terroir and the essence of artisanal craftsmanship.

name: Pathfinder Hemp & Root Limited Edition, 700ml
description: The Pathfinder is fermented from hemp and carefully refined by copper pot distillation. It is then blended with an alchemy of wormwood, angelic root, ginger, sage, juniper, saffron, orange peel, wild-crafted Douglas-fir and natural terpenes to yield this revolutionary spirit of both complexity and character. The Pathfinder tastes like an amaro, that fine class of European liquors known for bittersweet flavors rounded out by citrus and spice, and can be used as a flavorful substitute for amaro, whiskey, or vermouth. This miraculous elixir, like the hemp plant itself, has no pyschoactive effects, yet contains enough vitamin E, antioxidants, and other nutrients, to go favorably hand-in-hand with a balanced diet. And since there's no alcohol in The Pathfinder, it won't give you a hangover, either!

name: Roots Divino Bianco N/A Vermouth
tagline: N/A Vermouth - just add tonic!
description: Roots Divino are non-alcoholic aperitifs based on wine (di vino). The halo shape on the label symbolizes the divine effect of enjoying a drinking occasion without the alcohol. They're Bianco uses rosemary, thyme & wormwood, making it perfect to enjoy over ice with a lemon slice & tonic for a refreshing non-alcoholic spritz!

name: Roots Divino Rosso N/A Vermouth
tagline: N/A Vermouth - just add tonic!
description: Roots Divino are non-alcoholic aperitifs based on wine (di vino). The halo shape on the label symbolizes the divine effect of enjoying a drinking occasion without the alcohol. They're Rosso uses bitter orange, gentian & wormwood, making it perfect to enjoy over ice with tonic & slice of orange for a nice non-alcoholic spritz!

name: St. Agrestis Amaro Falso, 2x200ml
tagline: The Amaro for when you're not Amaro-ing!
description: Made by hand at their distillery in Brooklyn, NY using old world methods, St. Agrestis aims to create naturally colored, perfectly balanced and incredibly flavorful spirits while reinventing the way you drink some of the world’s most iconic spirits and cocktails. Created as the non-alcoholic counterpart to the beloved St. Agrestis Amaro, Amaro Falso is made using the same combination of all-natural citrus, botanical, and herbal ingredients found in their spiritous version, sans alcohol. Ready-to-drink and individually portioned, Amaro Falso is similar to an Amaro Highball, driven by nuanced notes of herbal spice, mint and bitter complexity from gentian root. The result is a refreshing beverage that makes it an ideal cocktail that fans of Italian aperitivi and digestivi expect. Lastly, carbonation and nitrogen have been added to help mimic the bite and mouth feel that alcohol typically provides. Enjoy chilled straight from the bottle or over ice with an orange twist.

name: St. Agrestis Mezcal Negroni, 2x200ml
tagline: The Negroni for when you're not Negroni-ing!
description: Made by hand at their distillery in Brooklyn, NY using old world methods, St. Agrestis aims to create naturally colored, perfectly balanced and incredibly flavorful spirits while reinventing the way you drink some of the world’s most iconic spirits and cocktails. Made with many of the same botanicals found in their beloved favorite, Phony Mezcal Negroni emphasizes mezcal qualities by offering nuanced notes of smoke, vegetal complexity and earthiness to compliment its bitter foundation. Gentle carbonation is added to help mimic the bite and mouth feel that alcohol typically provides. Enjoy chilled straight from the bottle or over ice with an orange twist.

name: St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, 2x200ml
tagline: The Negroni for when you're not Negroni-ing!
description: Made by hand at their distillery in Brooklyn, NY using old world methods, St. Agrestis aims to create naturally colored, perfectly balanced and incredibly flavorful spirits while reinventing the way you drink some of the world’s most iconic spirits and cocktails. This is your non-alcoholic classic Negroni. It has nuanced juniper, citrus, and floral notes and drinks with the same bitterness drinkers of the classic cocktail expect, sans alcohol. They've also added carbonation to help mimic the bite that alcohol typically provides. Enjoy chilled straight from the bottle or over ice with an orange twist. Or for a bubbly, low ABV option, top with Prosecco for a Negroni Sbagliato.

name: San Pellegrino Sanbitter, 10pc - 100ml
description: This famous Italian soda has a flavor similar to Campari, without the alcohol. Lightly sweetened and carbonated, it is great to pour over ice, garnish with a twist of lemon, or use as a mixer with bourbon or gin. When finished, don't throw the bottle away - they make great bud vases!

name: Crodino 6pk
tagline: N/A Classic Italian Aperitvo!
description: An Italian classic since 1965! The perfect N/A apertivo to enjoy when the sun is setting, you have a few cheeses & small bites and you want to quite literally, chill. To enjoy the intense citrus/fruity notes and the pleasant bitter finish, serve Crodino in a wine glass with a generous helping of ice. Garnish with a slice of orange and you're set!

name: Lurisia Chinotto, 4pk
description: The unique aroma of our Chinotto comes from the west side of the Liguria Riviera where, since 1500, Chinotto trees have grown. There is now a Slow Food Presidium to protect the precious citrus fruits that give this drink it's characteristic amber color and scent of citrus & spices. Not too sweet, it is perfect enjoyed right from the bottle or as a mixer when you want some extra punch!

name: Casamara Club Alta, 4pk
tagline: N/A soda reminiscent of classic Italian aperitivos!
description: The 2 founders at Casamara Club think it should be easier for you (and your guests) to enjoy a really good drink without the alcohol. Accordingly, all their recipes are minimally processed with carefully sourced ingredients. The result is a lineup of delicious & refreshing drinks that are far less sweet than others on the market. Perfect for drinking all day! Alta is an Italian style botanical soda with classic aperitivo aromatics and an extra dry finish. It has a pleasant pink citrus bite, and warm, fruity spice notes, reminiscent of a Negroni.

name: Casamara Club Como, 4pk
tagline: N/A soda reminiscent of alpine aperitivos!
description: The 2 founders at Casamara Club think it should be easier for you (and your guests) to enjoy a really good drink without the alcohol. Perfect for drinking all day! Como is an Alpine style botanical soda with mountain amaro aromatics and an extra dry finish. It has citrus and breezy wildflower notes, reminiscent of Alpine amaro.

name: Casamara Club Onda, 4pk
tagline: N/A soda reminiscent of Sicilian aperitivos!
description: The 2 founders at Casamara Club think it should be easier for you (and your guests) to enjoy a really good drink without the alcohol. It has notes of coastal citrus and leafy green sage notes reminiscent of Sicilian amaro.

name: Casamara Club Super Clasico N/A Apertivo
tagline: N/A soda reminiscent of sitting in a Milan cafe at 6pm!
description: Super Clasico is a bittersweet, sunset-hued aperitivo built like a proper libation with full cocktail-strength. Each botanical is extracted separately before blending. Italian chinotto, a bitter citrus grown along the Calabrian coast, opens bright and sharp alongside juniper. Orris root harvested from the roots of the iris flower provides a grounding, earthy bass note. Tart red currant lends acidity, not sweetness. Kola nut and allspice develop tannin structure. Bourbon-grade Madagascar vanilla rounds the finish. It tastes like sitting at a Milan cafe at 6pm as the city shifts gears!

name: Jack Rudy Cocktail Co. Extra Bitter Tonic, 8oz
description: The Jack Rudy Cocktail Company is a family-run company based in Charleston, S.C., and Lexington, KY. They take long-forgotten staples of the American bar and reinvent them so we can enjoy cocktails from the golden age, as our grandparents might have. The small company got a huge boost when the New York Times, Wall Street Journal, GQ, and others praised their debut product Small Batch Tonic. They’ve since added many great products. Their Extra Bitter Tonic has an added bitterness for those that like a fuller, drier gin and tonic. It pairs nicely with a classic, juniper-forward gin

name: Scrappy's Aromatic Bitters, 5oz
description:
Seattle bartender Miles Thomas founded Scrappy’s Bitters in his search for better bitters for the best bartenders. After years of experiments, Scrappy’s officially launched in 2008, and a small, but dedicated team has been making handcrafted bitters in Seattle, WA ever since.

Scrappy’s answer to the classic aromatic bitters. These bitters were created to be used in classic cocktail recipes. They add balance and a bit of spice to your favorite spirits.

Despite not having any actual "black lemon" in this bitters, the bright and fresh lemon flavor has rich floral notes and deep earthy spices that are reminiscent of the "black lemon," hence the name.

description: Fee Brothers started in Rochester, New York in 1864. Now in their fourth generation, they are still making quality bitters, brines and cocktail mixes. name: Fee Brothers Orange Bitters, 4oz
description: Fee Brothers started in Rochester, New York in 1864. Now in their fourth generation, they are still making quality bitters, brines and cocktail mixes. name: Fee Brothers Rhubarb Bitters, 4oz
description: Fee Brothers started in Rochester, New York in 1864. Now in their fourth generation, they are still making quality bitters, brines and cocktail mixes. Fee Bros, using flavors available in 1800's America, developed their Rhubarb Bitters for a historical taste.

name: Fee Brothers West Indian Orange Bitters, 4oz
description: Fee Brothers started in Rochester, New York in 1864. Now in their fourth generation, they are still making quality bitters, brines and cocktail mixes . No self respecting home mixologist can build a bar without orange bitters. Fee Brothers West Indian Orange is a great place to start. Made from the skins of oranges grown in the West Indies, it pairs perfectly with whiskey and rum drinks. After you have added a dash to your next Martini, you may never drink one without these orange bitters again.

name: Fee Brothers Whiskey Barrel Bitters, 4oz
description: Fee Brothers started in Rochester, New York in 1864. Now in their fourth generation, they are still making quality bitters, brines and cocktail mixes . This limited production bitter is truly unique. Fee Brothers takes their aromatic bitters and slowly matures them in freshly emptied whiskey barrels from Tennessee's best whisky producers. Perfect for a Manhattan or Old-Fashioned, they can also be substituted for Angostura bitters.

name: Peychaud's Bitters, 5oz
tagline: Bartender...one Sazerac, please...
description: Antoine Peychaud moved to New Orleans in 1793. An apothecary, Peychaud brought with him a recipe for something special that could cure any ailment - bitters. Aside from bitters' healing properties, Peychaud also discovered it tasted really good when he mixed it with brandy. You could try and make a Sazerac without Peychauds Bitters, but you would have to call it something else. Don't limit yourself, though - feel free to try it in a Manhattan, Old Fashioned or Whiskey Sour.

name: Bittermilk Tom Collins with Elderflower & Hops, 502ml
description: Husband and wife team, Joe and MariElena Raya, founded Bittermilk after years in the restaurant and bar industry to simplify making craft cocktails at home.
