Careful and lengthy aging in cherry, chestnut, acacia, oak and juniper barrels imparts a rich, balanced blend of sweet & sour. Perfect for salad dressing & marinades.

name: Fini Balsamic Vinegar, 250ml
description: Fini Balsamic of Modena has been on our shelves for a long time, and for good reason. If quality is on the X axis and cost is on the Y axis, this vinegar scores in the upper right corner. Great for salad dressing, marinades & even drizzling on aged cheeses & fresh berries - all without seeing the dollars pouring out of the spout with the vinegar!

name: Ciacco Barolo Wine Vinegar, 250ml
description: From the heart of Piemonte terroir comes this rich, ruby-colored red wine vinegar that is produced in Modena by an Acetaia that specializes in monovarietal vinegars, voted #1 monovarietal vinegar in Italy by Gambero Rosso and made from 100% DOCG Barolo Nebbiolo grapes. This exceptional wine vinegar is a perfect condiment for salads, meat dishes, polenta, and braised meats. Savory and smooth, it will become a go-to item in your kitchen.

name: Prelibato White Balsamic Vinegar, 200ml
description: For its Prelibato, (white balsamic condiment), Acetaia Malpighi uses the best part of the grape - the “Trebbiano Modenese." These grapes are crushed softly and slowly, resulting in a juice that is transparent. The juice is then filtered and placed in a centrifuge to make it dense without being cooked. Lastly, it is aged in ash wood for up to 5 years to obtain its delicate aroma and retain its clear color. What does this mean to you? It means that your get to enjoy an amazing, transparent balsamic vinegar on your pork, salads, fresh mozzarella, cured meats and fresh berries.

name: Ritrovo Selections Apricot Balsamic Vinegar, 200ml
description: This Apricot Balsamic is made from ripe apricots, and organic grape must, resulting in a balanced vinegar with an intense apricot flavor and notes of almond, lemon peel, and orange blossom that is reminiscent of Italian summers. The bright acidity complements its rich flavor and subtle sweetness creating a versatile product that has varied culinary applications. This vinegar makes an excellent glaze for poultry, especially chicken, Cornish game hen and squab, as well as pork or veal. Its brightness also lends itself well to traditional salad dressings, grilled fruit, and cream-based desserts, such as semifreddo, panna cotta and zabaione.

name: Ritrovo Selections Blood Orange Balsamic Vinegar, 200ml
description:
Ritrovo Selections is a premium importer of foods that represent Italy’s traditions and quality. Ritrovo means to rediscover in Italian. Over the last 20 years, the Seattle-based company has vastly expanded its line of products and won numerous international awards for quality.

Enjoy the bold flavor of Sicily’s famous ‘Tarocco’ winter blood oranges year-round. Crafted by vinegar master Nicolo Verrini, this white balsamic blends real Sicilian blood orange juice with white grape must for a bright, balanced taste. Perfect on salads, duck confit, roasted squash, or to deglaze meat dishes.

name: Ritrovo Selections Mediterranean Herb Balsamic, 200ml
description:
Ritrovo Selections is a premium importer of foods that represent Italy’s traditions and quality. Ritrovo means to rediscover in Italian. Over the last 20 years, the Seattle-based company has vastly expanded its line of products and won numerous international awards for quality.

With a brilliant green color and aromatic flavors of Italian basil and fresh rosemary combined with sweet white grape, this balsamic vinegar is a perfectly balanced condiment for salads, ceviches, pickling, and even mixology.

name: Ritrovo Selections Organic Apple Balsamic Vinegar, 200ml
description: Ritrovo Selections is a premium importer of foods that represent Italy’s traditions and quality. Ritrovo means to rediscover in Italian. Over the last 20 years, the Seattle-based company has vastly expanded its line of products and won numerous international awards for quality. Their Organic Apple Balsamic Vinegar is made from tart, organic Trentino apples and organic Modena grape must. The agrodolce (agro=sour; dolce=sweet) vinegar has good balance and a rich flavor. It blends beautifully with fruity olive oils from Southern Italy.

name: Ritrovo Selections Organic Citrus Balsamic Vinegar, 200ml
description: Ritrovo Selections is a premium importer of foods that represent Italy’s traditions and quality. Ritrovo means to rediscover in Italian. Over the last 20 years, the Seattle-based company has vastly expanded its line of products and won numerous international awards for quality. Their Organic Citrus Balsamic Vinegar is a lively balsamic vinegar inspired by foods of the Amalfi Coast. It’s made with lemon juice, Trebbiano grape must and wine vinegar. Excellent in garden salads, on seafood, or drizzled over ripe berries.

name: Ritrovo Selections Organic Tomato Balsamic, 200ml
description: Ritrovo Selections is a premium importer of foods that represent Italy’s traditions and quality. Ritrovo means to rediscover in Italian. Over the last 20 years, the Seattle-based company has vastly expanded its line of products and won numerous international awards for quality. Their Organic Tomato Balsamic Vinegar captures the essence of the harvest in an invigorating sweet and savory vinegar. Made in Italy with juice extracted from tomatoes at peak ripeness and white grape must before being aged in wood, this vinegar will surprise you with its nuanced flavor. Excellent drizzled over caprese salads or on grilled halibut.

name: Ritrovo Selections Organic Turmeric Balsamic, 200ml
description: Ritrovo Selections is a premium importer of foods that represent Italy’s traditions and quality. Ritrovo means to rediscover in Italian. Over the last 20 years, the Seattle-based company has vastly expanded its line of products and won numerous international awards for quality. Their organic white balsamic with turmeric is truely unique. A SOFI Best New Product Award Winner, it strikes the perfect balance of sweet and mild bitterness with a lovely aromatic quality.

name: Regalis Cabernet Vinegar, 250ml
description: Brewed in Catalonia, Spain, this cabernet sauvignon vinegar carries deep notes of mature red fruits and chocolate. Made using the Schutzenbach method for acetification, this vinegar is as much an expression of terroir as the wine it came from. It has a balanced acidity, a sweet undertone, and a long finish. It rounds out a hearty beef stew beautifully, makes for a delectable reduction in a sweet application, and mixes into a terrific cocktail.

name: Regalis Chardonnay Vinegar, 250ml
description: Evocative of honey, citrus, and sunshine, this chardonnay vinegar is bursting with depth. Brewed from carefully sourced chardonnay wine, the brightness in this vinegar is mellowed by a hint of sweetness and a savory minerality. Several years of aging in our cellars lend this vinegar a full and dynamic mouthfeel. It heightens any seafood dish, whether a delicate hiramasa crudo or a lightly poached halibut filet, and shines in quick pickles or even behind the bar!

name: Regalis Cider Vinegar, 250ml
description: While the cider of northern Spain is revered in its own right, the vinegar it produces is equally bright and complex. Made with the famed Schutzenbach method, this apple cider vinegar mellows in acidity as it ages to offer a full bouquet of apple aromatics suggestive of almonds, cooked fruit, and spices. Needless to say, it is perfect for seasoning apples in sweet or savory applications, but will also instantly transform a pot of braised pork shoulder. It makes an easy natural tonic, too, when diluted with still or sparkling water.

name: Regalis Pedro Ximenez Vinegar, 250ml
description: For hundreds of years, Pedro Ximenez grapes have been dried under the Spanish sun and concentrated to produce a dessert wine. The vinegar produced from this wine shares these sweet, syrupy characteristics but is balanced by a delightful acidity and a long, full finish. This vinegar shines where a balsamic might, but is less sweet and offers more minerality. Consider using it drizzled over ice cream or fresh berries, or in a stonefruit salad with freshly pulled mozzarella.

name: Regalis Rose Wine Vinegar, 250ml
description: A versatile vinegar to be kept on the counter at all times, this rosé wine vinegar can be used universally wherever a balanced hit of acidity is required. Made from small production tempranillo wine using the Schutzenbach acetification method, it maintains floral notes of bright red berries and bittersweet fruit. While it pairs perfectly with summer vegetables and winter’s leafy greens, it also shines in a mignonette for oysters or used in a quick pickle.

name: VR Aceti Lambrusco Vinegar, 250ml
tagline: Ritrovo Selections product
description: Another great product from our good firends at Ritrovo Selections. Made by VR Aceti in Emilia Romagna, this vinegar is flavorful, full-bodied and complex. Made from 100% Lambrusco grapes, it is great for beef dishes, salads and marinades.

name: VR Aceti Trebbiano White Wine Vinegar, 250ml
tagline: Ritrovo Selections Product
description: Made by VR Aceti in Emilia Romagna, this vinegar is crisp and lively. Made from Trebbiano and Sauvignon Blanc grapes, is it perfect for salads, marinades and ceviche.

name: Boulou Cabernet Verjus Rouge, 750ml
description:
A classic condiment that dates back to ancient Rome, Verjus is the juice that’s made from the pressing of unripe grapes. Although similar to vinegar, Verjus it’s not acetified so it’s gentler and milder, not as acidic and with an added natural sweetness. And unlike wine, it’s not fermented so it doesn’t have any alcohol content.

Cabernet Verjus by Boulou is made from Cabernet wine grapes, beautifully red, sweet and fruity, with a well-balanced acidity. Use it to add a sweet-tart flavor and a deeper taste to recipes that would be overwhelmed by the tartness of vinegar - dressing, glaces, and even poaching fruit. This red wine verjus is perfect to soften the flavor of bitter greens like Arugula, or to add flavor to sauces and marinades for meats.

name: DeLouis Cider Vinegar, 500ml
description: DeLouis cider vinegar, also known as apple cider vinegar, is made from fermented apple juice. It is a popular ingredient in many cuisines and is widely used in cooking, pickling, and salad dressings. Cider vinegar has a pale amber color and a tangy, fruity flavor with a subtle sweetness. It is known for its mild, delicate taste, making it a popular choice for dishes where a strong vinegar flavor is overwhelming. It can be used to add flavor to a variety of dishes, including salads, marinades, sauces, and stews.

name: Pojer e Sandri Quince Wine Vinegar, 250ml
description:
Pojer e Sandri's single-fruit vinegars are in a class of their own. After carefully selecting fruit from the orchards of family, friends, and select farmers in the area, Pojer e Sandri gently press the fruit and inoculate the juice with yeast to ferment.

After reaching the desired sugar content, the fermented juice is placed in oak barrels containing some of the vinegar "mother." Depending on the fruit, the aging process might take anywhere from 18 to 24 months for the right balance of acidity and fruitiness to be achieved.

Quince's delicate aroma makes it perfectly suited for seafood such as poached halibut or sautéed scallops. Drizzle over tender greens or a tropical fruit salad made with mango and papaya.

name: Pojer e Sandri White Wine Vinegar, 250ml
description:
Pojer e Sandri crafts their White Wine Vinegar using a blend of local Dolomiti white grape varietals such as Riesling, Kerner, Incrocio Manzoni, Sauvignon, and Pinto Bianco. The resulting vinegar features aromatic floral notes of elderflower blossoms, acacia, and citrus zest, grounded by strong mineral notes that harken to the Dolomites' famous volcanic cliffs.

Ideal for use in making a lively mayonnaise; salad dressings for delicate and tender greens such as mache, lettuces, endives and frisee; and for pickling and preserving vegetables to make a giardiniera. This white wine vinegar will add a sparkle of brightness to any recipe calling for white wine.

name: American Vinegar Works 19.53 "Miles from the Tree Cider" Vinegar, 250ml
description: Made with apple cider from northern Massachusetts this Apple Cider Vinegar is a tribute to Johnny Appleseed who was born exactly 19.53 miles from vinegar works and is credited with spreading (apple cider!) apple trees. ACW thinks their former neighbor would really appreciate what they have done with his orchards and be smitten by this slightly sweet and highly tangy small-batch New England Apple Cider Vinegar.

name: American Vinegar Works Chardonnay Vinegar, 250ml
description: Made with chardonnay from California this vinegar would be a blanc de blancs if it were a champagne. Luckily it is not, it is better. It is slow fermented in small batches using a unique process from the early 1800s and aged in 25-gallon American oak barrels.

name: American Vinegar Works Honey Vinegar, 250ml
description: Honey wine, also known as mead, is an alcoholic beverage made by fermenting honey with water, sometimes with added fruits, spices, or herbs. With a rich history dating back to Viking and medieval times, it offers a sweet and aromatic drinking experience.The honey notes are unmistakable in this barrel-aged, limited-edition vinegar that has a warm, hazy honeycomb glow from the unfiltered and raw honey. Made with mead from Vermont and finished with raw clover honey after barrel aging!

name: American Vinegar Works Hot Cider Vinegar, 250ml
description: A truly unique vinegar and one of our favorites. This Apple Cider Hot Vinegar is made by co-fermenting local apple cider with a mix of fruit, spices, and peppers. It will start with a slightly smoky or bacon flavor followed by a savory note and, finally, just a touch of heat. This is not a hot sauce but a one-of-a-kind vinegar that you can add to nearly everything!

name: American Vinegar Works IPA Malt Vinegar, 250ml
description: Made from a Massachusetts craft IPA this vinegar is malty and tangy leaving you with a slight mouth water finish from the hops. It is slow fermented in small batches using a unique process from the early 1800s and aged in 25-gallon American oak barrels. This IPA Beer Malt Vinegar is the ultimate vinegar for fish and chips.

name: American Vinegar Works Maple Cider Vinegar, 250ml
description: Made with apple cider from northern Massachusetts and organic Vermont maple syrup from Runamok this vinegar perfectly balances sour and sweet to produce a beautifully toffeed cider vinegar. A little bit of fall in New England captured in a bottle!

name: American Vinegar Works Red Wine Vinegar, 250ml
description: Made with California Shiraz (or Syrah) this vinegar is a bold standout that will quickly become your go-to red wine vinegar for your most versatile vinaigrettes. This vinegar was co-fermented in small batches using a unique process from the early 1800s and aged in 25 gallon American oak barrels. This is one of the best red wine vinegars you can find.

name: American Vinegar Works Rice Wine Vinegar, 250ml
description: Made with junmai-grade sake from California this rice wine vinegar is elegant and has more weight than commercial vinegars. It is slow fermented in small batches using a unique process from the early 1800s and aged in 25-gallon American oak barrels. A perfect partner for your micro greens, cucumbers, and any other dish where you would use an expressive rice wine vinegar.

name: American Vinegar Works Rose Vinegar, 250ml
description: Made with California rose wine this vinegar is bright, summery, and, frankly, beautiful. It is slow fermented in small batches using a unique process from the early 1800s and aged in 25-gallon American oak barrels. Lighter than a red wine vinegar but with more body than a white wine vinegar.

name: Castello di Volpaia Red Wine Vinegar, 250ml
description: Produced in the cellars of a medieval village in the Chianti hills of Tuscany, Castello di Volpaia's aged red wine vinegar is produced from carefully selected wines of the region. These unique vinegars are produced using the "truciolo" method: the wine is percolated through "trucioli" (natural wood chips), transforming the natural alcohol of the wine into the acetic acid of vinegar while enhancing the wine's complex bouquet. After this, the vinegar is allowed to age in oak and chestnut barrels for another 10 to 12 months. The result is an intense, aromatic vinegar of exceptional roundness, with a rich flavor that enhances foods from salads to meats and berries. A little sediment in the bottom of the bottle is a natural byproduct of the process and will not detract from the qualities of the vinegar.

name: Castello di Volpaia Red Wine Vinegar, 500ml
description: Produced in the cellars of a medieval village in the Chianti hills of Tuscany, Castello di Volpaia's aged red wine vinegar is produced from carefully selected wines of the region. These unique vinegars are produced using the "truciolo" method: the wine is percolated through "trucioli" (natural wood chips), transforming the natural alcohol of the wine into the acetic acid of vinegar while enhancing the wine's complex bouquet. After this, the vinegar is allowed to age in oak and chestnut barrels for another 10 to 12 months. The result is an intense, aromatic vinegar of exceptional roundness, with a rich flavor that enhances foods from salads to meats and berries. A little sediment in the bottom of the bottle is a natural byproduct of the process and will not detract from the qualities of the vinegar.

name: Castello di Volpaia White Wine Vinegar, 250ml
description: Produced in the cellars of a medieval village in the Chianti hills of Tuscany, Castello di Volpaia's aged white wine vinegar is produced from carefully selected wines of the region. These unique vinegars are produced using the "truciolo" method: the wine is percolated through "trucioli" (natural wood chips), transforming the natural alcohol of the wine into the acetic acid of vinegar while enhancing the wine's complex bouquet. The result is an intense, bright vinegar with a rich flavor that enhances everything from salads to meats to fresh greens. Made with Trebbiano and Malvasia wine.

name: Castello di Volpaia White Wine Vinegar, 500ml
description: Produced in the cellars of a medieval village in the Chianti hills of Tuscany, Castello di Volpaia's aged white wine vinegar is produced from carefully selected wines of the region. These unique vinegars are produced using the "truciolo" method: the wine is percolated through "trucioli" (natural wood chips), transforming the natural alcohol of the wine into the acetic acid of vinegar while enhancing the wine's complex bouquet. The result is an intense, bright vinegar with a rich flavor that enhances everything from salads to meats to fresh greens. Made with Trebbiano and Malvasia wine.

name: El Majuelo Pedro Ximenez Sherry Vinegar, 250ml
description:
This sweet sherry vinegar is produced using the Pedro Ximénez grape. The grapes are left on the vine longer than usual, increasing the residual sugars and ultimately producing a sweet vinegar. The grapes are pressed and aged in American Oak barrels for at least 2 years. The result is an exquisite sweet and sour vinegar with a lower acidity.

El Majuelo is a family-run company in Jerez, Spain. Joaquin’s family has been making sherry vinegar in Jerez for 4 generations. A trained winemaker and cellarmaster, Joaquin took over the business from his father. He uses traditional criaderas and soleras process of transferring vinegars from barrel to barrel over a period of many years, giving the vinegars their unique character. El Majuelo is known as one of the top artisan sherry producers in the region.

name: El Majuelo Sherry Vinegar, 750ml
description:
This dark amber sherry vinegar is smooth and light-bodied. Made from 100% Palomina Fina grapes and aged six months, it is complex, with notes of fig, almond, and oak tempering the bright acidity of the vinegar.

El Majuelo is a family-run company in Jerez, Spain. Joaquin’s family has been making sherry vinegar in Jerez for 4 generations. A trained winemaker and cellarmaster, Joaquin took over the business from his father. He uses traditional criaderas and soleras process of transferring vinegars from barrel to barrel over a period of many years, giving the vinegars their unique character. El Majuelo is known as one of the top artisan sherry producers in the region.

name: L'Estornell Garnacha Red Wine Vinegar, 250ml
description: Produced in the southern region of Priorato in Catalonia, this vinegar is made exclusively from Garnacha grapes and then aged in oak barrels for at least 20 years. Ruby in color, L'Estornell Garnacha Red Wine Vinegar is bright and aromatic, making it perfect for a classic vinaigrette.

name: Sanchez Romate Sherry Vinegar, 375ml
description: Aged for at least three years in oak, this vinegar is mildly sweet and bright with hints of almonds. It's unique character can be attributed to the location where it is made (soil and proximity to the ocean), and the solera process by which it is aged. Throughout aging, the vinegar is transferred from oak barrel to oak barrel, all the while being mixed with wines of varied ages. This process provides layers of complexity and an unrivaled balance between sweetness and acidity. The result is a vinegar that is famously amazing with tomatoes, in dressings & for marinating.

name: Ximenez-Spinola Vinegar En Rama,
tagline: Unfiltered, all natural Pedro-Ximenez Vinegar
description:
Ximénez-Spínola is a small, independent family winery, a specialist in wine & vinegar products exclusively from Pedro Ximénez grapes. They put all their effort into the quality of its production, which guarentees each bottle of wine or vinegar is the full expression of their efforts.

This vinegar is the result of a wonderful mistake, the consequence of a natural process where the work of the yeasts known as "mycoderma" converted the Pedro Ximenez raisins into vinegar. The resulting vinegar is then obtained directly from the barrel. Bottled "En Rama" means that the vinegar is bottled unfiltered and in the same conditions in which it is taken directly from the cask without undergoing any further treatment, therefore maintaining all the aromas and flavours. This is an intensely acetic vinegar of great intensity and elegance, with the sweetness characteristic of the Pedro Ximenez variety.

name: Banyuls Vinegar, 500ml
description: This vinegar comes from the French seaside town of Banyuls, home to one of France's great wines of the same name. Aged in oak barrels for 5 years, Banyuls is uncommonly smooth. It has distinct aromas of walnut, spice, vanilla and licorice. Its nutty flavor profile makes it the perfect ingredient for vinaigrettes made with hazelnut or walnut oil. It's also great for deglazing - as it adds a balanced acidity to duck, game and foie gras.

name: Beaufor Champagne Vinegar, 500ml
description: It makes sense that Champagne makes good vinegar. It also makes sense that the resulting vinegar shares some of the same flavor and aromatic qualities of Champagne. With a slight hint of vanilla and a delicate and uniquely toasty bouquet, it is perfect for vinaigrettes and sauces. Imported from the heart of the Champagne region of France.

name: Beaufor Red Wine Vinegar, 500ml
description: This is the everyday red wine vinegar that you need to keep at the ready. Aged in oak barrels for 2 months, it is round, clean, woodsy and bright. Perfect for vinaigrettes and marinades.

name: Beaufor White Wine Vinegar, 500ml
description: An everyday vinegar made by a respected French company. This white wine vinegar is bright, clean and aromatic. Perfect for a classic French vinaigrette with mince shallots, egg yolk, dijon and extra virgin olive oil.

name: A L'Olivier Passion Fruit Vinegar, 200ml
description: In 1822, Monsieur Popelin, a pharmacist, set up a shop devoted to olive oil in Paris and A L'Olivier was born. Today, the family owned company still makes amazing olive oil, along with high quality vinegars and nut oils. This vinegar is simultaneously fresh, sour and smooth. Use it instead of lemon juice to finish grilled fish, or toss with a variety of fresh fruits.

name: A L'Olivier Raspberry Infused Vinegar, 200ml
description: In 1822, Monsieur Popelin, a pharmacist, set up a shop devoted to olive oil in Paris and A L'Olivier was born. Today, the family owned company still makes amazing olive oil, along with high quality vinegars and nut oils. A combination of intensely fruity, acidic raspberry and vinegar, this product is the ideal way to deglaze duck breasts, veal or chicken. Blend with hazelnut or olive oil in a salad with fennel, arugula and roasted hazelnuts. You can even stir it into sparkling water for a nonalcoholic cocktail.

name: Bragg's Apple Cider Vinegar, 16oz
description: Made from delicious, healthy, organically grown apples, this vinegar has a multitude of uses. Full of sweet acidity, it’s a wholesome way to add delicious flavor to salad dressings, sauces and marinades veggies.

name: Grosoli Cream with Balsamic Vinegar of Modena, 250ml
description: A reduction is only as good as the balsamic used. Sweet and savory, this thick, aromatic balsamic cream is ready to beautifully finish grilled meat and fish, salads, pasta and risotto.

name: DeLaurenti Garlic Butter
tagline: Made in the DeLaurenti kitchen!
description: We know that you can make garlic butter on your own – we also know that you (and we) rarely do. Please, allow us to help. You know the soft pillowy garlic bread wrapped in foil that always ruins whatever meals follows it? Well…now you can have that same great warm garlic bread sensation without all the negative consequences. Spread this butter on your favorite loaf of artisan bread, wrap it in foil and pop it in the oven. Made with 82% butter fat butter, freshly roasted garlic, herbs, a pinch of chili flakes & Parmigiano-Reggiano. Perfect for tossing with fresh pappardelle, on corn on the cob or grilled fish. Also makes a great steak butter!

name: DeLaurenti Truffle Butter
tagline: Made in the DeLaurenti kitchen!
description: This butter is made in the comfort of the DeLaurenti kitchen with 82% butterfat butter, truffle flecks and high quality truffle oil. Mixed, molded and set, it is ready to toss with your fresh pappardelle or dolloped on a bone-in ribeye!

name: A Butter Place Cacio e Pepe Butter
description: The folks behind A Butter Place started making butter as a pandemic hobby, hand-kneading each pound. Their technique is based on the old-time French style. Based in the Greenwood neighborhood of Seattle, their mission is simple: to provide high-quality, flavorful butter made from locally sourced Cream from Washington Jersey cows, enriched with real, local ingredients. With black pepper, Parmigiano-Reggiano & subtle lemon zest, their Cacio e Pepe compound butter is perfect for finishing a steak or topping grilled vegetables. You're just minutes away from sophisticated butter noodles!

name: A Butter Place Salted Bulk Butter
description: The folks behind A Butter Place started making butter as a pandemic hobby, hand-kneading each pound. Their technique is based on the old-time French style. Based in the Greenwood neighborhood of Seattle, their mission is simple: to provide high-quality, flavorful butter made from locally sourced Cream from Washington Jersey cows, enriched with real, local ingredients. Their salted bulk butter is perfect on a crusty loaf of bread!

name: A Butter Place Unsalted Bulk Butter
description: The folks behind A Butter Place started making butter as a pandemic hobby, hand-kneading each pound. Their technique is based on the old-time French style. Based in the Greenwood neighborhood of Seattle, their mission is simple: to provide high-quality, flavorful butter made from locally sourced Cream from Washington Jersey cows, enriched with real, local ingredients. Their unsalted bulk butter will take your baking to the next level!

name: Beillevaire Seaweed Butter, 125g
description: Pascal Beillevaire, renowned French affineur, doesn't stop at making cheese. His butter is the same as his cheese...amazing. It is made using pasteurized cow's milk, churned and shaped in wooden molds with flakes of seaweed. Perfect for pairing with seafood!

name: Belgioioso Mascarpone, 16oz
description: In 1990, Belgioso became the first American company to start making Italian-style mascarpone. They got it right. This is your key ingredient for your famous tiramisu, Also fantastic with a myriad of other desserts and atop fresh berries!

name: Beurre de Barrate Fleur de Sel, 250g
description:
If you are looking for the butter wrapped in gold foil, this is it! We are now stocking beurre de baratte directly from Fromagerie Réo in Normandy, France. Founded in 1931 by cheesemaker Théodore Réaux, Fromagerie Réo is one of the few remaining producers of traditional beurre de baratte. Located in Lessay, Manche, the dairy is committed to supporting the local economy and promoting sustainable practices. It sources milk from approximately forty producers located within a 30 km radius of the facility. Since 2016, Réo has been part of the Les Maîtres Laitiers du Cotentin group. Réo’s beurre de baratte is manually molded and offered under the brand Le Gaslonde. Made from local pasteurized cream, fleur de sel from Île de Ré, and cultures, the butter naturally varies in color throughout the year—from a deep yellow in spring, due to chlorophyll and beta-carotene in fresh grass, to a pale ivory in winter.

Long story short... Rodolphe le Meunier buys the beurre de baratte directly from Fromagerie Réo and wraps it in that distinctive gold packaging. Le Gaslonde beurre de baratte is 100% exactly the same product as the gold foil version—same producer, ingredients, size, etc.

name: Buji Brown Butter Stick
tagline: Brown Butter Perfected!
description: Buji Brown Butter was born from Lisa Herlinger’s passion for transforming simple ingredients into deep, complex flavors. Carefully crafted by cooking down grassfed salted butter and browning the milk solids to perfection, Buji Brown Butter is an excellent addition to your kitchen. Buji’s rich, nutty aroma, smooth texture and depth of flavor will leave a lasting impression on everyone who tastes it. Buji Brown Butter shines at breakfast served with oatmeal, French toast, or used to cook eggs. It elevates your dinner as a finishing butter on grilled or roasted meats and veggies. Not to mention all of its potential uses in baking! The possibilities are endless!

name: Burro di Panna Acidificata, 4oz
description: Discover a butter unlike any other, where tradition meets extraordinary flavor and texture. Guffanti's rich and intense cow's milk butter owes its unique personality—a very light and pleasant acidity—to an all-natural "secret": the acidification of the cream. They use the microorganisms naturally present in fresh cream to initiate a slow and controlled fermentation. The result? A butter with rich aromas and intense flavor and an incredibly creamy texture, perfect at any time of the day, from early morning to a gourmet snack. Magnificent on toast with anchovies for a bold and sophisticated contrast, or paired with jams and compotes to enhance their sweetness.

name: DeLaurenti House Butter
tagline: Fresh bulk butter with course sea salt
description: After a few issues with the FDA, we went looking to replace the French bulk butter we regularly had in the deli. For the life of us, we couldn't find something that had both the quality & the large sea salt crystals that we were after. Turns out, it was right in our back yard the whole time. Our friends at Cherry Valley Dairy in Duvall were kind enough to combine our favorite bulk fleur de sel with their amazing butter and voila! We had it! Made from the milk of their Jersey cows, it is silky, smooth & creamy with an occasional crunch from the course sea salt. Serve it like cheese, your friends will think it's the most buttery cheese they've ever had.

name: Delitia Water Buffalo Milk Whey Butter, 8oz
description: Water Buffalo Milk Whey Butter is a luxurious, creamy butter made from the milk of water buffaloes. Renowned for its rich and slightly tangy flavor, it's a gourmet alternative to traditional cow's milk butter. This artisanal butter is characterized by a smooth texture and a deeper, more complex taste profile, making it a favorite among chefs for its ability to elevate the flavors in a variety of dishes. It tastes best when consumed plain, on rustic bread or seasonal vegetables while remaining an ideal ingredient in cakes or custards.

name: Fatworks Chicken Fat Organic Cooking Oil, 212g
tagline: Kettle Rendered Chicken Schmaltz
description: Nothing really compares to organic Chicken Fat Schmaltz. It has the richness of duck fat but with a milder and more aromatic flavor. Schmaltz adds complexity to a variety of dishes that you simply cannot reproduce any other way. Schmaltz is a joy to cook with and is the easiest way to add depth and complexity to leafy vegetables, stir-fries, pan-fried steaks, fish, poultry, soups, stews, baked goods, and for a special treat spread it right on a piece of bread like you would a high-quality butter or fine olive oil. It's no exaggeration to say Schmaltz gives potatoes and other root vegetables a flavor that is beyond anything most of us have experienced. If potatoes could talk to schmaltz they would say, "You complete me!" Fatworks Chicken Schmaltz is made with 100% Organic Free Range Chicken and is rendered with the typical care and passion that you would expect from Fatworks.

name: Fatworks Leaf Lard Cooking Oil, 396g
tagline: Kettle-Rendered Made From Pastured Pork
description:
The finest Pasture Raised Leaf Lard available. The gourmet baker's secret weapon. The perfect gateway fat for those who don't want too much pork flavor in their lard. Rendered from the prized pasture-raised "leaf" (internal fat) making it less "porky" tasting than our other lard offering which comes from back fat.

Both have their uses but as there is no meat muscle in the leaf, this lard has a milder pork flavor. This makes for an amazing cooking fat that is delicate, light and "clean" tasting. Bakers have cherished Pasture Raised Leaf Lard because it creates the best crusts and cakes while not imparting any flavor of its own. And because of its high smoke point, Fatworks Pastured Raised Leaf Lard is simply perfect for frying and sautéing, especially when you want the natural flavors of your ingredients to shine. Fatworks Pure Premium Pasture Raised Leaf Lard is essential for anyone interested in cooking with traditional fat. They source the fat from small family farms in the US.

name: Fatworks Traditional Ghee, Cultured Clarified Butter, 212g
tagline: Grass-Fed
description: Let's give some clarity to this clarified butter thing...if it's not cultured, it's not traditional ghee. Fatworks is sure that there are those who wish to debate this, but traditional ghee IS indeed cultured. That's why they insist on sourcing cultured, organic grass-fed butter from domestic family farms. Fatworks experimented with less expensive organic butters from New Zealand and Europe but found that nothing came close to the butter they could source right here in the USA. Fatworks Traditional Ghee is small-batch cooked and roasted to spoon-licking perfection. Use it as you would butter or other cooking oils. Try our Ghee in baking, in a skillet or from the spoon. Also good in smoothies and even coffee to give you clean fat fuel for the day. Their grass fed cow ghee is sourced from 100% Organic butter, is Keto and Paleo friendly as well as being Lactose and Casein Free. So, step right up and get your Vitamin B12, Vitamin A, Vitamin E, Vitamin D, CLA, MCT and Omega 3s. The smoke point is over 480? so this Ghee is great for high heat cooking!

name: Isigny Beurre de Baratte, 250g
tagline: Traditional French Butter from Normandy
description: Isigny Ste Mere's creamy, yellow-hued butter has a distinct caramelized and nutty flavor, made using traditional Baratte method in Normandy, France. Churned and formed by hand, it has just the right amount of salt. Perfect for toast, croissants, scones and more.

name: Le Gall Demi-Sel Butter, 250g
tagline: Impossibly creamy French butter...seriously
description: This staff favorite is made in Brittany, France, a marshy region so famous for its butter that it was historically exempt from the salt tax! Produced with fresh cream and fermented using traditional methods, this butter is a game changer. Layers of distinct, rich flavor border on cheese-like qualities. Oh, and the texture. Impossibly smooth and creamy with a minimum of 82% butter fat. Yup, I said it...let's not pretend here people. Keep this butter at the ready for your favorite warm bread or baguette. The origin of the expression "it's the bread and butter of the operation" comes to mind. Next time you have a few people over, put it out as the "cheese" course and don't tell anyone. Sorry...and you're welcome!

name: Le Gall Doux Butter, 250g
tagline: Impossibly creamy French butter...seriously
description: This staff favorite is made in Brittany, France, a marshy region so famous for its butter that it was historically exempt from the salt tax! Produced with fresh cream and fermented using traditional methods, this butter is a game changer. Layers of distinct, rich flavor border on cheese-like qualities. Oh, and the texture. Impossibly smooth and creamy with a minimum of 82% butter fat. Yup, I said it...let's not pretend here people. Keep this butter at the ready for your favorite warm bread or baguette. The bakers on our staff LOVE using this butter to make the most delightfully tender cakes!

name: Les Pres Sale Butter, 8.8oz
description: Stroopwaffles, beer, cycling, and...this butter. Just a few of the great things about Belgium. Churned to a creamy, lush 82% butterfat and flecked with coarse sea salt from Camargue, all that is missing is your favorite loaf of bread.

name: Little Island Creamery Butter, 8oz
description: Located on Puget Island in the Columbia River at Cathlamet, WA, Little Island Creamery is a 54 acre farm comprised of a barn, built in 1946, some out buildings and beautiful pastures. They raise and milk purebred Jersey cows whose milk is high in butter fat, which makes the best cheese, butter and curds anywhere! They love their cows and the love comes through! This butter is the real deal...rich, ultra-creamy and beyond flavorful!

name: Payson Breton Butter, 250g
description: This might be our customer's favorite butter. Commonly known as "the one in the blue checked wrapper," it is impossibly creamy and flecked with crunchy flecks of sea salt. This is not your cooking butter, this is your eating butter. Option 1: Baguette, butter, wine. Option 2: Baguette, butter, honey, coffee.

name: Plugra Salted Butter, 8oz
description: Plugrá uses specially selected cream with just the right amount of butterfat to produce the highest-quality European Style Butter. If you want to make great pastry, enrich sauces, or simply enjoy a piece of bread, this will help. Lightly salted & ready to go in a 1/2 pound block.

name: Plugra Unsalted Butter, 1#
description: Plugrá uses specially selected cream with just the right amount of butterfat to produce the highest-quality European Style Butter. If you want to make great pastry, enrich sauces, or simply enjoy a piece of bread, this will help. Unsalted & in a full pound block. Looks impressive in your refrigerator.

name: Plugra Unsalted Butter, 8oz
description: Plugrá uses specially selected cream with just the right amount of butterfat to produce the highest-quality European Style Butter. If you want to make great pastry, enrich sauces, or simply enjoy a piece of bread, this will help. Unsalted & ready to go in a 1/2 pound block.

name: Sterilgarda Panna da Cucina, 200ml
description: Panna da Cucina by Sterilgarda is the go-to cooking cream in Italian households. Silky, rich, and perfectly balanced for both savory and sweet recipes. From a classic pasta al salmone to a velvety mushroom risotto or a simple panna cotta, this is the cream that makes it all.

name: Good Honey Creamed Clover, 16oz
description:
The Ashusrt Family are 5th generation bee keepers, home harvesting honey in the USA since 1919.

Their Montana Creamed Clover honey is their raw and pure, using their unique creaming method. Good Honey’s creamed clover is whipped and chilled to perfection, creating a luxuriously smooth and spreadable texture. Crafted from only the finest clover blossoms, their creamed honey boasts a rich and delicate sweetness with a perfect velvety finish. It’s great for spreading over warm toast, stirring into tea, or enjoying by the spoonful!

name: Good Honey Montana Clover, 16oz
description:
The Ashusrt Family are 5th generation bee keepers, home harvesting honey in the USA since 1919.

Their Montana Clover Honey is the Olympic gold medal of honeys. When Montana Clover blooms in the summer months, Beekeepers and bees alike spend countless hours looking for this liquid gold. Although there are over 300 varieties of clover flowers, Montana Sweet Clover (Melilotus officinalis) is prized for its superior taste. They harvest it as a pure Montana clover, meaning it is not blended with other varieties, and is among some of the lightest colored honeys produced. Our favorite quality is its candied sweetness. If you’re looking for the most premium & tasty honey, look no further!

Delicate and sweet with clean floral notes. (A finishing honey)

name: La Trinquelinette Apricot Jam, 370g
description: This apricot jam is made in a small batches by a small family business in the village of Saint-Léger-Vauban in the Burgundy region. This area of France is known for its fertile soil and vineyards. All their jams are made with local fruit and brown unrefined sugar. Some of the jams are thicken with pectinei and some use rhubarb.Not too sweet, but sweet enough - perfect for your toasted baguette, French butter & coffee!

name: La Trinquelinette Blackberry Jam, 370g
description: This apricot jam is made in a small batches by a small family business in the village of Saint-Léger-Vauban in the Burgundy region. This area of France is known for its fertile soil and vineyards. All their jams are made with local fruit and brown unrefined sugar. Some of the jams are thicken with pectinei and some use rhubarb.Not too sweet, but sweet enough - perfect for your toasted baguette, French butter & coffee!

name: La Trinquelinette Raspberry Jam, 370g
description: This raspberry jam is made in a small batches by a small family business in the village of Saint-Léger-Vauban in the Burgundy region. This area of France is known for its fertile soil and vineyards. All their jams are made with local fruit and brown unrefined sugar. Some of the jams are thicken with pectinei and some use rhubarb.Not too sweet, but sweet enough - perfect for your toasted baguette, French butter & coffee!

name: La Trinquelinette Strawberry Jam, 370g
description: This strawberry jam is made in a small batches by a small family business in the village of Saint-Léger-Vauban in the Burgundy region. Some of the jams are thicken with pectinei and some use rhubarb.Not too sweet, but sweet enough - perfect for your toasted baguette, French butter & coffee!

name: Pojer e Sandri Quince Syrup, 150g
description:
Pojer e Sandri Cold Pressed Quince Syrup is made from 100% cold concentrated quince juice, and nothing else.

Their estate’s orchard is located at 700 meters and is surrounded by forest, an ideal location for organically cultivating two varieties of quince, Ronda and Silver. Every fall, they cold press carefully selected fruit into juice. Using a unique vacuum processing, Pojer e Sandri are able to concentrate the quince juice to a thick, maple syrup consistency without adding any sugar. Thus, the intrinsic characteristics of the quince remain intact in the final product.

Pojer e Sandri has truly captured the essence of quince. Unlike most sugary syrups, this Quince Syrup bursts with a tannic tartness balanced by just enough natural sweetness. The quince fruit’s distinct aromas and notes of plum, molasses, and pine are concentrated. One spoonful packs a flavorful punch that evokes the mountainous region from which it originates.

name: Girl Meets Dirt Ginny Jam, 7.75oz
description:
In an orchard by the sea (Warm Valley Orchard) lies a grove of old Italian Plum trees, harvested by long time islanders Bob & Maria Nutt. These beautiful plums have been crated off to Seattle the past few years to be soaked with botanicals in gin by Copperworks Distilling for their lauded & award winning Plum Gin (side note, Bob is brothers with Copperworks Founder Micah and Audra bought her first Shiro Plums aside from the farmette tree, from the Nutt family).

A few years back we fielded a call from Copperworks- basically- hey- we’ve got these boozy plums we normally compost but maybe you want them? HECK YA we do.

So in true full circle fashion we picked up a truckload of buckets of the inaugural 2021 season island Italian plums that had spent most of 2022 on the lash in a gin bath and brought them back home. We rolled up our sleeves and hand pitted each and every one of them, added some sugar and a squeeze of lemon to the party and have an exquisite new limited edition preserve!

name: Girl Meets Dirt Hot Damn Pepper Jam Spoon Preserves, 7.75oz
description:
The Girl Meets Dirt crew is really into fruit, but their farmers grow great vegetables too! Time to fire up the peppers. The result is a not so usual pepper jelly. They gave it the old GMD spin and maxxed out the spiciness but added lots of local fruit and a bit of punchy organic vinegar (made from WA apples) for balance. The quince and apple add body to the set allowing GMD to stay committed to their ‘no pectin’ policy. It’s legit hot (yes!). It’s legit amazing. And it’s all natural.

This is one of those jars you need in your refrigerator to spice up lackluster meals (visualize dipping coconut shrimp or topping grilled salmon) and serve as an instant cheese pairing by slathering on cream cheese and crackers at a moment’s notice. They're a game-changer for any charcuterie board or cheeseboard!

name: Girl Meets Dirt Orcas Pear, 7.75oz
description: At the height of ripeness Girl Meets Dirt picks Orcas Island pears and cooks them into a rosy preserve, with notes of ginger from their fresh kitchen garden grown bay leaves. Highly versatile, this preserve is a gorgeous topping to pannacotta and cheesecake.

name: Girl Meets Dirt Pear Balsamic. 7.75oz
description: This jam is always a star on a cheeseboard or grazing board with taleggio, asiago and blues. Truly an all-purpose condiment – try it over ice cream. Or play around – add a few glugs of balsamic to a teaspoonful, extra virgin olive oil, salt, and minced shallots and puree it together for a quick, rich vinaigrette for a salad (topped with blue cheese, fresh pear slices, and crispy shallots). Spoon it over a wedge of Rogue River Blue with wafer thin crackers or fresh pear slices for an intensely satisfying cheese pairing.

name: Girl Meets Dirt Rhuberry Preserves, 220g
description:
The Girl Meets Dirt crew is really into fruit, but their farmers grow great vegetables too! Time to fire up the peppers. The result is a not so usual pepper jelly. They gave it the old GMD spin and maxxed out the spiciness but added lots of local fruit and a bit of punchy organic vinegar (made from WA apples) for balance. The quince and apple add body to the set allowing GMD to stay committed to their ‘no pectin’ policy. It’s legit hot (yes!). It’s legit amazing. And it’s all natural.

This bright ruby small batch Reserve folds grassy red rhubarb from Ralph's Greenhouse in the Skagit Valley and from JBS Farm in Crow Valley on Orcas (where John and Susan Fleischer tend crowns that have been in the ground for fifty years) with tart, plump Northwest raspberries — classically preserved in just six copper pots, the way they always have.

name: Casina Rossa Saffron & Acacia Honey, 140g
description: Casina Rossa is a brand of artisan food products from the Abruzzo region of Italy created by Nicola and Paola DeLaurentiis. Their Saffron & Acacia Honey is complements aged cheeses, ice cream, or even roasted chicken or scallops.

name: Chateau Miraval Lavendar Honey, 500g
description: Château Miraval Lavender Honey is a rare, limited-edition, raw honey produced directly on the Provence property, often harvested in the summer or fall by resident beekeeper Noel Patterson. It is known for its delicate floral taste and creamy texture, reflecting the aromatic lavender fields surrounding the estate.

name: Dalmatia Fig & Orange Spread, 240g
description: Dalmatia combines the sweetness of Croatian figs with the zesty pop of coastal oranges. Made with care using hand-selected fruits, this is the perfect accompaniment to your charcuterie or cheese board. It pairs nicely with blue cheeses such as Bleu des Basque or Mitibleu, bloomy rind cheeses such as Brie du Pommier or Fromage de Meaux, or with fresh ricotta and walnuts over toasted bread. It’s not limited to cheese, however. It’s the perfect complement to your morning coffee when spread liberally on toast with butter.

name: Dalmatia Fig Spread, 240g
description: As good on toast as it is with aged sheep's milk cheese, this spread is made with figs from the Croatian coast. After we tried it for the first time, we knew it had to be on our shelves. This spread pairs well with almost any cheese - from rich and creamy to dry and sharp. Love figs, but not with cheese? No problem. Spread liberally on toast with butter and enjoy with your morning coffee!

name: Dalmatia Sour Cherry Spread, 240g
description: Dalmatia uses perfectly-ripened Croatian sour cherries to make this delightful spread. A popular charcuterie board recommendation from our deli staff, this spread pairs especially well with tangy goat cheeses such as Florette, Humboldt Fog, or Bocconcino di Langa. It also makes an excellent filling for chocolate cake or cookies!

name: Formaticum Cheese Bags, 15 count
tagline: Makes your cheese last longer & taste better!
description: Cheese is a living thing, and like all living things, it requires certain conditions to thrive. These French-made cheese storage bags provide the ideal environment for cheese to maintain its best qualities in your home refrigerator. Breathable enough to keep the cultures in the cheese alive, while still retaining enough humidity to avoid drying. Each package contains fifteen bags. A perfect gift for the discerning cheese lover!

name: Formaticum Cheese Papers, 20 count
tagline: Makes your cheese last longer & taste better!
description: Cheese is a living thing, and like all living things, it requires certain conditions to thrive. These French-made cheese storage papers are specially designed to keep cheese at its best in your home refrigerator. The paper allows cheese to breathe, while still retaining enough moisture to prevent drying. Each package contains fifteen sheets of paper and fifteen stickers. A perfect gift for the discerning cheese lover!

name: Girl Meets Dirt Bluebarb Preserves, 220g
description:
The Girl Meets Dirt crew is really into fruit, but their farmers grow great vegetables too! Time to fire up the peppers. The result is a not so usual pepper jelly. They gave it the old GMD spin and maxxed out the spiciness but added lots of local fruit and a bit of punchy organic vinegar (made from WA apples) for balance. The quince and apple add body to the set allowing GMD to stay committed to their ‘no pectin’ policy. It’s legit hot (yes!). It’s legit amazing. And it’s all natural.

In their Bluebarb Preserve, rhubarb, the harbinger of their season, with Cascadia blueberries and their classic French-inspired flair. This one is the PNW at her best.

name: Wedge Cheese Knives, 3 set
description:
Holcomb Studio's Wedge Cheese Knives are designed with sharp geometric blades and elongated frosted sage handles, adding depth and interest to any cheese board. The set includes three knives tailored for hard cheeses, soft cheeses, and every cheese in between. Their sharp, pointed blades make slicing and serving cheese easy.

The Wedge Cheese Knives are made of high-polished stainless steel and Tritan, and are dishwasher safe. Seemlessly blending modernity with natural, timeless materials, these knives are a stunning and handy addition to your kitchen!

name: Staff Pick - Goat's Milk
tagline: You choose the texture & the flavor, we'll choose the cheese!
description: If you are reading this, you like goat's milk cheese. Well, we do too! Here's all you do: just choose the texture, flavor & the amount and we'll do the rest! Based on your answers, we'll choose a cheese that we love and that fits your criteria - couldn't be easier! It's just like standing in front of the cheese case! Feel free to add any specifics in the Instructions/Additions field at checkout. The published price per lb is only a place holder - the exact price of the cheese will be determined by the amount selected and the actual price per lb of the cheese selected

name: L'Abbaye de Bel'loc
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - L'Abbaye de Bel'loc - Pyrenees, France
description: A beloved Basque sheep cheese, L'Abbaye de Bel'loc was facing extinction only a few years ago. Abbaye Notre-Dame de Bel'loc has been home to Benedictine monks since 1875. In 1959, they decided to start making cheese with milk from their own flock. Their cheese quickly became an international favorite. Unfortunately, by 2018, the monastery was down to only 20 residents and without new priests joining their community to continue their tradition of cheesemaking, they made the difficult decision to stop exporting their cheese. Thanks to the French nonprofit Habitat et Humanisme stepping in and using the abbey to house cheesemaking interns and others struggling with housing issues, we are able to enjoy this cheese again! Dense and silky, this delightful cheese has notes of brown butter, cooked cream, toasted nuts, and pale caramel. Try it and you will understand why we are so excited to have it back!

name: Tomme Corse Brebis
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Ottavi - Corsica
description: For 150 years, the Ottavi family's legacy has been passed down from generation to generation with a deep respect for tradition. Nestled in the Fium'Orbu Valley in Haute Corse, they work with the same passion as their ancestors to create cheeses that reflect their land and history. Their cheesemaking adventure began in 1948, when the generation in charge decided to create the Ottavi cheese dairy. From the beginning, everything was handmade and sold directly to locals, door to door. It is this proximity to people and to nature that has forged their identity. In the 1960s, faced with the growing success of their products, they decided to focus exclusively on cheese and maintaining traditional methods. Despite the changes of time, they remain committed to the ancestral practices passed down through the years and continue to produce cheeses with the same care to ensure authenticity. Each cheese is a way for them to extend this family heritage, while sharing a little of the Corsica they love so much. Tomme Corse Brebis is made from sheep’s milk and aged in the Ottavi cellars for three months where it develops its fruity and nutty taste. Excellent as a snack or grated over salads and pasta!

name: Ombra (Ros)
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Josep Cuixart - Catalonia, Spain
description: Ombra as it is known in the USA, Ros to the Spaniards, was created by esteemed Spanish cheesemaker Josep Cuixart. The name Ros means "blondie" in Catalan and was chosen to reflect Cuixart's nickname, (due to his fair hair) and the straw color of the cheese's interior when mature. Wheels are about three inches tall, with a natural rind, coated with gray and brown molds. The minimum age is four months, but the cheese can withstand up to ten months of ripening. The interior paste is firm and close-textured and occasionally studded with crunchy nuggets of crystalized amino acids. Flavors are of butterscotch and pineapple, and well balanced between citrus acidity and the sweetness of the milk. Once in hand, all you need is a glass of Rioja.

name: Le Berger Basque
tagline: Raw Sheep - Fermiers Basco Bearnais - Midi-Pyrenees, France
description: Great things come from the Basque region of France & Spain. Among them...breath taking views, iconic cycling climbs & beautifully aged sheep's milk cheeses. Le Berger Basque is a rustic, raw milk example that is a staff favorite. It is at once nutty, earthy, herbaceous and sweet. The paste is dense and creamy, growing more assertive toward the natural rind. If you enjoy other cheeses like Ossau-Iraty or Pyrenees Brebis, you need to add this one to the list!

name: Le Secret de Compostelle
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Agour - Pyrenees, France
description: This is a secret you want in on! Produced by Fromagerie Agour, Le Secret de Compostelle is an aged sheep milk cheese in the “brebis Pyrennes” style, similar to Ossau Iraty. Its name pays homage to a passage between the French and Spanish Basque regions, which was commonly traversed by pilgrims on their way to the city of Santiago de Compostela (Compostelle in French). Aged around eight months, this cheese is dense and firm, with a smooth, creamy texture. The natural rind is mildly pungent and savory, while the paste of the offers notes of cream, caramel, nuts, mushrooms, and olives.

name: Adarre
tagline: Pasteurized Goat/Sheep - Rodolphe le Meunier - Pays Basque, France
description: Put simply, this is a spectacular cheese. From the Basque region in France, it is selected by renowned affineur Rodolphe Le Meunier. Like any great recipe, all its components are in balance. Sweet, nutty, bright & tangy, it is the perfect combination of sheep & goat's milk. Add in it's creamy mouthfeel, and you know why Adarre makes every DeLa Deli Team member's Top 5!

name: Bamboozle
tagline: Pasteurized Cow & Goat - Goat Rodeo Farm & Dairy - Pittsburgh, PA
description: India Loevner and her husband, Steve, have owned their 130-acre rural property near Pittsburgh for decades. They raised their children there, with chickens and pigs, but it was never a working farm until India accompanied a friend to a dairy goat show and came home with the two top finishers. Goat Rodeo Farm & Dairy, the inevitable outcome, now makes about a half-dozen cheeses, from fresh chèvre to goat Gouda. Bamboozle is a blend of goat's milk from the Loevners' herd and cow's milk from neighboring farms. Supple, semi-soft texture with notes of prosciutto and peanuts, Bamboozle is aged for at least two months and washed with beer from Cinderlands Beer Co. Equally at home on a cheese board or melted on a burger!

name: Cabra Romero
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Lorenzo - Murcia, Spain
description: From the Murcia region of Spain, this mild goat cheese receives a coating of rosemary and lard in its final days of aging. Though the rosemary makes this cheese exceedingly herbaceous, it complements, rather than competes with the cheese itself. Murcia is known for its excellent quality of goat’s milk and this cheese is a reflection of it. The paste is ivory white & creamy with a bright, pleasantly piquant flavor.

name: Chabrin
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Onetik - Macaye, France
description:
From the French Basque Country, Chabrin is a natural rind, pressed cheese made in the traditions of the region using milk from a cooperative of farmers. Each wheel is aged in their cellars, for three months giving the cheese a lovely mineral aroma.

It is mildly goaty with sweet and nutty overtones. The dense, smooth and creamy texture coats the palette and lingers, makes this a very approachable introduction to goats’ milk cheese. Among aged goat cheeses, Chabrin is a DeLaurenti Deli Team favorite!

name: Ciel de Chevre
tagline: Raw Goat - Le Fermiere de Mean - Ardennes, Belgium
description: Modeled on a cow’s milk cheese made by the same producer, Ciel de Chevre is a Trappist style raw goat’s milk cheese. The milk used in this cheese is from a single farm-member of the cooperative. Over the course of 6 weeks, the cheese is washed in a brine solution that gives Ciel de Chevre’s salmon-pink rind its color and helps the ivory white interior develop its flavor and supple texture. The flavor of the semi-soft paste is tangy and savory to the point of meatiness. Its rind is edible and has a crunchy texture and salty flavor.

name: Etorki
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Fromagerie des Chaumes - Basque, France
description: Produced at Fromagerie des Chaumes at Mauléon, in southwestern France, Etorki, which means "origin" in local dialect, is a Basque-style sheep's milk cheese. The texture of Etorki is smooth, supple and velvety. The color of the interior paste is a gentle, golden, ivory and there are occasional holes or slits. Aromas are earthy and sweet. Flavors are rich and sweet with notes of hazelnut and caramel.

name: Fleur du Maquis
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Ottavi - Corsica
description: Made in Corsica from the milk of Lacaune ewes, this cheese's name translates to "flower of the maquis," the "maquis" being a local term for the typical thickets of rough underbrush where highway robbers and guerrilla fighters used to hang out. This cheese also goes by "Brin d'Amour," meaning "a breath of love." The sheep freely browse Corsica's scrubby, Mediterranean landscape and during production, to enhance the natural flavors present in the milk, the small cheeses are encrusted with rosemary, savory, oregano, marjoram, basil, and thyme. When young, Fleur du Maquis is semi-firm, pliable and moist, with citrus flavors and a pleasant, bright tang. With age the rind becomes dotted with a blue-grey mold. The texture of the cheese also becomes softer, absorbing the savory and herbaceous flavors of the rind. Flavors strike a delicate balance with the herbs, enhancing the warm, bright, sheepy quality of the interior paste. If allowed to mature fully, the paste breaks down and becomes runny and stronger tasting. This cheese pairs well with many types of wines, particularly Tempranillo and Alberino. It's fun to experiment alongside honeys, too; try it with a thyme honey or a floral honey from Corsica.

name: Garrotxa
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Sant Gil d'Albio - Catalonia, Spain
description: After near extinction in the early 80's, Garrotxa has grown in popularity and demand the last few decades, again becoming one of Spain's most notable goat cheeses. From the Catalan region in southern Spain, Garrotxa is immediately recognized by its powdery, suede-like gray rind. The moist paste is bright white with occasional small holes, or eyes. Flavors are earthy, nutty, and tangy, with a balanced acidity. Pairs well with marcona almonds, dry sherry, Rioja or cava.

name: Hootenanny
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Goat Rodeo Farm & Dairy - Pittsburgh, PA
description: India Loevner and her husband, Steve, have owned their 130-acre rural property near Pittsburgh for decades. They raised their children there, with chickens and pigs, but it was never a working farm until India accompanied a friend to a dairy goat show and came home with the two top finishers. Goat Rodeo Farm & Dairy, the inevitable outcome, now makes about a half-dozen cheeses, from fresh chèvre to goat Gouda. Hootenanny is their award-winning goat’s milk Gouda cheese made from spring and summer milk. Supple with notes of hickory nuts and wild flowers within a beautiful cream wax rind. Pairs well with crisp white wine or an amber ale.

name: L'Estanguet
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Les Saloirs de Louis - Basque Country, France
description: Louis Madec began his career as a shepherd before transitioning to aging cheese. Leading his sheep across the high mountain pastures and making cheese in a traditional cauldron gave him an appreciation for livestock farming and cheesemaking. Working with small producers in the valleys of the Upper Béarn, he selects cheeses with an objective of respect for the product, traditions, and the terroir. In addition to those traditional cheeses, he also ages some more innovative styles. L'Estanguet, a semi-firm goat cheese washed with Jurançon wine, is a result of such innovation. Sweet, creamy, tangy and nutty, the complex flavor of this goat tomme has quickly become a staff favorite!

name: La Chevrette
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Barbichette - Pays Basque, France
description: Part of the Barbichette range from Fromi, La Chevrette is a small goat tomme from the Pays Basque. Ripened for two months, we love its soft texture, distinctive rind, and delicately goaty notes. This Basque treat is the perfect snack for any time of day!

name: La Dama Sagrada
tagline: Raw Goat - MItica - Castilla la Mancha, Spain
description: La Dama Sagrada, or Sacred Dame, is produced using raw Murciana goat’s milk in the town of El Carpio de Tajo in the Castile-La Mancha Region. Made using the molds of a Manchego, the rind has the characteristic basket-weave pattern. With a minimum of 6 months aging, the paste develops a slightly dry yet chewy texture. The flavor is a balance of tang and grass with warm notes of toasted coconut.

name: Manchego 12 month DO
tagline: Raw Sheep - Mitica - La Mancha, Spain
description: The producer of this raw milk Manchego makes cheese in a small town called Daimiel located near Las Tablas national park. He has won 15 awards and counting since 2001. The rind bears the traditional basket weave design, and is rubbed with olive oil during its 9-12 months of aging. This is an exceptional cheese - it is nutty, buttery and balanced with a sweet lingering finish. It is perfect enjoyed simply with cured meats, marcona almonds and dried fruit.

name: Manchego 1605
tagline: Raw Sheep - Finca Sierra la Solana/Essex St. Cheese Co. - La Mancha, Spain
description: Named to commemorate the year in which Don Quixote was written, Manchego 1605 is truly unique. This cheese is hand-selected for importation by the Essex St. Cheese Company. The folks at Essex focus mainly on flavor profile instead of a specific aging time. In this case, the criteria is sweetness and balance, avoiding the overly salted qualities of many manchegos. The waxless rind helps the cheese to breathe, resulting in a clean, sweet aroma of hay and almonds. Flavors are rustic and sheepy to start, giving way to a pleasant, milky sweetness with hints of warm spice.

name: Manchego 4 Month DO
tagline: Raw Sheep - Mitica - La Mancha, Spain
description: The producer of this raw milk Manchego makes cheese in a small town called Daimiel located near Las Tablas national park. He has won 15 awards and counting since 2001. Aged 4 months, the rind of this young Manchego bears the same destinctive basket weave design as its 12-month counterpart. Soft, milky and sweet, it has a mellow, lingering finish. It is perfect enjoyed simply with cured meats, marcona almonds and dried fruit.

name: Ossau Iraty Fermier AOP
tagline: Raw Sheep - Fermiers Basco Bearnais - Midi-Pyrenees, France
description: The Fermiers Basco-Béarnais Cooperative was created almost 40 years ago in the Aspe Valley, in the heart of the Béarnais Pyrenees. The Cooperative brings together nearly 20 farms that are all firmly committed to a centuries-old pastoral tradition, offering a range of 100% raw milk cheeses with a long ripening process, made by hand under the control of a technician, within collective salting rooms. Ossau Iraty is a wonderful sheep's milk cheese produced in a specific area of the French Pyrenées. The name is derived from the production area that includes two neighboring provinces: the Ossau Valley, located in the Bearn; and Iraty, a forested area in the French Basque Pyrenées. Traditionally served with black cherry jam, this farmstead Ossau Iraty can be readily paired with cured meats and a wide variety of wines.

name: Pantaleo
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Latteria Sociale Santadi, Sardinia
description: Pantaleo is a unique goat’s milk cheese from Sardinia with very limited production. Aged a minimum of 100 days, it is made with milk from the Capra Sarda goat. The paste is ivory-colored with a pale rind and a sweet and clean floral finish. The off-dry texture makes it perfect to shave on salads or roasted vegetables, but its interesting flavor profile also make it perfect for a cheese plate.

name: Petit Agour Brebis
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Agour - Basque, France
description: Agour is a family owned and operated business in the heart of the Basque region of France. Petit Brebis is a pasteruized sheep's milk cheese with a smooth, creamy paste and a sweet, nutty flavor. Aromas are mild and pleasant with hints of roasted nuts. The distinctive orange rind is the result of it being rubbed with crushed espelette pepper during aging. It provides a vibrant color without affecting the flavor of the cheese.

name: Pyrenees Brebis
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Mons Fromagerie - Aquitaine, France
description: Pyrénées Brebis is an amazing cheese - but more for its subtlely than its assertiveness. Made in the forested area in the French Basque Pyrénées and aged by renowned affineur Herve Mons, this sheep's milk cheese is nutty and rich with a uniformly smooth and creamy texture. It is at once full flavored and accessible. The perfect choice for both the most adventurous and cautious of cheese lovers.

name: Ricotta Salata
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Mitica - Sardegna, Italy
description: This ricotta starts off with fresh sheep’s milk whey, which is pressed, salted and then aged to achieve its firm texture and briny taste. Similar to feta, Ricotta Salata is excellent crumbled, sliced into salads or grated over pasta. Often overlooked, this cheese is a cooking staple!

name: Tomme Brulee
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Pascal Beillevaire - Midi-Pyrenees, France
description: This is a remarkable cheese. Made in the Midi-Pyrenees region of Southwest France, it is aged by famed affineur Pascal Beillevaire. It has an impossibly smooth, creamy, golden/ivory paste with a nutty and sweet flavor. If an amazing texture and flavor wasn't enough, the rind is torched in the same way as the top of the famous dessert Creme Brulee. The result is a striking black and brown mottled rind - presentation is everything!

name: Wonderland
tagline: Raw Goat - Mountain Lodge Farm - Eatonville, WA
description: Nestled in the Cascade foothills, Mountain Lodge Farm hand-makes a variety of amazing cheeses. Wonderland, their take on a classic mountain tomme, is named for the beautiful trail that encircles Mt. Rainier. Made with raw goat's milk, Wonderland is rich, nutty, floral, and fruity. Its texture is firm but yielding with an eggshell colored paste. Perfect for snacking with salame and olives, it's also firm enough to shave on a salad or grate over roasted vegetables.

name: Alfred le Fermier - 2025 ACS Best in Show!
tagline: Raw Cow - Fromagerie la Station - Quebec, Canada
description: Fromagerie la Station’s journey to award-winning cheesemaking began with Alfred and Aglaé Bolduc’s 1928 arrival to the town of Compton in Québec province. Four generations later, the Bolduc family is still working the same land, now making farmstead organic cheeses and harvesting maple syrup. Best in Show winner at the American Cheese Society’s 2025 competition, Alfred le Fermier has a sunset yellow rind and a woodsy aroma. Alfred’s notes of floral honey, fruit, and hazelnut as well as its yielding texture make it ideal for melting, slicing onto sandwiches, or snacking.

name: Raclette de Compton au Poivre - 2024 ACS Best in Show!
tagline: Raw Cow - Fromagerie la Station - Quebec, Canada
description: Fromagerie la Station’s journey to award-winning cheesemaking began with Alfred and Aglaé Bolduc’s 1928 arrival to the town of Compton in Québec province. Four generations later, the Bolduc family is still working the same land, now making farmstead organic cheeses and harvesting maple syrup. Best in Show winner at the American Cheese Society’s 2024 competition, Raclette de Compton au Poivre has a copper-colored washed rind, a supple golden paste, and a line of pink peppercorns running through the center of the cheese. The aromas of apple, chestnut, and butter open even more when heated. Perfect for melting over boiled potatoes, crusty bread, cornichons, and cured meats!

name: Staff Pick - Cow's Milk
tagline: You choose the texture & the flavor, we'll choose the cheese!
description: If you are reading this, you like cow's milk cheese. Well, we do too! Here's all you do: just choose the texture, flavor & the amount and we'll do the rest! Based on your answers, we'll choose a cheese that we love and that fits your criteria - couldn't be easier! It's just like standing in front of the cheese case!
