name: Morbier AOP
tagline: Raw Cow - Jean Perrin - Cleron, France
description: Welcome back, Morbier! After a 9-year absence from the US, we are delighted to have authentic Morbier back in our case. This legendary cheese from the Jura mountains dates back to the late nineteenth century. Farmers would typically deliver their milk to the village cheese dairy to make Comte. However, in the winter when travel was more difficult and cows produce less milk, they would make their own smaller-format cheese on the farm. The curd made from the morning milking would be dusted in a layer of ash to protect it until finishing the process with curd from the following morning. These days Morbier’s distinctive line of ash through the center is more for tradition than anything else. This supple cheese delivers notes of yogurt, caramel, and fruit, developing roasted, spicy, and vegetal nuances as it ages. Morbier is a striking addition to a cheese board and it also melts wonderfully. Try using it as raclette or in the gratin known as morbiflette, a variation of tartiflette.

name: Shadow Blossom
tagline: Raw Cow - Hofkaserei Kraus/Restaurant Schattbuch - Allgau, Germany
description: Shadow Blossom is a product of the mutual admiration between cheesemaker Albert Kraus and Michelin starred Restaurant Schattbuch. After a lot of "talking shop" together during a few dinners, they came up with this cheese. Starting from a traditional Allgäu semi-hard cheese, they coat the rind with Wild Madagascar pepper, Long Pepper, tailed pepper, kampot pepper, pink berries and cardamom. Pleasantly soft and crunchy in texture, creamy and buttery in taste, with the kick and complex flavors of six different pepper varieties!

name: Le Cousin
tagline: Raw Cow - Schmidhauser - Haute Savoie, France
description: Family first they say...this cheese is true to the mantra. A border-crossing cheese, named Le Cousin after the cousin, Jurg, whose dairy produces this wonderful alpine cheese before it is moved to the Haute Savoie dairy (France) where it is aged 6 more months. A semi-firm, fruity cheese with a sweetly salty tang, it is great for melting a fondue or grilled cheese! Fun Fact: The paper label that is placed on every finished wheel has both cousins adorned in the their respective Swiss or French garb. Great outfits, great cheese!

name: OG Kristal
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Van Tricht - Roeselare, Belgium
description: This assertive Belgian gouda is a must-try cheese for any lover of tyrosine crystals. What are those? Glad you asked…they are the crunchy, salty, savory bits of amino acid that form in aged cheeses as the protein structure of the milk breaks down. Yes, those! Chances are you have enjoyed them before! Like many aged goudas, the base flavor of OG Kristal leans sweeter, with notes of boozy cherries and butterscotch. The crystallized texture provides a savory balance to the fruity, nutty sweetness.

name: Brabander
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Fromagerie L'Amuse/Essex St. Cheese Co. - Netherlands
description: Goat cheese meets aged gouda. Brabander embodies the most beloved qualities of both. Made from the milk of the Saanen goats in the Brabant region of southern Holland, Brabander is aged for six months by famed affineur Betty Koster at Fromagerie L'Amuse. Its porcelain-colored paste is buttery and creamy with a lasting finish of sweet caramel.

name: Challerhocker
tagline: Raw Cow - Käserei Tufertschwil/Chas & Co. - Lütisburg, Switzerland
description: Pronunciation: "hollar hocker." Translation: "sitting in the cellar." Originally an Appenzeller maker, Walter Rass began experimenting and fine-tuning recipes to create this remarkable cheese - the result is truly special. It is washed in wine and spices and aged for a minimum of 10 months. Deep in flavor with a slight fruitiness, it is firm yet creamy, with notes of roasted nuts and butterscotch.

name: Comte - Aged 24 Months
tagline: Raw Cow - Fromageries Vagne - Franche-Comte, France
description: This Comté is made using summer milk from the iconic French dairy cow breed Montbéliarde and then aged for two years by traditional cheesemakers in Eastern France. The end result is all the nutty flavors of Alpine cheeses that you love but kicked up a notch with a sublte fruitiness and a slight, yeasty sweetness. The longer aging process results in a scattering of tyrosine throughout the paste of this cheese - those crunchy crystals that make a cheese addictively snackable. This makes an excellent addition to fondue but is also delicious to munch on in it's pure form. Pair this with green apples, green grapes, or skip the fruit and pour yourself a glass of crisp, white wine!

name: Comte, aged 5-7 months
tagline: Raw Cow - Fromageries Vagne - Franche-Comte, France
description: Comte is unquestionably one of our favorite and most versatile cheeses on the planet. With layers and layers of flavors, it can be enjoyed when young or aged. Aged between 5-7 months, this version is a pliable, nutty, fruity comte with great melting properties. Perfect for everything from snacking to sandwiches to fondue.

name: Fontina Val d'Aosta
tagline: Raw Cow - Fromagerie Haut Val'Ayas - Piedmont, Italy
description: Often imitated, never duplicated - Fontina Val d'Aosta is the original Italian fontina. It is semi-firm & creamy, with a washed rind that imparts a mildly pungent aroma. Flavors are rich and nutty with a subtle hint of fruit and grass. One of the world's greatest melting cheeses, it is the centerpiece to Piedmont's famous fonduta - a silky blend of Fontina val D'Aosta, cream, eggs, and shaved white truffle. Also fantastic on a sandwich with prosciutto, or added to mozzarella on a pizza.

name: Gruyere 1655
tagline: Raw Cow - Fromagerie le Cret - Fribourg, Switzerland
description: Master Cheesemaker Jean-Marie Dunand runs the village dairy at 3,000 ft above sea level in the heartland of traditional Gruyère production in the Fribourg region of Switzerland. The dairy, which dates back to 1900, has been run by Dunand since 1986. He makes 18-20 wheels of Gruyère each day, 365 days a year, using freshly delivered milk from eight small local farms. After three months, the wheels are moved to the caves of Fromage Gruyère, where they are finished aging for the next 9 months before release. Each wheel is rigorously evaluated by an expert team before earning the 1655 label. The result is a cheese that is perfectly balanced. Sweet, salty, nutty, fruity, mushroomy and earthy.

name: Gruyere AOP Classic
tagline: Raw Cow - Le Superbe - Fribourg, Switzerland
description: Produced since 1115 in the area surrounding the little village of Gruyère in western Switzerland, this much-loved cheese is still made in local dairies according to the original traditional recipe. With its buttery, caramel flavor and ultra-creamy texture, it is one of the most popular cheeses in our case. Aged about 6 months, it is suitable for your cheese board, but also incredibly versatile in the kitchen. One of the world's great melting cheeses, it is perfect for fondue, quiche or grilled sandwiches.

name: L'Amuse Gouda
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Cono/Fromagerie L'Amuse/Essex St. Cheese Co. - Netherlands
description: L’Amuse Signature Gouda is the product of a close collaboration between several gouda producers, mainly Cono and Lutjewinkel, in the Beemster and Schermer region and Betty Koster, owner of L’Amuse cheese store, near Amsterdam in the Netherlands. Wheels are carefully graded and selected before being transferred to a warehouse where they are tended and matured at the cellars for up to 30 months before being released and sold. Koster matures these goudas at higher temperatures (51-54 F) and humidity levels higher than normal which allows the crystals to form while preserving the moist, buttery paste and nutty flavor. Bright orange in color with a thick wax rind, L'Amuse Gouda is hard and dense with flavors of butterscotch, caramel and hazelnuts.

name: Schnebelhorn
tagline: Raw Cow - Reto Guntensperger & Kaserei Butschwil - Saint Gallen, Switzerland
description: Schnebelhorn is made with raw milk which comes from Swiss Brown / Braunvieh cows. Its creator, Reto Güntensperger, is a third-generation cheesemaker in the canton of St. Gallen. His grandfather made Appenzeller, his father made Appenzeller, but Reto wants to branch out. When the Swiss Cheese Union collapsed in 1999, he had his chance. Cream enriched & aged for 8 months, it has aromas of toasted hazelnuts, brown butter & roasted onions. The paste is firm & pale gold, with flecks of crystals & a creamy finish.

name: Smoked Gouda
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Cheeseland - Netherlands
description: This mild and creamy gouda is produced in Northern Holland. It then travels to the USA to be slowly smoked over smoldering oakwood chips. The final product is velvety and silky with a dark, smoky rind. The paste maintains the rich creaminess of Gouda, but with subtle smoky undertones. For some reason, smoked gouda always makes us think of hiking and camping. It's fantastic with cooked and cured meats, on sandwiches or even as a burger topping.

name: Supreme des Alpes Signature
tagline: Thermised Cow - Moleson Signature - Friboug, Switzerland
description: Suprême des Alpes (supreme of the Alps) is a Swiss cheese made in the same style as Gruyère and Vacherin Fribourgeois. Made in copper cauldrons, Suprême des Alpes is the result of a collaboration between Fromi’s Master Cheesemaker and the Fromagerie Moléson. Under the rustic natural rind, the cheese is smooth, dense and compact with some small tyrosine crystals forming over the 12-month maturation. The interior has a sweet-savory aroma with hints of tropical fruit and broth, and a rich flavor of roasted nuts, sweet cream and alpine herbs. Perfect on its own or as a welcome addition to fondue!

name: Twisca
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Treur Kaas - Winkel, Netherlands
description: Twisca is a delicious and flavorful sheep milk gouda made in North Holland. This cheese owes its full, creamy taste to the meadows where the sheep are free to graze. The salty, wetland environment makes the grass in these meadows richer and the milk (and cheese made with that milk) much more complex. Twisca offers a savory nuttiness, balanced by a smooth texture. Delicious and infinitely pairable, it's a crowd pleaser that's sure to delight even the pickiest eater!

tagline: You choose the texture & the flavor, we'll choose the cheese!

name: Persille de Rambouillet
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Ferme de la Tremblaye - Ile-de-France, France
description: This unbelievably smooth ash-coated goat milk blue comes from La Tremblaye dairy, located in the countryside surrounding Paris. Persille de Rambouillet gets its name from its “parsley-veined” interior—persille—and the Rambouillet forest adjacent to the dairy’s picturesque farmland. With a supple texture and notes of white pepper and sweet cream, this blue is, well...amazing. Huge staff favorite!

name: Stichelton
tagline: Raw Cow - Joe Schneider - Nottinghamshire, UK
description: The other King of Blues, Stichelton is Stilton’s raw-milk cousin. Joe Schneider and Neal’s Yard Dairy Founding Director Randolph Hodgeson set out to make a raw-milk Stilton after 18 years of extinction. Since 2006, it has been handmade at Stichelton Dairy in Nottinghamshire. Ladled by hand, the range of flavors this soft, creamy raw milk blue can exhibit is extraordinary – from crisp, green apples to beef stock. We don’t have Stichelton all the time. When we do, you shouldn’t miss it!

name: Bayley Hazen Blue
tagline: Raw Cow - Jasper Hill Creamery - Greensboro, VT
description: DeLaurenti is proud to carry some of Jasper Hill's finest cheeses. Bayley Hazen is a favorite of both customers and staff alike. Initially assertive, Bayley Hazen finishes with soft, sweet and grassy flavors. It's perfect for topping a burger or crumbling onto a salad. Also great paired with green apples and a glass of port.

name: Bleu d'Auvergne
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Terre des Volcans - Auvergne, France
description: Sometimes referred to as the cow's milk version of Roquefort, Bleu d'Auvergne is much creamier and more approachable. Rather buttery with a subtle, earthy grassiness, this blue is assertive enough for your cheese board, but also perfect as a recipe ingredient. Great for everything from making steak butter to stuffing dates.

name: Bleu des Causses
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Mons Fromagerie - Midi-Pyrenees, France
description: This lesser known cousin to Roquefort is made with 100% raw cow's milk, and was originally a less expensive alternative for those who couldn't afford the highly prized King of French Blues. It is assertive and full flavored, but remains approachable. Another Herve Mons triumph. With hints of grass and earth, it is an interesting blue that is perfect when you feel like trying something new. Fantastic with any wines from the Languedoc in Southern France.

name: Blu Di Cuneo
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Caseificio Rabbia - Piedmont, Italy
description:
The result of a collective effort of a recently formed association of traditional cheesemakers from the Cuneo area, this spoonable blue is bursting with mouthwatering flavors. Each producer involved crafts this enticing blue cheese that is typical of the area according to traditional recipes and methods, to preserve and recognize this local cheese officially. Blu di Cuneo is similar in consistency to its neighboring blue somewhere between a gorgonzola dolce and gorgonzola cremificato, but inoculated with the penicillium roqueforti mold for a distinct difference in flavor from the former: rich and sweet notes of cultured cream intermingle with more savory mineral notes with a bit of brine on the finish, delivered in a compellingly creamy and pudding like paste sure to please most palates.

Caseificio Rabbia is dedicated to preserving the local traditional cheeses that are integral ingredients in the Piedmontese cuisine. They are located in Raffia near Cuneo - at the foothills of the Alps where they also have a special maturation cave that provides the perfect environment to capture the unique microbial character of the region. These flora in turn, populate on the cheese’s natural rinds, and ultimately aid in cultivating the resulting flavors in the finished cheese. These understated flavors are expressive of the native environment and lend a depth and unique character to this otherwise deceptively subtle class of cheeses. Currently in their 5th generation, the Rabbia family is dedicated to producing raw milk cheese, made from local herds within 1 kilometer of their facility. The resulting tomas are soothing, subtle and extremely snackable.

name: Chevretta Blauw
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Treur Kaas - Winkel, Netherlands
description: Chevretta Blauw is a farmstead goat’s milk gouda with blue mold. While that may sound like a divisive cheese, trust us on this one. The cheese has a delicately creamy texture thanks to the high quality milk and added cream. The lightly caramelized sweetness characteristic of a goat gouda balances perfectly with the minerality of the blue mold. Grab a wedge and see why our staff has so quickly fallen for this cheese!

name: Fourme d'Ambert
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Terre des Volcans - Auvergne, France
description: One of France's oldest cheeses, the production of Fourme d'Ambert dates back to Roman times. Named for its tall and narrow cylindrical shape, it is customarily cut into disks rather than wedges. This makes an eye-catching addition to any cheese platter. It is earthy and mushroomy, with a dense creamy texture. Perfect on a burger, with dried fruit, honey, or a glass of port.

name: Glacier Blue
tagline: Raw Cow - Cascadia Creamery - Trout Lake, WA
description: Cascadia Creamery is committed to sustainable and humane practices and has been certified organic for decades - they also happen to make really great cheese. Their cows graze happily on the meadow grasses enriched by the volcanic soil of Mt. Adams. Glacier Blue is rich, dense and approachable, making it a great blue for all occasions. Perfect on everything from a cheese plate to a burger to a salad. Even suitable for dessert with honey and candied nuts.

name: Gorgonzola Piccante
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Formaggi Ciresa - Lombardy, Italy
description: Slightly more aged and firm than its sweeter counterpart, Gorgonzola Piccante is densely creamy. The paste is light yellow with widespread blue and green marbling. With a robust and sharp flavor, this is perfect for crumbling on top (or inside) a burger. Its creamy texture is also suitable for melting into a sauce, or using as part of your filling for ravioli. Great with roasted walnuts, honey and bright fruits for dessert.

name: Mitibleu
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Mitica - Castilla la Mancha, Spain
description: Mitibleu is a rare sheep’s milk blue from Spain that was originally designed to rival the famous French blue, Roquefort. This cheese is produced in a dairy near the medieval city of Toledo, in the heart of Manchego country. The milk used comes from the plentiful sheep that graze on the plains of La Mancha. Mitibleu is aged 4 months, with a bold and spicy flavor. Although full of flavor, it packs less bite than its French inspiration.

name: Roquefort
tagline: Raw Sheep - Gabriel Coulet - Aveyron, France
description: Roquefort is the undisputed King of French Blues. Roquefort starts with baking loaves of rye. After aging for a few weeks, this bread will yield an entire year's supply of penicillium roqueforti, the mold used to inoculate the cheese curds. This mold, combined with raw sheep's milk, give Roquefort its unique character. Could it get better? Well...this one is aged by famed French affineur Herver Mons as well! Aromas are powerful, with notes of bread and yeast. The texture is crumbly yet creamy, with a taste that is at once pleasantly salty, sweet, briny and piquant. Roquefort is amazing on its own, on a salad, or with a glass of Sauternes.

name: Saint Agur
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Fromagerie de Chaumes - Auvergne, France
description: Looking for a crowd-pleasing blue? There's a reason we sell a lot of this pasteurized cow's milk cheese from France's volcanic central Auvergne region. Saint Agur is an irresistibly buttery double-cream cheese threaded with spicy blue veins. The texture is soft, creamy & spreadable with a pale cream-colored paste. Not only is it perfect for a cheese board, its ultra-creamy texture makes it excellent to incorporate into salad dressings & sauces for grilled steak.

name: Stilton
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Colston Bassett/Neal's Yard Dairy - Nottinghamshire, England
description: Founded in 1913, and still one of the smallest Stilton dairies in the UK, Colston Bassett uses more traditional methods than most other Stilton producers. The curd is still hand-ladled before draining, which preserves its structure, resulting in a luscious, creamy texture when the cheeses are mature. The rind is a mottled orange-brown with patches of natural white mold. Flavors are rich and lactic with a wonderful balance of blue mold, earth and butter. In the end, you will not enjoy a more fantastic blue cheese. Enjoy as is, use it to top your favorite steak hot off the grill, or enjoy it with candied nuts and a glass of port for dessert.

name: Brebirousse d'Argental
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Fromi - Rhone-Alpes, France
description: Mild. Creamy. Buttery. Rich. Any questions? Brebirousse d'Argental is one of those cheeses that you can't help but love. In fact, if you say you don't, one might either question your honesty, or wonder if you were describing a different cheese. Essentially it is a sheep's milk brie with a more ultra-silky texture and a mild sweetness. Add the striking orange rind and all you are lacking is a crusty loaf of bread and a glass of wine!

name: Fresh Ricotta
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Calabro Cheese Co. - East Haven, CT
description: Calabro ricotta is a special cheese. The texture is impossibly light, fluffy and creamy. Flavors are milky, buttery & sweet. Once you try it, it will be impossible to go back to the generic tubs you find at your local grocery store. The curd is still hand-dipped and hand-packed into Calabro’s instantly recognizable metal containers that are pierced with tiny holes to allow the whey to drain, even after the cheese is shipped. Delicious when enjoyed as is, it is also an essential ingredient for your ravioli, lasagna and cannoli filling. If that's not all, it is also great for baking, or drizzling with honey for an amazing dessert.

name: Perail de Brebis
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Fromagerie a Millau/Papillon - Aveyron, France - 3.5oz
description: Made in Aveyron in the Midi-Pyrenees region of southern France, Perail de Brebis is a soft ripened sheep's milk cheese with a thin and velvety rind and a dense, creamy texture. It has faint aromas of hay and earth, but is mild and sweet enough to appeal to a wide audience. When allowed to reach room temperature, it will become extremely soft and runny - perfect for spooning onto a crusty loaf of bread. Enjoy with a crisp white or rosé from southern France.

name: Primo Pascolo
tagline: Raw Cow - Caseificio Rabbia - Piedmont, Italy
description:
Primo Pascolo, which translates to “first pasture,” is an ode to Spring in Piedmont. The cheese’s lively aromatics capture the succulent smells of a spring meadow. This raw cow’s milk, natural rind cheese is delicately tangy and vegetal, finishing with subtle yet complex hints of buttered popcorn and clover honey. The cheese’s signature springy texture is divinely doughy and fun to eat. Primo Pascolo is great all on its own as a table cheese for snacking but is also an amazing ingredient melted into risotto or creamy pasta to kick up the umami.

Caseificio Rabbia is dedicated to preserving the local traditional cheeses that are integral ingredients in the Piedmontese cuisine. They are located in Raffia near Cuneo - at the foothills of the Alps where they also have a special maturation cave that provides the perfect environment to capture the unique microbial character of the region. These flora in turn, populate on the cheese’s natural rinds, and ultimately aid in cultivating the resulting flavors in the finished cheese. These understated flavors are expressive of the native environment and lend a depth and unique character to this otherwise deceptively subtle class of cheeses. Currently in their 5th generation, the Rabbia family is dedicated to producing raw milk cheese, made from local herds within 1 kilometer of their facility. The resulting tomas are soothing, subtle and extremely snackable.

name: Brie de Jouvence
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Ferme de la Tremblaye - Ile-de-France, France
description: Brie de Jouvence is the closest thing to traditional raw milk French brie. Low temperature pasteurization, the highest quality milk, and traditional Norman methods of production result in a flavor profile that is akin to the original - full flavored, creamy, grassy, lactic, and rich.

name: Camembert
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Le Pommier/Mons Fromagerie - Normandy, France - 9oz
description: This is the closest thing to traditional French camembert that you'll find in the US. Ripened by master affineur Herve Mons, the paste is deeply golden, supple and yielding. Flavors are earthy and buttery with pleasant aromas of mushroom and truffle. Enjoy at room temperature with a crusty baguette, slice and serve atop a fresh salad, or sprinkle with chopped garlic and fresh herbs and bake until warm and molten.

name: Carboncino
tagline: Pasteurized Cow, Goat & Sheep - Caseificio dell'Alta Langa - Piedmont - 5oz
description: This lovely Italian cheese hails from the agricultural heart of Piemonte. The name comes from the dusting of charcoal gray ash that covers the soft, silky white interior. Made from a blend of cow, goat, and sheep milk, each of which adds delicate nuances of flavor to the cheese. The texture is light and spongy.

name: Delice de Bourgogne
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Fromagerie Lincet - Burgundy, France
description: From the Burgundy region in France, Delice de Bourgogne is made with cow's milk that has been enriched with crème fraiche. The result is a decadent, full-flavored, but mellow cheese with a smooth, melt-in-the-mouth texture. It has a wonderful mushroomy aroma, with a pleasantly tangy finish. Nearly impossible to resist, it pairs perfectly with Champagne and fresh berries.

name: Fromage d'Affinois
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Fromagerie Guilloteau - Rhône-Alps, France
description: Don't know what kind of cheese your guests like? Choose Fromage d'Affinois. This soft-ripened double crème is lush, decadent and silky. With just a faint aroma of mushrooms on the rind, the mild & buttery flavors will please the crowd without being boring.

name: Moses Sleeper
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Jasper Hill Creamery - Greensboro, VT
description: Moses Sleeper is made with pasteurized cow's milk by Jasper Hill Farm in Vermont. Named after a historic local pioneer scout, this cheese is akin to a more mild version of Reblochon. The flavor is approachable and savory with hints of fresh milk, hay, toasted nuts and butter. Beneath the thin, bloomy rind, the interior paste is ivory white in color with a semi-soft, gooey texture. Pairs well with a crisp apple, cured meats, and a crusty baguette.

name: Bocconcino di Langa
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Caseificio della'Alta Langa - Piedmont, Italy - 4oz
description: Meaning "little mouthful," Bocconcino is made with goat's milk that has been enriched with cream. It has a thin, soft, edible rind and a smooth ivory paste. Flavors include notes of tangy, fresh cream and subtle hints of grass. Enjoy with crusty bread at room temperature.

name: St. Stephen, 8oz
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Four Fat Fowl - Stephentown, NY
description: Four Fat Fowl is the cheesemaking project dreamed up by a self-proclaimed family of maniacal cheese lovers. Their commitment to making locally-sourced, handcrafted cheeses began when they turned their Sunday dinner table discussions into reality in 2013. Through careful crafting, they make cheeses that showcase the bounty of the Hudson Valley and please palates far and wide. It seemed only fitting that their name should be locally-sourced as well. Stephentown, NY has a rich history going back to the colonial era. In the seventeenth century, the Dutch colonized the Hudson Valley and established a system of landholding called patroonship. The patroon acted as the landlord to tenants who rented land to live on and farm. Stephentown was named after Stephen Van Rensselaer, the last patroon of the patroonship that now comprises Rensselaer County. His tenants called him the “Good Patroon” because he was lenient in collecting rent, which included a day’s labor, ten to twenty bushels of wheat per hundred acres, and “four fat fowl.” St. Stephen, their award-winning flagship cheese, is a handcrafted triple cream that bursts with buttery and milky overtones. This cheese boasts a smooth, silky interior made from fresh, all natural jersey cow milk and cream. A bloomy rind adds an earthy flavor with nutty undertones. St. Stephen will leave you wanting more to share with a friend and a glass of bubbly!

name: Tentation de Saint-Felicien, 6oz
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - La Fromagerie l'Etoile - Rhone-Alps, France
description: Produced in the Rhône-Alpes by La Fromagerie l’Etoile, makers of St Marcellin and St Felicien, Tentation came about as a way to use surplus cream, by adding it to the milk before making the cheese. Once ripe, the cheese becomes soft and gloriously runny. Delightfully rich and creamy, it is almost obligatory that Tentation be scooped up with a crusty baguette.

name: Drunk Monk
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Johan Deweer - Belgium
description: Third-generation Belgian cheesemaker Johan Deweer was born into a farming and dairy family. He spent his childhood absorbing everything he could along the way, immersing himself in the family business, which included both raising livestock and growing crops. What makes this cheese special is the producer’s partnership with Kaasaffineurs Van Tricht to use a special beer wash for the ripening rind, Rex, a Belgian blonde ale with Cascade hops created by Van Tricht and organic Belgian brewer, Brouwerij Anders. The resulting Trappist monk-style cheese is made from pasteurized milk from Holstein and Brown Swiss cows and vegetarian rennet. Aged for five to seven weeks, it is semisoft, silky, and sweet like freshly churned butter or heavy cream. It has brioche-like yeasty notes from the Belgian blonde ale wash, a sweet creaminess, and a fudgy, gooey, and pliable texture. Great with everything from a cheese board to burgers to fondue!

name: Brillat Savarin
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Fromagerie Delin - France
description: Named for the French gastronome Brillat Savarin who famously said "tell me what you eat and I'll tell you what you are." Well...if you eat this cheese, suffice to say you are really awesome. A triple creme, meaning it has a minimum of 75% butterfat, Brillat Savarin is as decadent as cheeses come. Rich? Yes. Heavy? Nope. Impossibly smooth and creamy, it is enrobed with a pillowy soft, edible cotton rind. The cheese literally cries out for Champagne! Bubbles required!

name: Belgioso Burrata
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - BelGioioso - Green Bay, WI - 8oz
description: Traditionally from Puglia in southern Italy, this is one of the freshest of all cow's milk cheeses. Milky, sweet, fresh mozzarella on the outside, with molten ribbons of curd and cream on the inside. Each 8oz package contains two 4oz pieces of burrata packed in water for optimum storage. Drizzle with olive oil and a pinch of sea salt and serve with crusty bread. You can work up from there by adding any of the following: grilled bread, prosciutto, salame, sliced tomatoes, fresh herbs, grilled vegetables, aged balsamic or sauteed rapini.

name: Buf Buffalo Burrata
tagline: Pasteurized Buffalo - Buf Creamery - El Rosal, Columbia - 8oz
description: Imported from the Columbia...yes, that's right, Columbia. Trust us, if it wasn't really good, we wouldn't be selling it. You love burrata, we know this. You also love mozzarella di bufula. Well, time for these two to meet. Buf's Burrata di Bufula combines two great things - the bright, tangy of buffalo milk and the molten texture of fresh burrata. Each package contains one, 8oz piece of fresh burrata di bufala packed in water for optimum storage.

name: Buf Mozzarella di Bufala
tagline: Pasteurized Buffalo - Buf - El Rosal, Columbia - 8oz
description: Imported from the Columbia...yes, that's right, Columbia. Trust us, if it wasn't really good, we wouldn't be selling it. Mozzarella di Bufala is wonderfully fresh and delicate with a pleasant tang. This is the perfect cheese to use on your Pizza Margherita, in a salad or with other classic Italian recipes. Each package contains one, 8oz piece of fresh mozzarella packed in water for optimum storage. Voted the #1 Mozzarella in 2016 by the American Cheese Society.

name: Epoisses
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Fromagerie Berthaut - Burgundy, France
description: After having been almost completely out of production during both World Wars, Epoisses was resurrected in the 1950s. The signature rind is washed with brine and Marc de Bourgogne (the local pomace brandy) and can range in color from light orange to nearly brick red. It has an intense and pungent aroma, with more subtle flavors of bacon and custard. No need for cheese knives or a cutting board - just spoon the creamy paste onto a crusty French baguette and enjoy with any wine from Burgundy.

name: Florette
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Fromagerie Guilloteau - Rhone-Alps, France
description: Love brie but in the mood for something a bit less barnyard and a bit more bright? Look no further. Florette combines the creamy, lush texture of it's cow's milk cousin with the bright piquancy of goat cheese. Ivory white in color with a ultra-creamy, spreadable texture, this cheese is a perfect gateway goat.

name: Fresh Mozzarella
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Grande Cheese Co. - Brownsville, WI
description: Originally made using water buffalo's milk, the cow's milk version is perfect for your Caprese Salad or Pizza Margherita. Slice into medallions and drizzle with olive oil and a pinch of sea salt for a simple, but satisfying appetizer. Four rounds to a pound, each piece is packed in a little water for freshness. Feel free to add a little tap water for storage. Before using it on pizza, drain the water and let the cheese rest in the fridge for an hour. Pour off excess water (this would have wound up in the middle of your pizza), use and enjoy!

name: Gina Marie Cream Cheese
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Sierra Nevada Cheese Co. - Willows, CA
description: Gina Marie is the original natural cream cheese. With all due respect to the mass produced cream cheese that you find at your local grocery store, there really is no comparison. Made using only milk, cream, and salt, this cheese is void of any fillers, stabilizers, and gums. Light and fluffy in texture, fresh and creamy in flavor, use it liberally whenever you have a craving for cream cheese.

name: Harbison Mini
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Jasper Hill Farm - Greensboro, VT
description: Harbison is named for Anne Harbison, affectionately known as the grandmother of Greensboro, VT. Harbison is a soft-ripened cheese with a rustic, bloomy rind, made by Jasper Hill Farm. Young cheeses are wrapped in strips of spruce cambium, the tree's inner bark layer, harvested from the farm's woodlands. Harbison is woodsy and sweet, balanced with lemon, mustard, and vegetal flavors. Before enjoying, be sure to bring it up to room temperature - then you can spoon the interior paste onto a crusty baguette!

name: L'Affine au Chablis, 200g
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - La Formagerie Germain - Burgundy, France
description: A true regional speciality, l'Affiné au Chablis Germain cheese is made from pasteurized cow's milk. Its lightly gold-tinged rind reveals a meltingly soft and creamy center. It gets its distinct flavor and characteristic color from its wash with Chablis wine. It has a lush, creamy texture with flavors that are mild with a fresh, floral and fruity aroma.

name: La Tur
tagline: Pasteurized Cow, Goat & Sheep - Caseificio dell'Alta Langa - Piedmont, Italy - 8oz
description: Made by Caseificio dell'Alta Langa near the town of Alba in northern Italy, La Tur is a dense and creamy blend of cow, sheep, and goat's milk. The rind is soft, wrinkled, thin and delicate. The interior paste is ivory in color with a light, fluffy, mousse-like texture, becoming extremely soft and creamy under the rind. Flavors are rich and sweet with a subtle tang. Due to its fragility, it is encased in a cupcake-like wrapper and placed in a protective plastic container. When ripe, the molten creamline commonly sticks to the paper as it is removed. The cheese that ends up on the paper will taste as good as the cheese that ends up on your cheeseboard!

name: Langres
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Fromagerie Germain - Champagne-Ardenne, France
description: Langres is a French cow's milk cheese that originated from the plateau of Langres in the region of the Champagne Ardenne. Successive washings during aging result in a beautiful orange hue and a pungent, intense aroma. The flavor, however, is much more mellow and approachable. Combine these characteristics with a super dense, creamy texture and a glass of Champagne and you will be very happy.

name: Le Secret des Lys
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Jean Perrin - Franche Comte, France
description: Remember St. Marcellin? We do too. Due to forces beyond our control, it's not available to us anymore. Queue Secret des Lys. It has all the same qualities - rich, molten, spoonable & a free crock! The more you buy, the more ramikens you will have for olives & pits, too! Let it come to room temperature, or even gently heat it in the oven before serving! Instant fondue!

name: Mt. Tam, 7oz
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Cowgirl Creamery - Petaluma, CA - 8oz
description: Named after the 4,000 ft. Mt Tamalpais that lies at the southern end of Marin County, Mt. Tam is a triple cream cheese made using local organic milk with the addition of cream. This bloomy rind cheese is silky smooth, creamy and extremely rich. Buttery and mellow with a faint aroma of mushrooms, it has wide appeal without a shortage of character.

name: Nocciolo
tagline: Pasteurized Cow/Goat/Sheep - Caseificio dell'Alta Langa - Piedmont, Italy
description: Il Nocciola, meaning hazelnut in Italian, is a beautiful cow/goat/sheep combo from Northern Italy's Piedmont region. It is sweet, buttery, bright & impossibly creamy. Despite it's diminutive stature, it brings maximum impact. It's hard to find anyone who doesn't love this cheese, especially when you hand them a glass of bubbly to go with it!

name: Saint-Nectaire Laitier AOP
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Xavier David - Auvergne, France
description: Saint-Nectaire has been made in the Auvergne region of France since at least the 17th century. This cheese is aged traditionally on rye straw for at least 4 weeks in damp volcanic cellars in the town of Allanche. Affineurs wash the cheese with a salt water brine during maturation and turn the cheese over on a regular basis to achieve its characteristic orange and grey rind. Known for its creamy, unctuous paste and hazelnut flavor, Saint-Nectaire pairs easily with charcuterie and a crusty baguette and melts beautifully into recipes!

name: Sawtooth
tagline: Row Cow - Cascadia Creamery - Trout Lake, WA
description: Made by the Cascadia Creamery in Trout Lake, WA. Named for the nearby Sawtooth Huckleberry Fields on the shoulder of Mt. Adams where Native Americans have picked berries for thousands of years. This semi-soft, washed rind cheese has a fudgy, smooth texture and a complex, peaty flavor with notes of freshly pickled walnuts and honeycomb.

name: Taleggio
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Delitia - Lombardy, Italy
description: Taleggio is a cheese whose origin dates back to the 10th century. Production takes place in the Val Taleggio region of northern Italy, from which its name is derived. Its pungent, washed-rind aroma belies its more mild, buttery and mushroomy flavor. The texture is creamy, rich and spreadable, becoming increasingly softer as the cheese ages. Taleggio's creamy texture makes it perfect to fold into risotto, pasta and sauces, but there is perhaps no better way to enjoy it than with the end of a fresh baguette.

name: Vacherousse d'Argental
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Fromi - Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes, France
description: Vacherousse d'Argental is a soft cow's milk cheese. The cheese is washed with annatto to create its distinctive orange-red color and then aged for two weeks to allow its white mold rind to develop. This decadent double creme cheese is buttery and delicate. Serve with crusty bread and slices of crisp apple. Sure to be a crowd pleaser!

name: Staff Pick - Cow's Milk
tagline: You choose the texture & the flavor, we'll choose the cheese!
description: If you are reading this, you like cow's milk cheese. Well, we do too! Here's all you do: just choose the texture, flavor & the amount and we'll do the rest! Based on your answers, we'll choose a cheese that we love and that fits your criteria - couldn't be easier! It's just like standing in front of the cheese case! Feel free to add any specifics in the Instructions/Additions field at checkout. The published price per lb is only a place holder - the exact price of the cheese will be determined by the amount selected and the actual price per lb.

name: Morbier AOP
tagline: Raw Cow - Jean Perrin - Cleron, France
description: Welcome back, Morbier! After a 9-year absence from the US, we are delighted to have authentic Morbier back in our case. This legendary cheese from the Jura mountains dates back to the late nineteenth century. Farmers would typically deliver their milk to the village cheese dairy to make Comte. However, in the winter when travel was more difficult and cows produce less milk, they would make their own smaller-format cheese on the farm. The curd made from the morning milking would be dusted in a layer of ash to protect it until finishing the process with curd from the following morning. These days Morbier’s distinctive line of ash through the center is more for tradition than anything else. This supple cheese delivers notes of yogurt, caramel, and fruit, developing roasted, spicy, and vegetal nuances as it ages. Morbier is a striking addition to a cheese board and it also melts wonderfully. Try using it as raclette or in the gratin known as morbiflette, a variation of tartiflette.

name: Brandenettle
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Gesneden Kaas - Netherlands
description: Walking through the woods, you want to avoid nettles, not so with Brandenettle. Nettle cheese is a Dutch specialty: the tops of nettles are used to give the cheese a fresh edge. Strange? A little, but trust us, this cheese is really good. Admittedly, we are usually skeptical of flavored cheeses, but this one is different. It's subtle herbaceousness & creamy texture make a crowd pleaser that is great on sandwiches!

name: Drunk Monk
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Johan Deweer - Belgium
description: Third-generation Belgian cheesemaker Johan Deweer was born into a farming and dairy family. He spent his childhood absorbing everything he could along the way, immersing himself in the family business, which included both raising livestock and growing crops. What makes this cheese special is the producer’s partnership with Kaasaffineurs Van Tricht to use a special beer wash for the ripening rind, Rex, a Belgian blonde ale with Cascade hops created by Van Tricht and organic Belgian brewer, Brouwerij Anders. The resulting Trappist monk-style cheese is made from pasteurized milk from Holstein and Brown Swiss cows and vegetarian rennet. Aged for five to seven weeks, it is semisoft, silky, and sweet like freshly churned butter or heavy cream. It has brioche-like yeasty notes from the Belgian blonde ale wash, a sweet creaminess, and a fudgy, gooey, and pliable texture. Great with everything from a cheese board to burgers to fondue!

name: Westcombe Cheddar
tagline: Raw Cow - Westcombe Dairy - Somerset, UK
description: Aged 12 to 18 months, Westcombe Cheddar is a handcrafted, traditional clothbound Somerset cheddar. The recipe has not varied much in the more than 100 years since it was first made. One of only 3 cheeses to receive the 'Artisan Somerset Cheddar' designation from Slow Food. Most importantly, however, is how it tastes. It has a deep flavour with a mellow lactic tang and long notes evoking hazelnut, caramel and citrus. The texture is structured and firm, with a smooth, gradual breakdown that helps the flavours unfold and linger. Westcombe Cheddar is what’s known in Somerset as a 'five mile cheese', as you’re still tasting it (in a good way) five miles down the road!

name: Caciocavallo Silano
tagline: Raw Cow - Mitica - Molise, Italy
description: Caciocavallo Silano is one of Southern Italy’s oldest cheeses. A pasta filata cheese, it is made by kneading the newly formed curds (coagulated with calf and goat rennet) until an elastic, stringy texture is achieved. This version is made with raw cow’s milk aged for at least 90 days. Its rind contains small grooves left by the restraining cords, and it has a beautiful seal that is burnished into the rind. The cheese is mild and milky with slight piquancy. Use it as a table cheese or enjoy it on a sandwich with prosciutto - crudo or cotto!

name: Cornish Kern
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Catherine Mead & Dane Hopkins - West Cornwall, UK
description: Named World’s Best at the 2017 World Cheese Awards, this cheese is made by Catherine Mead and the team at Lynher Dairies near Truro, West Cornwall. The make is inspired by Gouda, and the unique use of Alpine-style starter cultures encourage flavors of tropical fruit & roasted cashews. Smooth and well-rounded, it has a butterscotch aroma, nutty sweetness and a depth of flavor that is the result of its lengthy maturation process. The dark, stippled wax rind is a great visual contrast for a cheese board!

name: Mahon
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Mitica - Spain
description: The most famous cheese from the Balearic Islands, Mahon is a square-shaped wheel with a characteristic orange rind. It is made with milk from island cows who live in the protected biosphere of the island of Menorca. Aged 4 months, it has a creamy texture with plenty of moisture in the paste. It is mild and buttery with a nutty finish. Perfect for melting!

name: OG Kristal
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Van Tricht - Roeselare, Belgium
description: This assertive Belgian gouda is a must-try cheese for any lover of tyrosine crystals. What are those? Glad you asked…they are the crunchy, salty, savory bits of amino acid that form in aged cheeses as the protein structure of the milk breaks down. Yes, those! Chances are you have enjoyed them before! Like many aged goudas, the base flavor of OG Kristal leans sweeter, with notes of boozy cherries and butterscotch. The crystallized texture provides a savory balance to the fruity, nutty sweetness.

name: Asiago Fresco
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Mitica - Veneto, Italy
description: Also known as Pressato, this young Asiago is aged only 20-40 days. The mild flavors are buttery and creamy, with a delicate tang. Enjoy sliced and melted on a sandwich, grated on pizza, or eaten with crusty bread.

name: Cabot Clothbound Cheddar
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Cabot Creamery/Cellars at Jasper Hill - Greensboro, VT
description: Cabot Clothbound Cheddar is the result of a highly successful collaboration between cheesemakers at Cabot's Vermont Creamery, and The Cellars at Jasper Hill in Vermont. Cabot makes wheels of clothbound cheddar and sends them to Jasper Hill for aging. After 10 months, beautiful wheels of mature Vermont Clothbound Cheddar emerge. Reminiscent of a classic English cheddar, it is at once sweet, savory, and tangy with a creamy but brittle texture.

name: Caciotta al Tartufo
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Monti Trentini - Italy
description: This is a great, young truffle cheese with plenty of bang for the buck! Made with pasteurized cow's milk, it has a semi-soft, creamy and mild paste with the pungency of real Italian Summer truffles. Perfect for your cheese board, or to crumble on pizza with sauteed mushrooms!

name: Cantal Entre-deux
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Fromagerie Duroux - Auvergne, France
description: Cantal is one of France's oldest and most traditional cow's milk cheeses. The texture is semi-firm, moist and slightly crumbly with a natural rind mottled with brown, gray, and rust colored molds. Mild and accessible, it has flavors of butter, fresh milk, nuts, citrus, and caramel. Classically used in gratin, fondue, and soups, Cantal also works well paired with fresh fruit or roasted nuts.

name: Challerhocker
tagline: Raw Cow - Käserei Tufertschwil/Chas & Co. - Lütisburg, Switzerland
description: Pronunciation: "hollar hocker." Translation: "sitting in the cellar." Originally an Appenzeller maker, Walter Rass began experimenting and fine-tuning recipes to create this remarkable cheese - the result is truly special. It is washed in wine and spices and aged for a minimum of 10 months. Deep in flavor with a slight fruitiness, it is firm yet creamy, with notes of roasted nuts and butterscotch.

name: Daniel's Reserve
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Daniel's Artisan - Ferndale, WA
description: Part of the Ferndale Farmstead family, Daniel's Artisan cheeses are Daniel Wavrin's passion project. Daniel's Reserve is a unique hybrid of Dutch techniques and the Italian styles Ferndale Farmstead is known for. The curds are rinsed with cold water before being formed into large wheels, contributing terroir from the heavy rain in the Puget Sound. This is a fine example of the pristine results made possible with the Pacific Northwest sun, air, and animals. Aged over two years, its rich, robust flavors of butterscotch and caramel captivate the senses with a distinctive crystal crunch from tyrosine development. A quintessential element to charcuterie boards and equally as delicious on a sandwich!

name: Fontina Val d'Aosta
tagline: Raw Cow - Fromagerie Haut Val'Ayas - Piedmont, Italy
description: Often imitated, never duplicated - Fontina Val d'Aosta is the original Italian fontina. It is semi-firm & creamy, with a washed rind that imparts a mildly pungent aroma. Flavors are rich and nutty with a subtle hint of fruit and grass. One of the world's greatest melting cheeses, it is the centerpiece to Piedmont's famous fonduta - a silky blend of Fontina val D'Aosta, cream, eggs, and shaved white truffle. Also fantastic on a sandwich with prosciutto, or added to mozzarella on a pizza.

name: Fuego
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Daniel's Artisan - Ferndale, Washington
description: Fuego, by Daniel's Artisan Cheese, is a milky cow's milk cheese rubbed with a spicy blend of chiles from the Yakima Valley.

name: Isle of Mull Cheddar
tagline: Raw Cow - Reade Family/Neal's Yard Dairy - Isle of Mull, Scotland
description: What happened when a couple of Somerset natives relocated to the Isle of Mull? They built a farm and the island's only creamery. After production, Isle of Mull Cheddar is aged by Neal's Yard in London for about 18 months. Depending on time of year, this farmstead cheddar can vary in color from pale yellow to bright white. Occasionally natural blue veining will occur, but don't let this deter you; consider it a tasty bonus! Complexly flavored, Isle of Mull is at once sharp, tangy, fruity and earthy.

name: Kirkham's Lancashire
tagline: Raw Cow - Graham Kirkham/Neal's Yard Dairy - Lancashire, England
description: In 1939 there were 202 farmhouse producers of Lancashire. Today, only the Kirkham family remain, with Graham Kirkham the third generation to follow in his family's footsteps by making raw milk Lancashire according to the traditional method. This involves combining curds from several days' milkings – an approach as unique as it is time consuming, having originated in the days when Lancashire farms were much smaller, and didn't have enough cows to make cheese on a daily basis. But it's well worth the effort for the resulting complexity of taste. Neal's Yard Dairy has worked closely with the Kirkhams for over 30 years to continue the tradition os this treasured territorial cheese. Best known for its inimitable crumbly-yet-creamy texture – a texture the Kirkham family call ‘buttery crumble’ – this raw milk farmhouse Lancashire boasts a bright, full flavor finished off by a light, yogurty tang. For a deeply British experience, serve this on toast alongside a plum jam and crack open an English style ale.

name: LegenDairy Cheddar - Aged 20 Years!
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Renard's Artisan Cheese - Sturgeon Bay, WI
description: Renard's Artisan Cheese is a fourth generation cheesemaker in Door County, Wisconsin. Their cheeses have been a staple in Door County since their beginning and are now beloved around the world. The 20 year aging process transforms this gourmet cheddar into a true work of art. As it matures, it develops mouthwatering crystals that provide a unique textural experience. Each bite delivers a beautiful combination of sharpness and richness, with nutty undertones. LegenDairy 20 Year Aged Cheddar boasts a flavor profile that includes hints of caramel, a distinct but pleasant sharpness, and a sophisticated saltiness that enhances every savory morsel. The cheese has a crumbly yet creamy texture that melts beautifully in your mouth, leaving a long-lasting finish that keeps you coming back for more. Whether enjoyed on a cheese platter, paired with your favorite wine, or used in gourmet recipes, LegenDairy Cheddar is the ultimate indulgence. Elevate your cheese experience and treat yourself or your guests to this incredible artisan cheese. You won't be disappointed!

name: Mimolette
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Isigny Sainte Mere - Normandy, France
description: Produced around the town of Lille, in the Flanders area of Pas-de-Calais, northern France, Mimolette is an aged, raw cow's milk cheese. Apart from its distinctive shape, Mimolette's other striking feature is its bright orange color, the result of using natural annatto seasoning during production. The interior paste of the cheese is very dense, hard and smooth with flavors of caramel, butterscotch and toasted nuts.

name: Point Reyes Toma
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Point Reyes Farmstead Cheese Co. - Point Reyes, CA
description: Produced in Marin County, an hour north of San Francisco, Point Reyes Toma is made in the tradition of the great Italian cow's milk table cheeses. Toma is firm in texture with rich, buttery and grassy flavors and a slightly tangy finish. It is ideal for snacking, sandwiches, and grating into pasta.

name: Quebec Vintage Cheddar
tagline: Raw Cow - Old Quebec - Quebec, Canada/Lancaster, PA
description: After production, this cheddar spends about a year aging in Quebec and then at least an additional 2 years in Lancaster, PA. Vintage Cheddar is dry and crumbly with a sharp, tangy flavor. Our best selling cheddar, this makes a lasting impression on a cheese platter served with crisp apples and roasted nuts. It is also amazing melted into potatoes or macaroni and cheese.

name: Queso Botanero
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Don Froylan - Salem, OR
description: The Ochoa family has been producing queso fresco since the late 1990s when Don Froylan and Zoila moved their family to Oregon. Unable to find any authentic Mexican cheese, they began making some in their home kitchen with 10 gallons of milk every day. The whole family, from youngest to oldest, had their share in the cheese making process. As it became popular Don Froylan had the dream to open a commercial creamery but he didn’t know where to begin. Sadly, he passed before he was able to achieve his dream. His family decided to make it a reality and opened the creamery, choosing the brand name Don Froylan in loving memory of their hard working father. They proudly continue to produce of the most authentic and highest quality Mexican line of cheese in the United States. Made with the freshest jalapeños and cilantro, their Queso Botanero is a smooth, creamy melting cheese perfect for quesadillas, nachos, grilled cheese or just as a snack. Bright and full of fun flavor, soon to be a new favorite in your kitchen!

name: Schnebelhorn
tagline: Raw Cow - Reto Guntensperger & Kaserei Butschwil - Saint Gallen, Switzerland
description: Schnebelhorn is made with raw milk which comes from Swiss Brown / Braunvieh cows. Its creator, Reto Güntensperger, is a third-generation cheesemaker in the canton of St. Gallen. His grandfather made Appenzeller, his father made Appenzeller, but Reto wants to branch out. When the Swiss Cheese Union collapsed in 1999, he had his chance. Cream enriched & aged for 8 months, it has aromas of toasted hazelnuts, brown butter & roasted onions. The paste is firm & pale gold, with flecks of crystals & a creamy finish.

name: Sleeping Beauty
tagline: Raw Cow - Cascadia Creamery - Trout Lake, WA
description: Cascadia Creamery is a family run operation located in the foothills of Mt. Adams in the town of Trout Lake, Washington. It has been certified organic for decades and is committed to sustainable and humane practices. They also make outstanding cheese. Sleeping Beauty is made with the raw milk from cows grazing on the grasses grown in the rich volcanic soil of the Cascade Mountains. Buttery and sweet in flavor with a slightly tangy finish, its paste is a beautiful pale gold with small eyes. The texture is both creamy and slightly crumbly. It has a beautiful gray mottled rind that develops over the aging period of 75 to 100 days. This is a great beer cheese.

name: Sparkenhoe Red Leicester
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Clark Family/Neal's Yard Dairy - Leicestershire, England
description: Until David and Jo Clarke decided to revive the practice in 2005, Red Leicester in its clothbound form had been extinct for 50 years. Though neither David nor Jo had any experience of cheesemaking, they had a herd of Holsteins, whose pedigree and quality had been carefully overseen by the Clarke family for three generations. Drawing on a combination of old books and local advice, the pair settled upon a recipe and set to converting the milk of their 150 cows into Red Leicester, using animal rennet and annatto, a natural plant dye obtained from a South American bush that has been used in the coloration of cheeses for almost 300 years. The cheese is clothbound with lard. As it matures, the texture dries and the flavor strengthens and deepens, from savory, smooth and mellow, to nutty and rich.

name: Tomme de Savoie
tagline: Raw Cow - Mons Fromagerie - Savoie, France
description: Tomme simply refers to the round/small shape of a cheese, combined with the region or town where it's made. In this case, it is a raw, cow's milk cheese from the mountainous Eastern region of the Savoie in the Rhone Alpes. One of France's ancient cheeses, it is mild & semi-firm with a golden paste and a mottled & rustic brownish-gray rind. Made from the skimmed milk left over from the production of butter, the flavor is earthy & rustic with a pleasant tang.

name: Truffle Gouda
tagline: Raw Cow - Melkbus - Netherlands
description: Melkbus' line of cheeses are made on single-family farms identified by the numbers printed on each wheel of cheese. Truffle Gouda comes exclusively from Farm 149. This farmstead cheese starts out like traditional Boerenkaas (raw milk farmer cheese), until black truffle shavings are generously added to the curd prior to pressing. Intensely truffley, this is not only our most popular truffle cheese, but also our most popular gouda. Its texture is semi-soft and creamy with balanced flavors of sweetness, earth and truffle.

name: Yoredale Wensleydale
tagline: Raw Cow - Ben and Sam Spence - Wensley, UK
description: Ben and Sam Spence began making cheese in 2019 after leaving their finance jobs for a slower pace of life in the countryside. Initially working on Ben’s family’s farm, they started working on a raw milk Wensleydale. They set up their own micro dairy—and they really do mean micro dairy as it is set up in their garage—and developed a partnership with a small local dairy farm. With the support of other cheesemakers and Neal’s Yard Dairy, they are now making this traditional Wensleydale. Yoredale has all the lemon yogurt acidity you expect from a Wensleydale, with more mineral, earthy tones closer to the rind.

name: Fresh Ricotta
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Calabro Cheese Co. - East Haven, CT
description: Calabro ricotta is a special cheese. The texture is impossibly light, fluffy and creamy. Flavors are milky, buttery & sweet. Once you try it, it will be impossible to go back to the generic tubs you find at your local grocery store. The curd is still hand-dipped and hand-packed into Calabro’s instantly recognizable metal containers that are pierced with tiny holes to allow the whey to drain, even after the cheese is shipped. Delicious when enjoyed as is, it is also an essential ingredient for your ravioli, lasagna and cannoli filling. If that's not all, it is also great for baking, or drizzling with honey for an amazing dessert.

name: Lioni Burrata con Panna, 8oz
tagline: Pastuerized Cow - Lioni Latticini - Union, New Jersey
description: The Salzarulo family moved from Lioni, Italy to Brooklyn, New York in 1980, where they founded Lioni Latticini. After decades of cheesemaking in Italy, they brought their expertise to the United States, and currently offer a range of exceptional fresh cheeses. Produced with a fusion of traditional techniques and modern technological precision, their products embody all the best qualities of fresh Italian cheese – mellow, delicate, yet still abundantly flavorful. This cow’s milk burrata is blissfully rich. The thin outer rind stretches around a filling of slightly sweet, creamy panna di latte and tender pasta filata mozzarella. Cut it open, and the interior spills out, instantly enriching your dish with a cascade of cream. This burrata will magically transform even the simplest salad into a summery delight!

name: Bocconcino di Langa
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Caseificio della'Alta Langa - Piedmont, Italy - 4oz
description: Meaning "little mouthful," Bocconcino is made with goat's milk that has been enriched with cream. It has a thin, soft, edible rind and a smooth ivory paste. Flavors include notes of tangy, fresh cream and subtle hints of grass. Enjoy with crusty bread at room temperature.

name: Persille de Rambouillet
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Ferme de la Tremblaye - Ile-de-France, France
description: This unbelievably smooth ash-coated goat milk blue comes from La Tremblaye dairy, located in the countryside surrounding Paris. Persille de Rambouillet gets its name from its “parsley-veined” interior—persille—and the Rambouillet forest adjacent to the dairy’s picturesque farmland. With a supple texture and notes of white pepper and sweet cream, this blue is, well...amazing. Huge staff favorite!

name: Belgioso Burrata
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - BelGioioso - Green Bay, WI - 8oz
description: Traditionally from Puglia in southern Italy, this is one of the freshest of all cow's milk cheeses. Milky, sweet, fresh mozzarella on the outside, with molten ribbons of curd and cream on the inside. Each 8oz package contains two 4oz pieces of burrata packed in water for optimum storage. Drizzle with olive oil and a pinch of sea salt and serve with crusty bread. You can work up from there by adding any of the following: grilled bread, prosciutto, salame, sliced tomatoes, fresh herbs, grilled vegetables, aged balsamic or sauteed rapini.

name: Bellwether Farms Creme Fraiche
description: Family owned and operated, Bellwether Farms is located in Sonoma County, California, about an hour north of San Francisco and a few miles from the Pacific Ocean. Their award-winning French-style cultured cream has a rich, nutty flavor with an appealing tart finish. Works perfectly for savory & sweet applications. Great for enriching soups, sauces, pastry, pies & berries!

name: Bezi Original Labneh
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Bezi - New York, NY
description: Co-founders Ilay and Hasan grew up eating labneh at breakfast and dreamed of making it a staple in every American kitchen. Labneh is a creamy, spreadable dairy dip traditionally enjoyed across the Middle East and Mediterranean. Ilay, a McKinsey consultant turned cheesemaker, moved to New York from Istanbul to pursue her MBA. During that time, she followed her passion and worked on a farm milking cows and sheep and learned the art of making cheese from scratch. Hasan, on the other hand, is a Berkeley engineer and an heir to one of Turkey's largest cheesemaking families. His grandfather, known as "The Cheese King" in Turkey, built the Bahcivan Gida factory from the ground up, transforming it into an empire. Their paths serendipitously crossed at a previous job where they bonded over a shared passion for dairy. Together, they embarked on a mission to make labneh a thing in the US and created BEZI: the labneh that labnehs better than any other labneh out there. High in protein, low in tang, and ready to party!

name: Buche Maitre Seguin
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Soignon - Poitou-Charentes, France
description: Balanced and smooth, Buche Maitre Seguin ripens into three distinct textures. The outer rind is thick and fluffy, while the creamline directly underneath gets soft and oozy. The inner paste is dense and chalky. Bright and lemony in flavor, this cheese is as at home on a cheese board as it is on a fresh green salad.

name: Buf Buffalo Burrata
tagline: Pasteurized Buffalo - Buf Creamery - El Rosal, Columbia - 8oz
description: Imported from the Columbia...yes, that's right, Columbia. Trust us, if it wasn't really good, we wouldn't be selling it. You love burrata, we know this. You also love mozzarella di bufula. Well, time for these two to meet. Buf's Burrata di Bufula combines two great things - the bright, tangy of buffalo milk and the molten texture of fresh burrata. Each package contains one, 8oz piece of fresh burrata di bufala packed in water for optimum storage.

name: Buf Mozzarella di Bufala
tagline: Pasteurized Buffalo - Buf - El Rosal, Columbia - 8oz
description: Imported from the Columbia...yes, that's right, Columbia. Trust us, if it wasn't really good, we wouldn't be selling it. Mozzarella di Bufala is wonderfully fresh and delicate with a pleasant tang. This is the perfect cheese to use on your Pizza Margherita, in a salad or with other classic Italian recipes. Each package contains one, 8oz piece of fresh mozzarella packed in water for optimum storage. Voted the #1 Mozzarella in 2016 by the American Cheese Society.

name: Cheesella di Bufala
tagline: Pasteurized Cow & Buffalo - Guffanti - Campania, Italy
description: What happens when two spectacular cheesemaking traditions meet? When legendary mozzarella (made with buffalo milk) is literally preserved in the rich, stretched-curd cheese of Caciocavallo? Fresh and aged? One answer: the fabulous Cheesella di Bufala. A novelty with over 200 years of history behind it! With it's lactic and buttery taste, Cheesella di Bufala is perfect for pizzas and pastas. Buy it by the whole, half or quarter wheel - all priced by the pound. Each wheel is approximately 1.3 lbs. Like with our other cheeses sold by the wedge, the actual price will be determined when we put it on the scale.

name: DeLaurenti Pimento Cheese Spread
tagline: Made in the DeLaurenti kitchen!
description: Our take on this Southern classic is a little bit savory, a little bit smoky, and delightfully spicy. Made in our kitchen using New School American Cheese, spicy peppadews, and smoked paprika. Perfect for scooping with a cracker, spicing up your grilled cheese, or adding some kick to your burger!

name: Dorstone, 8oz
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Neal's Yard Dairy - Herefordshire UK
description: Named after the Village of Dorstone above the River Wye in England, this ash-ripened goat's milk cheese is made in the style of classic French goat cheeses. Aged for only 3 to 4 weeks, Dorstone has a fluffy interior and a thin, delicate rind with a lightly acidic and citrusy flavor.

name: FETA Voras 2/4.4#
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep/Goat - Essex St. Cheese/Tastanis - Florina, Greece
description: Feta Voras is made in the far Northwestern corner of Greece, in the province of Florina using mostly sheep's milk and a small amount of goat's milk. This is mountainous land, covered in wildflowers and herbs. The small third generation firm, run by brothers Andreas and Sokratis, makes a creamy, crumbly cheese that you’ll want as a staple in your home. Mount Voras is one of Greece’s highest peaks and its nearby slopes make up the grazing ground for the sheep whose milk becomes Feta Voras. Florina is one of the seven regions that can make traditoinal PDO feta. It’s made in small blocks, sprinkled with sea salt from the port of Patras, aged for about three months, then sliced into wedges and packed up for shipment to New York.

name: Florette
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Fromagerie Guilloteau - Rhone-Alps, France
description: Love brie but in the mood for something a bit less barnyard and a bit more bright? Look no further. Florette combines the creamy, lush texture of it's cow's milk cousin with the bright piquancy of goat cheese. Ivory white in color with a ultra-creamy, spreadable texture, this cheese is a perfect gateway goat.

name: Fresh Buffalo Ricotta
tagline: Pasteurized Buffalo - Calabro Cheese Co. - East Haven, CT
description: If you like Calabro's award winning fresh ricotta, you will love their equally as delicious fresh Buffalo Ricotta! It is similar to the cow's milk version with a light, smooth & delicate texture, but with the hallmark tang of fresh buffalo milk. Perfect for filling ravioli, for bruschetta with honey or lasagna!

name: Fresh Mozzarella
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Grande Cheese Co. - Brownsville, WI
description: Originally made using water buffalo's milk, the cow's milk version is perfect for your Caprese Salad or Pizza Margherita. Slice into medallions and drizzle with olive oil and a pinch of sea salt for a simple, but satisfying appetizer. Four rounds to a pound, each piece is packed in a little water for freshness. Feel free to add a little tap water for storage. Before using it on pizza, drain the water and let the cheese rest in the fridge for an hour. Pour off excess water (this would have wound up in the middle of your pizza), use and enjoy!

name: Gina Marie Cream Cheese
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Sierra Nevada Cheese Co. - Willows, CA
description: Gina Marie is the original natural cream cheese. With all due respect to the mass produced cream cheese that you find at your local grocery store, there really is no comparison. Made using only milk, cream, and salt, this cheese is void of any fillers, stabilizers, and gums. Light and fluffy in texture, fresh and creamy in flavor, use it liberally whenever you have a craving for cream cheese.

name: Gina Marie Farmer's Cheese
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Sierra Nevada Cheese Co. - Willows, CA
description: Use this Fresh Russian-Style Farmers Cheese as a filling for blintzes, lasagna, or filled pasta. Make a cheesecake or other baked desserts, spread on toast or bagels. It has half the fat of our Gina Marie Cream Cheese with all the probiotic benefits of kefir cultures. Light, creamy and mild, it is perfect for all your sweet & savory recipes!

name: Halloumi, 6oz
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Lost Peacock Creamery - Olympia, Washington
description: Lost Peacock Creamery is a Grade A Goat Dairy and Farmstead Cheesemaking Operation in Olympia, Washington. Halloumi is bright white, with a mozzarella-like texture and a light, salty flavor. Cut into batons, put it on a skewer, and cook it directly on the grill until charred and warm. Don't worry, Halloumi's strong, rigid network of protein will keep it from melting into the coals. Enjoy as is topped with fresh herbs, add the grilled cheese to the top of a salad, or crumble into an omelette. For the colder months, fry the cheese lightly in olive oil in your favorite saute pan. Lost Peacock's Halloumi is a delightfully crispy on the outside, gooey on the inside, squeaks in your mouth, bit of perfection. This cheese was made to be the star of the show!

name: Humboldt Fog
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Cypress Grove Chevre - Arcata, CA
description: A pioneer in American cheese-making since the 1980s, Cypress Grove Chevre helped redefine what many Americans recognized as cheese. Humboldt Fog is their award winning flagship cheese. Each handcrafted wheel features a distinctive ribbon of edible vegetable ash. You'll enjoy flavors of buttermilk and fresh cream, complemented with floral notes, herbaceous overtones, and a clean citrus finish. As Humboldt Fog matures, the creamline develops and the flavor intensifies.

name: Idaho Grilling Cheese, 8oz
tagline: Pasteruized Cow - Ballard Cheese - Gooding, ID
description: Stacie and Steve Ballard, started their 35-acre farm in Gooding, Idaho in 1995. Steve wanted to start a dairy farm despite not having any personal experience in part because other family members were already in the farming business. Steve and his son Travis had both worked with heavy mechanical equipment and were good with their hands. Those skills were indispensable to the success of the farm. The family diversified into cheesemaking with Travis in 2004 to add more value to their milk and diversify from the volatile milk market. Their Idaho Grilling Cheese is a traditional semi-firm Mediterranean grilling cheese with a distinctive layered texture. It is mildly salty with a rich buttery taste. Idaho Grilling Cheese can withstand a tremendous amount of heat without melting. It develops a delicious golden crust when grilled, BBQ'd, or fried. A must-try for fans of Halloumi!

name: Leonora
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Fancendera/Mitica - Leon, Spain
description: Leonora is a goat's milk cheese produced in the mountainous region of Leon in northwestern Spain. Known for its distinctive loaf shape, the interior paste is bone white with a dense cakey texture toward the middle and a silky cream line just under the rind. Flavors are bright and creamy with a pleasant lemony tang.

name: Lost Peacock Fresh Chevre
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Lost Peacock - Olympia, WA
description: Lost Peacock Creamery is a wife & husband Grade A creamery in Olympia, WA. When in doubt, go local. Especially when it comes to rich, creamy, fresh chevre. Happy goats make great milk. Great milk makes great cheese. It's safe to say that the 3 dozen grass pasture fed goats have a great life. Spread this seasonal chevre on crostini, fold it into fresh pasta with herbs, dot it on your pizza or crumble it on your wild green salad!

name: Meredith Dairy Marinated Feta
tagline: Pasteurized Goat/Sheep - Meredith Dairy - Meredith, Australia
description: Yes, Australians can make great cheese, too. These delicate little white cubes of spreadable goat/sheep farmstead cheese are a customer favorite in our cheese case. Marinated in olive oil with sprigs of thyme and cracked black pepper, they are perfect to spread on grilled bread or set aloft a handful of fresh, wild greens or grilled vegetables.

name: Monte Enebro
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Rafael Baez - Castille-Lyon, Spain
description: Made in Avila, Spain, by legendary cheesemaker Rafael Baez and his daughter Paloma, Monte Enebro is a goat's milk cheese made in a distinct log shape. Its name translates to Juniper Hill, referring to the bountiful juniper plants surrounding the dairy. The cheese is coated in penicilium roqueforti, the mold that makes blue cheeses blue. When young, the interior paste of the cheese is pure white and slightly chalky and brittle in texture. With age, the paste tends to break down and become runny and almost translucent just under the rind. Flavors in the younger cheeses are mild, bright and tangy, with distinct citrus notes combined with a cellar-like aroma and flavor imparted by the blue rind. As the cheeses mature, the aromas become more pungent and the flavors evolve and strengthen, becoming quite assertive, tasting of barnyard and goat. Perfect with Sauternes or Spanish dessert wine.

name: Nocciolo
tagline: Pasteurized Cow/Goat/Sheep - Caseificio dell'Alta Langa - Piedmont, Italy
description: Il Nocciola, meaning hazelnut in Italian, is a beautiful cow/goat/sheep combo from Northern Italy's Piedmont region. It is sweet, buttery, bright & impossibly creamy. Despite it's diminutive stature, it brings maximum impact. It's hard to find anyone who doesn't love this cheese, especially when you hand them a glass of bubbly to go with it!

name: Petite Pave de Paris
tagline: Pasteurized Cow/Goat - Ferme de la Tremblaye - Ile-de-France, France
description: Made to resemble the iconic paving stones of Paris, Petite Pavé de Paris is a masterpiece of sustainable farming and artisanal cheesemaking from Ferme de la Tremblaye. From its appearance to its flavor, this is truly a unique cheese. The square shape and ashed rind give the cheese its Parisian cobblestone appearance. The paste of the cheese is mottled buttery yellow and ivory thanks to the alternating layers of cow’s milk curd and goat’s milk curd. Petite Pavé de Paris is tart and fruity with a mineral finish, the perfect complement to a light and bright wine!

name: Shabby Shoe
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Blakesville Creamery - Port Washington, WI
description: Blakesville Creamery is a farmstead creamery, meaning the cheeses are made by hand on the same farm where the animals are raised and their milk is collected. Their goal is to humanely raise healthy goats using sustainable farming practices and to produce the highest quality of handmade artisan cheeses. Because of this, care and attention to the purity, quality, and flavor of the milk are critical to the production process. Their cheeses are ripened naturally, focusing on developing characteristic flavor and texture and eschewing shortcuts or techniques that would affect quality. Despite the grungy name, this cheese is pristine! An homage to the French Chabichou (pronounced, you guessed it, "shabby shoe"), Shabby Shoe nails the thin wrinkled rind, gooey creamline, and incredibly light texture of the original. The taste is bright, featuring notes of citrus, sweet cream, and grass, with a short, clean finish–reminiscent of fleeting clouds on a summer day. With this delicate chèvre, Blakesville Creamery connects the dots between the Loire Valley and the shores of Lake Michigan. One bite and you'll understand why Shabby Shoe has quickly become a staff favorite!

name: Tomme de Chevre Grand-Mere
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Fromagerie P. Jacquin - Loire, France
description: Located in the Centre-Val de Loire, Fromagerie Pascal Jacquin et Fils has specialized in making and aging the region’s traditional and exemplary goat’s milk cheeses since 1947. “Grandmother Adrienne” is a beautifully bloomed goat cheese. It has a fudgy texture towards the center and a runny, silky cream line. Flavors of buttermilk, lemon and faint minerality, make it perfect for a cheese course or simple meal with a fresh salad, bread and a crisp white from the Loire.

name: New School Quality American Cheese
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - New School Quality American Cheese - Santa Monica, CA
description: This cheese changes everything. As much as we all might hate to admit it, there is a time and place for good ol' American Cheese. Burgers, grilled cheese...you know what I mean. Creamy, gooey, rich...oh but the conflicting emotions that come with it when you venture to read the ingredients on the back of the Kraft package! What if you could have all of the benefit, with none of the sacrifice and conflict? There aren't many scenarios when the answer to this question is an unequivocal yes. Thanks to Chef Eric Greenspan, who has spent the better part of 25 years being a nationally recognized champion of American Comfort food, this cheese is a definite YES. Sliced from the block without cutting corners, New School American Cheese is finally American Cheese done right. Made in small batches from simple ingredients you can pronounce and recognize, like aged cheddar, cream, and real butter, there is no better-tasting or melting American cheese.

name: DeLaurenti Shredded Mozzarella and Provolone, 1#
tagline: As seen on a DeLaurenti slice!
description: As seen and enjoyed on our famous pizza on 1st & Pike! Walk in the 1st Ave door and smell the unmistakeable aroma of hot pizza coming out of the oven! So what if it's 10:45am...pizza for breakfast! Want to enjoy pizza like this in the comfort of your own home? Well, you can't do it without this cheese. It is mild but flavorful and ultra gooey! Load up and get going! Roughly 1lb of cheese amply covers a large pie.

name: Ferndale Farmstead Smoked Scamorza, 9.5oz
tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Ferndale Farmstead - Ferndale, WA
description: A signature Italian cheese...made right here in Fernadale, WA! This cheese is hung on ropes to age and lightly smoked, a technique used by artisans for hundreds of years.
