This barrel-selected estate Pinot has enough depth and complexity to enchant the palate with a harmonious blend of ripe raspberries, earthy tobacco, and a touch of spice. Try it with a rosemary-infused rack of lamb or za'atar-spiced roasted eggplant with a creamy tahini sauce.

name: Illahe Willamette Valley Pinot Noir
tagline: Willamette Valley, OR - 2021 - Pinot Noir
description: Illahe Vineyards embraces sustainable, horse-powered farming and traditional winemaking methods. This classic Willamette Valley mid-range Oregon Pinot Noir exudes elegance and finesse, boasting vibrant notes of raspberry, black cherry, and earthy undertones. It’s leagues better than the cheap plonk but still decently affordable. Delight your palate by pairing this captivating Pinot with a savory mushroom risotto or a sumptuous roast chicken.

name: Le Fontane 'Sabbe Rosse' Rosso
tagline: Sicily, IT - 2023 - Frappato, Nero d'Avola
description: Le Fontane shares familial ties to the legendary COS and Occhipinti wineries in Sicily, and this new project absolutely belongs in the same conversation. The Sabbie Rosse, named so due to red clay soils in the vineyard, is like an alternate take of their Cerasuolo di Vittoria. This wine is mostly Frappato, with just over a quarter of it being Nero d'Avola. The result is a medium-ish bodied red with inviting red berry and rose notes and a lingering, raspberry-tinged finish. Delicate herbal notes on the palate pair perfectly with poultry and richer fish, like tuna or salmon.

name: Le Fontane Cerasuolo di Vittoria Classico DOCG
tagline: Sicily, IT - 2022 - Frappato, Nero d'Avola
description: Cerasuolo di Vittoria is the only DOCG in Sicily, and Le Fontane's interpretation stands comfortably among its peers as a great and delicious wine. The wine is equal parts Frappato and Nero d'Avola, showcasing the gorgeous terroir of the area via graceful herbal and red berry notes on the nose and fine, mouth-watering tannins anchored by vibrant and lingering Bing cherry notes on the palate. While the wines of Etna are rightfully on the rise at the moment, this appellation has stood the test of time and this wine in particular has quickly become a staff favorite.

name: Le Fraghe Bardino
tagline: Veneto, IT - 2020 - Corvina/Rondinella
description: Bardolino draws a lot of parallels to Valpolicella. They both utilize the same grapes, but the Bardolino appellation falls a little closer to Lake Garda. In effect, the wine region has somewhat more of a coastal influence and the wine itself is a little lighter and breezier. Takes a chill quite well, too!

name: Le Ragnaie Brunello di Montalcino DOCG
tagline: Tuscany, IT - 2020 - Sangiovese Grosso
description: Generally, our favorite Brunello producer. This vintage boasts restrained oak, unleashing earthy vigor and bountiful fruit — think ripe black cherries and wild berries. Decant for a couple of hours and savor its evolving complexity. Cellaring? Tuck it away for five to eight years and prepare for a spectacular unveiling. If drinking now, decant it for at least two hours before indulging in this powerful, refined masterpiece.

name: Les Vignerons d'Estezargues 'Cuvee des Galets' Cotes du Rhone
tagline: Estezargues, FR - 2021 - Grenache, Syrah, Carignan
description: Discover exceptional value in this organic marvel from Les Vignerons d'Estezargues, a trailblazing Rhône co-op championing natural winemaking. Dubbed "cave co-op with a natural twist," this wine delivers remarkable quality under $15. Revel in the harmonious blend of ripe raspberries, juicy black cherries, and a touch of spice. Elevate a simple weeknight with this standout, and let it shine alongside a hearty ratatouille or grilled lamb chops. Cheers to affordability meeting excellence.

name: Mark Ryan 'Lonely Heart' Cabernet Sauvignon
tagline: Red Mountain, WA - 2020 - Cabernet Sauvignon
description: Mark Ryan's 'Lonely Heart' is made from relatively younger vine plantings from the esteemed Quintessence vineyard on Red Mountain. The Cabernet Sauvignon, with gentle extraction, matures for two years almost solely in new French oak, amplifying its complexity. It offers notes of blackberry, cedar, and roasted coffee with a spicy nuanced finish. It's one of the best Red Mountain wines. Match its bold sophistication with a grilled, aged ribeye steak or fettuccine with a hearty Bolognese ragu.

name: Mark Ryan 'The Chief' Red Blend
tagline: Columbia Valley, WA - 2021 - Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Petit Verdot
description: Mark Ryan’s accessibly-priced wines have earned the winery both a loyal following and the respect of elite producers. This robust Washington Cabernet Sauvignon, blended with a touch of Merlot, is intense but approachable in its youth. It tempts with aromas of black plum, vanilla, and tobacco. Pair it with grilled steak, mushroom risotto, or even better, a meal combining both!

name: Mark Ryan 'The Dissident' Red Wine
tagline: Columbia Valley, WA - 2021 - Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc Malbec, Petit Verdot
description: The 2021 Dissident is composed of a blend of fruit from several of Washington state’s finest vineyards. Red Mountain Cab from Quintessence and Henry Earl vineyards form the foundation, along with Merlot from Red Willow and Phinny Hill. This Mark Ryan wine is designed to be drunk a bit younger than most of his other main-label wines. With robust fruit in a well-structured blend, this approachable wine has blackberry and dark chocolate aromas and a spicy finish. Pair this one with hearty dishes like braised short ribs or beef stroganoff.

name: Mark Ryan Numbskull BDX
tagline: Columbia Valley, WA - 2020 - Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Petit Verdot
description: Mark Ryan's Numbskull BDX serves up an artful whisper of new oak and Cabernet sourced from esteemed vineyards. It's an uncomplicated delight. Expect bold black currant notes and a subtle cloak of earthiness. Pair this with a prime rib or robust vegetable stew for an experience that punches above its weight class. A lotta bang for your buck!

name: Plani Arche Montefalco Rosso DOC
tagline: Umbria, IT - 2022 - Sangiovese, Sagrantino
description: Those familiar with Montefalco are likely informed due to their experience(s) with a grape called Sagrantino. An historic and delicious grape that stateside, at least, holds two noticeable barriers of entry: the wine's price and its absolutely massive structure. Both issues are pleasantly addressed with the Montefalco Rosso DOC. On its own, Sagrantino needs time for the tannins to incorporate and mellow out a bit. But this wine, primarily Sangiovese with just a splash of Sagrantino, is easier to approach in its youth but is peppered with those decadent, plummy, dark-fruited notes you get in full varietal expressions. Definitely the kind of wine that shines with grilled meat and American barbecue.

name: Plani Arche Montefalco Sagrantino DOCG
tagline: Umbria, IT - 2020 - Sagrantino
description: Montefalco's an historic town that sits right in the middle of Umbria, south of the more well-visted Perugia and Assili. Here, a grape called Sagrantino reigns supreme. This is not the kind of red wine you bring to someone who isn't sure if they like red wine. Everything red wine skeptics complain about has been cranked up to eleven here: the fruit, the tannins, the structure. This wine is big and bold and highly rewards the patient consumer. Decant this wine and give it plenty of time to breathe, enjoy with your favorite cuts of beef or lamb.

name: Podere Ruggeri Corsini 'Bricco San Pietro' Barolo DOCG
tagline: Piedmont, IT - 2018 - Nebbiolo
description: Poderi Ruggeri Corsini is a family-run winery situated in Monforte d'Alba, a historic village known for its ancient stone houses at the heart of the Langhe. This single-vineyard Barolo is elegant but still quite meaty, with well-polished tannins and a smooth finish. It features notes of ripe currants, tobacco, and cocoa powder. This Barolo is a great value, partly because Corsini wines are imported directly into the state, bypassing an intermediary. It pairs well with a hearty osso buco or a sharp, aged cheese. Eminently suitable for aging, if you can resist a Barolo that already drinks well.

name: Podere Ruggeri Corsini Langhe Nebbiolo DOC
tagline: Piedmont, Italy - 2018 - 100% Nebbiolo
description: Nebbiolo is the noble grape behind the likes of Barolo and Barbaresco. Notoriously difficult to grow, this grape rewards patient and skilled growers with fruit that is similarly delicate to Pinot Noir but with a little bit more bitter, earthen characteristics. While most famously known for wines that see the grape spending a long time in wood, this version of the grape is much more approachable in its youth while still showing the drinker how interesting it can be. Try it out with heartier pasta dishes and cream sauces- don't forget that this area of Italy is known for white truffles, too!

name: Quinta Milu La Bicicleta Voladora Rioja
tagline: Navarra, Spain - 2018 - Tempranilla
description: This is a Rioja for fans of Beaujolais. Classic Tempranillo spice and dark fruit, but none of the power and tannins you would expect from a wine with extended elevage in oak barrels. Lighter and fresher in style, and at that weeknight-wine price!

name: Savage Grace Cabernet Franc
tagline: Yakima Valley, WA - 2017 - Cabernet Franc
description: Cabernet Franc is probably most well known as the main red varietal of the Loire Valley in France. Think Saumur or Chinon, wine that is deep red in color, and smells of dark berry and green pepper. What's really quite amazing, and unfortunately we don't know how such technology was created, but winemaker Michael Savage has somehow extended the Loire Valley to reach Yakima. This expression of Cab Franc is perfect for fans of the old world and those who want balanced fruit, medium tannins, and something to pair with roasted poultry.

name: Sonder Red Field Blend
tagline: Columbia Valley, WA - 2021 - Rhone Varietals
description: This Yakima-made beauty drinks like a light-bodied Cotes du Rhone. Sonder, a boutique winery, makes wines with minimal intervention to express the terroir. Their fruit-forward blend of classic Rhone varietals offers a refreshing profile of summer berries and light pepper notes. Enjoy this food-friendly wine with grilled lamb, vegetable skewers, or herb-crusted chicken thighs.

name: Swick Willamette Valley Pinot Noir
tagline: Willamette Valley, OR - 2022 - Pinot Noir
description: A classic rendition from an experimental winemaker. Joe Swick, known for daring cofermentations and extended macerations, leans into the traditional with this one. The result: a fresh and vibrant Pinot Noir that doesn't compromise on taste. Swirl the wine in your glass and revel in luscious strawberry, earthy forest floor, and a hint of spice. Pair this captivating Pinot with a delicate cedar plank salmon or a savory mushroom risotto and embrace the sublime.

name: Two Vintner Syrah
tagline: Columbia Valley, WA - 2022 - Syrah
description: Two Vintners Syrah, a perennial award-winner, proves its worth as a standout, budget-friendly Washington Syrah. Laden with luscious blackberry and hints of black pepper, it displays the winery's knack for expressing the distinctive Columbia Valley terroir. This classic Syrah, celebrated for its value and consistency, pairs wonderfully with a juicy lamb shank or a smoky barbecued brisket.

name: Vignobles Guillaume Vin de Pays de Franche-Comte IGP
tagline: Franche-Comte, FR - 2019 - 100% Pinot Noir
description: This wine hails from Franche-Comté and pours its heart into every drop. Imagine Burgundy's soulful essence, gently nudged by Jura's embrace and swayed by Côte d'Or's whispers. At a tantalizing value, each sip conjures French Pinot dreams — a delicate balance of fruit, earth, and spice. This sly, stylish delight leaves one wondering, "How am I only learning of this now?”

name: Villa Sant'Anna Vino Nobile di Montepulciano DOCG
tagline: Tuscany, IT - 2020 - Sangiovese
description: Elegant and enjoyable, this Vino Nobile echoes Brunello, yet speaks its own language. Black cherry, licorice, and untamed herbs intertwine and unfold on the palate. Enjoy now or let time work its magic on this one. Paired with rosemary-infused lamb, this lavish Tuscan gem comes alive.

name: DeLaurenti Rosato 750ml
tagline: Tuscany, IT - Sangiovese - 2024
description: A new batch of DeLaurenti Rosato has made it to our shelves! This rose is reminiscent of the roses of Provence, despite being entirely Tuscan Sangiovese. Refreshing, dry, and light with a slightly tart berry finish. This wine will transport you to a sunny afternoon on a breezy Mediterranean beach, no matter what time of year you pop the cork!

name: Arnot-Roberts Rosé
tagline: North Coast, CA - Touriga Nacional - 2025
description: Despite its location, Arnot-Roberts make wines that have a decidedly European edge to them. This rosé of Touriga Nacional has some familiar aromatics if you're a fan of Port, but that's about where the similarities end. Dry, a little prickly, and incredibly refreshing.

name: Can-Vi Rosat
tagline: Blancafort, ES - Monestrell - NV
description: This refreshing and dry rosé of Monestrell (the Spanish name for Mourvedre) is made entirely of young vine, organic fruit. A lively, textural rosé that, despite its darker color, is quite light on the palate. Plus, the can makes for easy enjoyment out in the wild!

name: Can-Vi Sparkling Rosat
tagline: Blancafort, ES - Monestrell - NV
description: This sparkling rosé of Monestrell comes from one of our favorite Catalonian winemakers, Jordi Llorens. Delicious, well-farmed fruit, in a wine that finishes its fermentation in can, and delivers a pét-nat with fine and lively bubbles!

name: Cedergreen 'Viola' Rosé
tagline: Columbia Valley, WA - Cabernet Franc, Gamay - 2025
description: If you've shopped or eaten at the market anytime in last decade or two, you've probably enjoyed a glass or three of Cedergreen's rosé. This lighter blend of Cab Franc and Gamay has some gorgeous floral and fruity aromatics and a crisp, dry finish.

name: Chateau Jouclary Cabardes Rose
tagline: Languedoc Roussillon, France - 2019 - Cinsault/Cab Franc/Grenache
description: Rose from Southern France is sometimes a gamble but rest assured that we're doing the hard work of tasting through all available options and only bring you the best. Through all this "hard work" we were really impressed with the rose from Chateau de Jouclary this year! Classic tart berry on the nose, crispy and dry finish, but a unique salty/savory note on the palate that just begs to be paired with fresh veggies and creamy cheeses.

name: La Bastide des Oliviers Rosé
tagline: Provence, FR - Cinsault, Carignan, Grenache, Syrah - 2025
description: A light, pure, and refreshing Provençal rosé is hard to beat when the sun starts hanging around extra late in the day. La Bastide des Oliviers makes one of our favorites because it's exactly what you want it to be at a pretty darn great price, too.

name: Le Vigne di Faraone Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo DOC
tagline: Abruzzo, IT - Montepulciano - 2022
description: Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo is an appellation for rose of Montepulciano in a Abruzzo. The word Cerasuolo designates the cherry color of the wines. It's darker than most rose, slightly more rich, but still finishes dry with some refreshing acidity.

name: Marcel Giraudon Bourgogne Rosé
tagline: Bourgogne, FR - Pinot Noir - 2025
description: While we don't always associate rosé when it comes to wine from Bourgogne, it is a rare and rewarding treat to come across such bottlings, and this one is no different. If you're patient with it, and don't mind cellaring this wine for a few years, you'll be highly rewarded. But if you can't wait - and to be honest, who could blame you? - this wine is a stunner with fresh garden produce, bistro classics, and the bounty of PNW seafood.

name: Mary Taylor Agenais Rose
tagline: Lot-et-Garonne, FR - 2022 - Cabernet Sauvingon, Cabernet Franc - 2022
description: This rose comes from this no-man's land between Bordeaux and the Languedoc, historically a wine region only known for bulk grocery store wine. However, this is a small, organic production brought in via Mary Taylor Wines, and displays not only tremendous value, but expectional flavor. A vibrant, light-cherry color in the glass that's reminiscent of Tavel, this rose is refreshing and textural, and great with seafood and lighter proteins.

name: Ostatu Rioja Rosado
tagline: Rioja, ES - Tempranillo, Garnacha, Viura - 2025
description: Bodegas Ostatu is easily one of the best houses operating in Rioja Alavesa. This rosé isn't just some passable pink to get you through the summer, this is a real wine of character. Mostly Tempranillo and Garnacha, there's also a splash of the white grape Viura in here; the combination of all three pointing to a true, albeit light, expression of this corner of the country. Brimming with red fruit and citrus peel, this dry rosé is great all year, but especially on a sweltering summer afternoon down by the water.

name: Pinard et Filles 'Verre de Gris' Rose
tagline: Quebec, CA - Frontenac Gris - 2020
description: While one may not always associate Quebec and rosé, this one is sure to leave an impression. A tense and nervous expression of Frontenac Gris, this wine shines with rustic cured meats or anything off the grill.

name: Poberaj Ramato
tagline: White Salmon, WA - 2021 - Pinot Grigio
description:
100 days whole cluster skin contact in 10HL open top wood cask.

Pressed into a neutral French barrel and aged for 3 years.

name: Ridge of Wonders Rosé of Pinot Noir
tagline: White Salmon, WA - Pinot Noir - 2025
description: High-Altitude Pinot Noir from the Washington side of the Columbia River Gorge make for an ethereal, aromatic rosé that doesn't feel reminiscent of any other more-storied rosé-producing region, but fits nicely in a lineup of all the Mediterranean classics. There's a delicate salinity to this wine as well that makes it especially friendly with shellfish and summer produce, too.

name: DeLaurenti Prosecco
description: Our very own prosecco from just outside Trieste. Crisp, dry and delicious. There is no prosecco season - this wine is good 12 months a year!

name: Angol d'Amig 'Pulonia' Emilia Bianco Frizzante IGP
tagline: Emilia, IT - 2022 - Pignoletto, Trebbiano Modenese
description:
Winemaker Marco Lanzotti is quietly making some of the most exciting sparkling wines in Modena. His Pulonia cuvée is a golden-yellow expression of Pignoletto* and Trebbiano Modenese. It's simultaneously soft and nutty and bright and citrusy. The mousse on this pet-nat frizzante is fine, albeit a little more rustic than what you might expect from sparkling wine vinified in the traditional method. Given the wine's origins, it's hard to imagine a better pairing for this wine than rustic salumi or Parmigiano Reggiano-forward dishes.

*Pignoletto is not formally recognized as a grape name anymore, as the grape was proven genetically identical to Grechetto di Todi/Grechetto Gentile. The name now refers to the DOC where white wines are made of this grape, but clearly, some wineries are still holding on to the grape's traditional name.

name: Angol d'Amig 'Scaramusc' Lambrusco dell'Emilia IGT
tagline: Emilia, IT - 2022 - Lambrusco Grasparossa, Lambrusco di Sorbara, Lambrusco Salamino
description: Lambrusco comes in many shapes and styles these days, but Marco Lanzotti's Scaramusc might just be one of the most intense and brooding that we have in the shop. But, despite it's intense blackberry and richer savory notes, the wine comes in under twelve percent alcohol and feels quite light on the palate.  A dry and refreshing treat while you snack on Reggiano, mortadella, and grissini while you wait for your pizza to come out of the oven.

name: Aval Cidre Blanc 12oz
tagline: Bretagne, FR - Apples - NV
description: Lightly tannic and massively approachable, this cider, comprised of fresh-pressed juice from sour apples, is a pristine example of classic Bretagne cider. Mineral-driven with bright fruit notes, this dry cider is an excellent option with paella, lighter soups, and Thai food.

name: Aval Cidre Gold 12oz
tagline: Bretagne, FR - Apples - NV
description: Classic French profile, composed of bitter and bittersweet apples ideal for quality cider. Bold and slightly musky, the Aval Gold is a great alternative to a blanc de blancs style Champagne, perfect with cured meats and spicy curry.

name: Aval Cidre Rose 12oz
tagline: Bretagne, FR - Apples - NV
description: This cider gets its color from sour, red-fleshed apples and is dry, slightly tannic, and a great bridge to cider if you're a fan of sparkling rose wine. It makes a refreshing pairing for rich, creamy cheeses and a great apertif.

name: Jean-Louis Denois "Classique" Brut
tagline: Limoux, FR - Pinot Noir, Syrah, Chardonnay - NV
description: A joyous, fruit-driven sparkler from the foothills of the Pyrenees. Jean-Louis Denois blends Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, and a touch of Syrah to create a wine with fine bubbles, almond and dried red-berry notes, and surprising depth for the price. Crisp, clean, and thoroughly charming.

name: Lini 910 Lambrusco Rosso
tagline: Emilia-Romagna, IT - Lambrusco Salamino, Ancellotta - NV
description: This Lambrusco is totally dry, fully sparkling, and charming enough to make pizza swoon. The wine defies convention and dazzles the palate with lush berry notes and tinges of earthy spice. It’s the perfect wine for pizza lovers and oenophiles alike. A sip or two and you’ll understand why this wine is having a moment right now.

name: Son of Man "Sagardo" Cider
tagline: Columbia River Gorge. OR - 2021 - Apples

name: Carpano Antico Formula Vermouth
tagline: Essential to your Manhattan, Old Fashioned or Negroni!
description: What can we tell you about Antica that you don't already know? If you are like us, you can't resist those welcoming floral and vanilla notes- especially since Manhattans and Old Fashions are never out of season. Add the fact that you can't make a Negroni without it and it's not much of a choice anymore.

name: Moxie Mule Vermouth Bianco
tagline: Seattle, WA - NV - Grapes & Botanicals
description:
This handcrafted vermouth checks three stellar boxes for us: local, Black-owned, and absolutely delicious!

This white vermouth is a lot more complex than many in this category. Slightly sweet, featuring orange peel, golden raisins, vanilla, licorice root, jasmine, calendula red rose, and wormwood. This definitely isn't just for your martinis!

Enjoy this vermouth year-round in spritzes, cocktails, or on its own over ice.

name: Byrrh Grand Quinquina
description:
red-fruit digestive/aperitive

french

name: Cappelletti Apertivo
description: The Aperitivo Cappelletti, endearingly known to locals as just “Specialino”, may be the oldest style of the classic red bitter still in production. Unlike its larger commercial rivals, Cappelletti is less sweet and has a wonderful drying finish. Additionally, it still uses natural carmine color for a crimson red and retains a vinous texture from its wine base. It offers a vibrant and flavorful profile, complemented by bitter undertones on a traditional wine base. This yields a Negroni or Spritz that is dry and refreshing in the finish. It is made just outside of Trento in Alto Adige by the Cappelletti family, who also produce a number of other exceptional aperitivi and amari.

name: Cardamaro Vino Amaro
description: Cardamaro has the distinction of being the only wine bitter based on cardoon, an ingredient recognized as imperative to Piedmontese gastronomy. Warm spices, citrus, and floral notes give complexity and versatility to this amaro, and it can be enjoyed on its own with nuts and cheese as an aperitif or digestif. It also mixes well with ginger ale or whiskey, or it can be substituted for whiskey in a lighter-style Manhattan.

name: Cocchi Americano Bianco
description: Cocchi Americano was created in 1891 by Giulio Cocchi and since then produced without interruption according to the original recipe. Cocchi Bianco includes quinine and citrus for a flavorful, refreshing profile. In Piemonte it is served chilled with ice, a splash of soda and a peel of orange. The combination of fruit, spice and bitter undertones make is a fitting addition to many mixed cocktails. This same profile makes it splendid pairing with all kinds of pickles, nuts, charcuterie and cheeses.

name: Cocchi Americano Rosa
description: Cocchi Americano was created in 1891 by Giulio Cocchi and since then produced without interruption according to the original recipe. The name "Americano" is both due to the alcohol made bitter ("amaricato") by the addition of herbs and spices, and to the American habit of drinking vermouth with ice and soda. In Cocchi Americano Rosa, the Brachetto d'Acqui wine base provides the white rose and rich berry notes typical of the famous sparkling wine of the same variety, while the addition of rose and ginger to the traditional bitter base provides a rounder profile. Just add club soda or sparkling wine, or add a splash to cocktails for added depth.

name: Dolin Dry Vermouth
description: This iconic vermouth has been a staple across the Atlantic from its beginning, and was later immortalized by James Bond and his Dry Martini. Dry vermouth is still acclaimed by bartenders and mixologists from around the world. Slightly sweet, with a subtle golden tint, our dry vermouth has a generous and rich nose with hints of citrus bark underscored by the freshness of menthol and balsamic notes. Almond and stone fragrances dominate the slightly bitter citrus base and bring balance to the fine dry Vermouth de Chambéry.

name: Dolin Vermouth Blanc
description: The first white vermouth was created in Savoie in 1881. Sweet and aromatic, this Vermouth de Chambéry is a favorite for and remains a timeless symbol of elegance. It has clear brilliant color and a complex nose with aromas of freshly-picked Alpine botanicals, followed by camphor and then citrus notes. It has a pleasant harmony of botanical notes with a fine, silky texture. To complete the impression, the aromas of broom and elderflower in this white vermouth give way to notes of fresh almond and peach.

name: Dolin Vermouth Rouge
description: Dolin's red vermouth has a very long history, punctuated with many prizes and awards. It's recipe is unchanged since its inception. This vermouth has a lustrous coppery color, gentle aromas of fruit compote, prunes and walnuts with grassy notes, tempered by spicy aromas like Szechwan pepper. The hits keep coming with notes of almond, citrus, pear and cinnamon with gingerbread, and oregano.The very rich bouquet is tempered by a subtle bitter base wine. Perfect for your Negroni or Manhattan.

name: Lillet Blanc
description: Lillet Blanc is the original and most iconic apéritif in the LIllet line-up. Made mostly with Sémillon and Sauvignon grapes, it mixes beautifully in a simple spritz with an orange slice and elevates any classic cocktail. It has a floral aroma of mint & vanilla with flavors of candied orange, orange blossom, honey and pitted fruit.

name: Lillet Rose
description: With it's aromas of red berries, orange blossom & grapefruit, Lillet Rosé is a must-have for the spring and summer season! With its accessible, fresh and fruit-forward flavor, Lillet Rosé pairs perfectly with gin, tequila and Champagne!

name: Lillet Rouge
description: Compare to Lillet Blance, Lillet Rouge brings more fruit flavors and aromas for a richer, more deeply flavored experience. Made mostly with Merlot grapes, it has an aroma of ripe, dark fruits such as blackberry & plum. With flavors of fresh orange, ripe berries, vanilla & spice, its perfect for a spiced Sangria or your next Negroni!

name: Mattei Cap Corse Blanc, 750ml
description: A true Quinquina Blanc, and unique among aperitif wines. The profile of the Cap Corse Mattei BLANC aperitif wine is defined by its distinctly Corsican components. Its all-mistelle base is of Vermentinu and Muscat Petit Grains, lending a terrific minerality, acidity and floral tones. The local Cedrat (aka citron) adds unique citrus aroma and a silky texture. Since its creation in 1872 by Louis-Napoléon Mattei, Cap Corse Mattei is the oldest and best known aperitif of Corsica. Still today family owned, and all macerations, aging and bottling are done in house.

name: Mattei Cap Corse Rouge, 750ml
description: Among the most famous of French Quinquina, enjoyed for generations by visitors and residents of the Island of Corsica. It is composed of a variety of distinctive and aromatic spices, walnuts and cinchona bark on a base of Corsican Muscat and Vermentinu mistelles. The result is an aperitif of tremendous depth with a wonderfully dry finish. Traditionally served neat or on ice with tonic or soda. It mixes well with rye whiskey, apple brandy or brandy. Since its creation in 1872 by Louis-Napoléon Mattei, Cap Corse Mattei is the oldest and best known aperitif of Corsica. Still today family owned, and all macerations, aging and bottling are done in house.

name: Pasubio Vino Amaro
description: Pasubio is a true taste of the Dolomite Mountains in the Trentino region. On a base of rich aged wine you’ll find notes of blueberries, pine and smoke, together with bitter alpine herbs. It is rare among amari to feature mountain berries. The recipe from Giuseppe Cappelletti dates back to the early 20th century and is among the Erboristeria’s first amari. Traditionally enjoyed neat, typically at cellar temperature or chilled. Pasubio makes simple and delicious spritzes with tonic, soda, sparkling lemonade, or bitter lemon. Also pairs well in mixed drinks with bourbon, rye, or brandy.

name: Regal Rogue Lively White Vermouth
description: Regal Rogue Lively White is bursting with citrus and floral notes, marrying an Orange, organic un-wooded Chardonnay with native Lemon Myrtle, Desert Limes, Finger Limes and Native Thyme with Elderflower, Lemongrass, Grapefruit and Chamomile.It's semi-dry character make it perfect for citrusy, refreshing cocktails.

name: Trabanco Quinquina En Rama 750ml
tagline: Asturias, SP - Apples & Botanicals - NV
description: Like most families from the Asturian countryside, the Trabancos have always made their own cider from their own apples, but in 1925 Emilio Trabanco decided to turn this household hobby into a family business. Trabanco cider quickly became known throughout the region as the premier natural cider from Asturias. Alma is the perfect aperitif produced by the blending of en rama cider with white wine and various botanicals steeped in vinous alcohol. The primary botanicals in Alma de Trabanco include cinchona, wormwood, savory, gentian, artemisia, boldo, cinnamon, star anise, coriander, thyme, and vanilla. Fruits include cherry, orange peel, and lemon. The flavor profile is bright, refreshing, and satisfying.

name: DeLaurenti Roero Arneis DOCG
description:
Arneis is Piedmont’s native white, grown for centuries on the same hills that yield Barolo and Barbaresco. By the 1980s it had almost vanished, but a small band of growers nursed it back, and in the ’90s it re-emerged as Roero’s calling card - sometimes dubbed "Barolo bianco," though it needs no comparison to justify its place at the table.

This bottling comes from the sandy slopes of Santo Stefano Roero. It pours a bright straw yellow. The nose suggests fresh fruit and white flowers. On the palate it’s crisp and poised, with stone-fruit flavors giving way to a clean, mineral finish, typical of the Roero landscape.

Think of Arneis as a lively alternative to Sancerre or a Pinot Grigio with more nerve. Chill it lightly and pair with shellfish, grilled trout, or a simple roast chicken. It’s the sort of everyday white that makes summer meals feel complete.

name: Angiolino Maule Masieri Bianco
tagline: Veneto, IT - 2023 - Garganega
description: Angiolino Maule, a pioneer of natural winemaking in Italy, provides a delightful twist on Soave with his Masieri Bianco. Swirls of pear, citrus, and stone fruit are balanced by crisp acidity in this refreshing white wine. Our wine buyer, Tom Drake, says, “It’s like wine agua fresca. I love it.” This versatile Garganega-based gem pairs brilliantly with fresh salads, delicate seafood, or an afternoon by the pool.

name: Cardedu 'Nuo' Vermentino di Sardegna
tagline: Sardegna, IT - 2021 - Vermentino
description: Sardinian Vermentinos are known for their captivating balance of vivacity and depth, and this wine is no exception. The esteemed Cardedu estate delivers a quintessential example in this bright, citrusy Vermentino — Meyer lemon, tangerine zest, and delicate elderflower. A leesy texture adds complexity, while a touch of saline minerality lingers. The bright acidity makes it a versatile wine but we recommend it with grilled halibut or a plate of Linguine ai Frutti di Mare and pretending you’re dining al fresco on Sardinia’s sun-soaked, breezy coast.

name: Cirelli Vino da Tavola Bianco
tagline: Abruzzo, IT - NV - Trebbiano, Pecorino
description: Just because you're looking for an inexpensive, weeknight sort of wine, doesn't mean you should have to sacrifice flavor and quality. This wine blends Trebbiano and Pecorino (the grape, not to be confused with the cheese) for a light, snappy, refreshing white wine suitable for any occasion.

name: Cirelli Vino Orange
tagline: Abruzzo, IT - NV - Trebbiano
description:
Although orange wine may be having a moment, it isn't any more of a fad than white, red, or rosé wine. Despite its confusing name, the 'orange' in orange wine only refers to the color of the wine. You may also come across terms like amber wine or skin contact wine, and the three are synonymous. In order to make this style of wine, the winemaker leaves the white grape skins in contact with the grape juice for an extended period of time, like one does when making a red wine.

In this case, Cirelli macerates Trebbiano for about a month on its skins, followed by a soft pressing into stainless steel. What comes through in the bottle are subtle black tea tannins, a little bit of nectarine, and a mouth-watering, refreshing finish. This wine is sure to appease orange wine novices and afficianados alike!

name: Cor Cellars "Ago" Columbia Gorge Chardonnay
tagline: Lyle, WA - 2021 - Chardonnay
description: Cor makes several wines under the "Ago" label that highlight fruit from the Columbia Gorge. This is a dry, unoaked Chardonnay that shares a lot qualities with our favorite Alpine wines. Fittingly, this wine is great with all that Alpine cheese and Gouda in your basket, or with some PNW shellfish or salmon.

name: Domaine Billard Pere & Fils Bourgonge Blanc
tagline: Bourgogne, FR - 2021 - Chardonnay
description: Jerome Billiard brings a very holistic approach to the vineyard, eschewing the use of chemical fertilizers and plowing his rows with a horse. He allows the fruit to hang on the vine a little longer than most of his neighbors and allows his wines to ferment spontaneously, too, creating a Chardonnay here with a richer mouthfeel and concentration of fruit, without falling into the oaky and buttery side of things. This is a great wine for classic bistro fare - think roast chicken, hand-made sausages, and pates.

name: Domaine de Roally Viré-Clessé
tagline: Bourgogne, FR - Chardonnay - 2022
description: From the Thévenet family, this organically farmed Viré-Clessé ranks among the finest wines of the Mâconnais. Made from late-harvested old-vine Chardonnay, the 2022 shows vibrant acidity and steely minerality balanced by flavors of yellow apple and saline. Very dry with vibrant acidity, the finish of this wine lingers like a Mid-west Goodbye. Delicious now yet structured to age a decade or more. Wines of this quality from more prestigious parts of Bourgogne go for five or six times this price. One of our favorite white wines in the entire store.

name: Fidora Pinot Grigio Venezia DOC
tagline: Veneto, IT - 2021 - Pinot Grigio
description: Brimming with character, this crisp Pinot Grigio hails from a vast biodynamic estate in northern Italy. Delightful and budget-friendly, it boasts an inviting medley of citrus, green apple, and pear flavors. Share a bottle with friends or pair it with a scrumptious meal – this versatile gem shines on any occasion, echoing the charm of its Amarone sibling.

name: Graci Etna Bianco
tagline: Sicily, IT - 2023 - Carricante, Catarratto
description: As is the case with most Etna Bianco, Graci primarily utilizes Carricante and a splash of Catarratto. In effect, these grapes portray qualities similar to Chablis or great wines made from Vernaccia. The fruit comes from several contrada on Etna's northern slope, and the finished product from these volcanic vines is a crisp, mineral-driven white wine perfect for lighter, seafood-based pasta dishes. It's also a treat with the bounty of PNW seafood we're privy to in Seattle, and its natural citrus and flint aromas complement oysters perfectly.

name: Kiona Vineyards Chardonnay
tagline: Benton City, WA - 2018 - Chardonnay
description: Our friends at Kiona, who helped our House Red come to life, make a lot of fantastic wines. If you're in the market for a local Chardonnay that leans towards the richer end of the spectrum with just a slightly noticeable amount of oak, this is definitely the wine for you!

name: Le Chai Duchet 'The Berry Story' Macon Blanc
tagline: Bourgogne, FR - 2020 - Chardonnay
description: Le Chai Duchet's refreshingly dry Chardonnay hails from Southern Burgundy, delivering a flourish of tropical notes alongside crisp apple, an intriguing hint of yeastiness, and chalky minerality. Winemaker Alexis Duchet farms his family’s Mâcon vineyards organically. Biodynamic farming is challenging for the grapes, but excellent for the wine. Duchet’s Mâcon Blanc pairs nicely with freshly grilled seafood or creamy chicken dishes, making it an enchanting companion for a languid summer lunch.

name: Le Coste 'Due M' Moscato
tagline: Lazio, IT
description: Le Coste is a beautiful estate in Lazio, just a little outside Rome. The Due M cuvee is a blend of Moscato from two different sites- theirs, which is a mix of old and young vines, and from a friend who farms in a like-minded fashion. Their fruit goes through carbonic maceration and the sourced fruit does not. The result is a tropical, textured, orange wine that is incredibly dissimilar to the sweet Moscato wines found in the north. A delicious substitute for a light-bodied red at the table, we love it with Carbonara and Cacio e Pepe.

name: Le Fontane 'Calcis' Bianco
tagline: Sicily, IT - 2023 - Grillo, Insolia, Malvasia
description: Mediterranean white wines are so often a great choice because they present such versatility and approachability, especially considering the climate and cuisine of the Pacific Northwest. Le Fontane's 'Calcis' cuvée goes beyond simply being some "nice" choice, however, and excels when paired with halibut, shrimp, or other local shellfish. The wine is equal parts Grillo and Insolia, two grapes that bring equal parts wildflower and citrus-driven acidity, but there's also a splash of Malvasia in the blend that brings this gorgeous, tropical note to the front.

name: Le Monde Pinot Grigio
tagline: Friuli, IT - 2018 - Pinot Grigio
description: This Pinot Grigio from Friuli has all the bright, crisp fruit you'd expect and a mineral-driven, dry finish. A great daily-drinker to have on hand, this wine is also great with pesto-based pasta dishes or with some fresh panzanella.

name: Nanclares Y Prieto 'Dandelion' Albarino
tagline: Rias Baixus, ES - 2023 - Albarino
description: This Spanish white wine has this citrus and saline quality to it that perfectly complements sheep's milk cheeses, briney tinned fish, and jamon. It's incredibly refreshing but with a richer profile that lingers with minerality and fresh lemon zest.

name: Ridge Estate Chardonnay
tagline: Sonoma, CA - 2020 - Chardonnay
description: Silky elegance put California Chardonnay on the world map and this beauty by Ridge Estate is an exquisite example of just how good it can be. The winery embraces traditional winemaking and sustainability. This Chardonnay transcends oaky clichés, offering smooth sophistication that deftly balances soft, creamy pear and bright citrus notes. Pair it with a succulent roast chicken or buttery lobster risotto and settle into an evening of luxury.

name: Santola Vinho Verde
tagline: Vinho Verde DOC - Loureiro & Pederna - NV
description: This value-oriented gem hailing from Portugal's lush northwestern region is super fresh, bright, and slightly fizzy. Exhibiting vibrant notes of green apple, citrus, and subtle floral undertones, Santola Vinho Verde is suited for sipping solo or enjoying with friends, tapas, or appetizers. In a world where wine often takes itself too seriously, Santola Vinho Verde stands proud with an irreverent wink, an effervescent grin, and encourages you to raise a glass to the sheer delight of existence.

name: Savage Grace Columbia Gorge Chardonnay
tagline: Columbia Gorge, WA - Chardonnay - 2022
description: From a Certified Organic Columbia Gorge vineyard, fermented in neutral French oak barrels. It offers refreshing acidity, minerality, medium body and intense flavors. Salmon? Yes. Food optional? Also yes.

name: Savage Grace Red Willow Vineyard Sauvignon Blanc
tagline: Yakima Valley, WA - 2022 - Sauvignon Blanc
description: Savage Grace makes fantastic wines from fruit sourced from the Yakima Valley, Columbia Gorge, and Walla Walla. This Sauvignon Blanc comes from the famed Red Willow Vineyard and is the perfect bridge between Washington Sauvignon Blanc and Sancerre. Less melon and tropical fruit, a lot more minerality. Whether looking for local or imported wines, this is always a top choice for a seafood pairing.

name: Travis Tausend "Agori" Chardonnay
tagline: Fleurieu, AU - 2021 - 100% Chardonnay
description: Aussie wines often get (unfairly) overlooked due to the American market being flooded with mass produced “not so great” wines from our friends down under. Let your mind erase those thoughts here and now with this amazing Chardonnay from young maverick, Travis Tausend. You can show off this “new world” beauty to your most discerning friends and discover the potential this region is flexing!

name: Via Alpina Friuli Pinot Grigio DOC
tagline: Friuli, IT - 2022 - Pinot Grigio
description: Step beyond ordinary Pinot Grigio with this delightful beauty from Venica & Venica's second label. This wine has a racy, refreshing profile. Immerse yourself in a whirlwind of crunchy fresh fruit flavors – Anjou pear, green apple, and a subtle touch of citrus zest. Elevating the everyday, this vibrant palate-pleaser redefines the standard for Pinot Grigio — and it’s soooooooooooo much better than most on the market.

name: Raclette de Compton au Poivre - 2024 ACS Best in Show!
tagline: Raw Cow - Fromagerie la Station - Quebec, Canada
description: Fromagerie la Station’s journey to award-winning cheesemaking began with Alfred and Aglaé Bolduc’s 1928 arrival to the town of Compton in Québec province. Four generations later, the Bolduc family is still working the same land, now making farmstead organic cheeses and harvesting maple syrup. Best in Show winner at the American Cheese Society’s 2024 competition, Raclette de Compton au Poivre has a copper-colored washed rind, a supple golden paste, and a line of pink peppercorns running through the center of the cheese. The aromas of apple, chestnut, and butter open even more when heated. Perfect for melting over boiled potatoes, crusty bread, cornichons, and cured meats!

name: Isle of Mull Cheddar
tagline: Raw Cow - Reade Family/Neal's Yard Dairy - Isle of Mull, Scotland
description: What happened when a couple of Somerset natives relocated to the Isle of Mull? They built a farm and the island's only creamery. After production, Isle of Mull Cheddar is aged by Neal's Yard in London for about 18 months. Depending on time of year, this farmstead cheddar can vary in color from pale yellow to bright white. Occasionally natural blue veining will occur, but don't let this deter you; consider it a tasty bonus! Complexly flavored, Isle of Mull is at once sharp, tangy, fruity and earthy.

name: Poggio la Noce 2025 EVOO, 500ml
tagline: New Harvest 2025! This was an olive a few short weeks ago!
description: It's here... the 2025 Harvest!! We look forward to this oil coming out every fall - it is truly an amazing representation of true Tuscan olive oil. With hints of freshly cut grass, almonds & artichokes, it's not just one of our favorite oils, it happens to be produced by a couple of our favorite people - husband and wife team, Enzo Schiano and Claire Beliard. The olives from their 1,500 tree grove are hand-picked and pressed on the estate the same day. This helps to preserve all the intense flavor and fragrance of the olives and ensures the lowest grade of acidity possible. This oil was in it's olive state just a few short weeks ago, and in a few more short weeks, it will be gone...get it while you can, when it's gone, it's gone!

name: Spedalotto Tonda Iblea Olio Novello 1025, 500ml
tagline: This oil was an olive a mere 3 weeks ago!
description: Made with the famous Tonda Iblea olives of the Monti Iblei region in Sicily. This amazing oil has green, ripe flavors that are in perfect balance. It is soft with a fresh, green tomato aroma and fruity flavor, like a perfectly ripe late summer heirloom tomato. A delightful complexity is extracted from this single varietal olive, a result of the craftsmanship that goes into the cultivation of rich soil. Spedalotto Tonda Iblea’s approachable flavor profile is easy to love!

name: La Florentine Marron Glace, 7oz
description: La Florentine candied chestnuts a sweet/savory treat that will for sure go well with that glass of port or gelato after dinner.

name: Coufidou Prunes, 450g
tagline: Agen Prunes Stuffed with Prunes Mousse
description: The stuffed Prunes of Agen (Pruneaux d’Agen Fourrés) are a classic holiday delicacy, ranking as one of the most prestigious gifts in France. Splendid, full-bodied Agen Prunes are pitted, dried, gently rehydrated, and—delight of delights—filled generously with a smooth purée of their own fruit, delicately flavored with lemon peel and vanilla. Perfect as a sweet foil to cooked game, as a succulent side to foie gras, or served with Armagnac or Banyuls wine at the end of a meal. These prunes also pair beautifully with a cup of Mariage Frères tea for an afternoon treat. Each round tin contains 12 prunes filled with prune mousse.

name: Il Cassero Panforte Bianco, 250g
description: Il Cassero panforte is a dense, traditional Tuscan "strong bread" that has a long history in Tuscany.t is full of nuts, spices, candied fruits, and honey. Pairs well with an aged pecorino or a glass of Vin Santo!

name: Il Cassero Panforte Chocolate & Cherry, 250g
description: Il Cassero panforte is a dense, traditional Tuscan "strong bread" that has a long history in Tuscany. It is full of nuts, spices, candied fruits, and honey, while also featuring chocolate and cherries. Pairs very well with Vin Santo!

name: Il Cassero Panforte Trio, 300g
description: Il Cassero panforte is a dense, traditional Tuscan "strong bread" that has a long history in Tuscany. Can't decide on one flavor? How about a small sampling of each! This pack comes with the classic, fig & chocolate, and a savory version with black pepper.

name: La Florentine Assorted Torrone, 18pc
description: This soft nougat candy has been a mainstay at DeLaurenti for generations. Although this candy is commonly found in the toe of your stocking on Christmas, it is available here at our store the other 364 days of the year as well. Prepared with the finest crunchy almonds, smooth golden honey, pure cane sugar and fluffy egg whites, it will transport you back to your childhood. Each box contains eighteen individually packaged candies - 6 orange, 6 lemon and 6 vanilla.

name: Fabbri Amarena Cherries in Syrup, 120g
tagline: The Classic Amarena Cherry in Syrup!
description: The Fabbri Company of Bologna has been making uniquely delicious cherries in amarena syrup for over a century. Only the best wild cherries are carefully selected and candied in amarena syrup according to Gennaro Fabbri's original recipe, created in 1905. Eat them straight out of the crock, add them to cobblers and cakes, or top a perfect bowl of vanilla ice cream.

name: Antonio Mattei Almond Biscotti, 250g
description: Since 1858, Antonio Mattei has been producing Italian biscotti and confections in their historical bakery and shop located on Via Ricasoli, in the heart of the old city of Prato, Tuscany. The bakery has been run by the Pandolfini family for 3 generations. Throughout Tuscany, these biscotti are considered the standard-bearer. Their size, texture and taste are synonymous with quality and tradition. Made only with flour, farm fresh eggs which impart a golden yellow color, sugar, almonds, and pine nuts. Traditionally enjoyed at the end of a meal with a glass of Vin Santo, they are also perfect with coffee, gelato or panna cotta.

name: Lazzaroni Amaretti di Saronno Amaretti Snaps, 7oz
description: From the folks that know their amaretti. These cookies are crisp and snappy as the name would suggest. A perfet compliment to a bowl of vanilla gelato/ice cream, or crumbled on the top of your tiramisu for a amaretti-filled crunchy victory!

description: Since 1718, the Lazzaroni family has crafted amaretti cookies according to their family's traditional recipe. Individually wrapped in pairs with their distinctive paper, these crisp and airy cookies are perfect with coffee, wine or after dinner liqueurs.

name: Rinati Brigidini, 200g
description: Since the late 1800s, Rinati has been producing the classic Brigidino following the traditional Tuscan recipe. They are crisp and not too sweet with a unique aniseed aroma. If you have a nonna, you have seen her eating these.

name: Rinati Cialde de Montecatini, 225g
tagline: The Tuscan Specialty!
description: These Cialde di Montecatini (waffles of Montecatini) are a Tuscan specialty perfectly suited for coffee, gelato or cocktails! Old school confection at it's best.These aren't your I-hop waffles folks. They are 2 thin, crisp wafers sandwiching a thin layer of not too sweet crumbly almond paste. They will crumble, but then you will pick up all the crumbles and enjoy eating them.

name: DeLaurenti Classic Chocolate Chip Cookie
description: A lot has been said about this cookie. We think it's the best around. It's won awards and been enjoyed by thousands of our important customers. Buy one, you won't be disappointed.

name: DeLaurenti Chocolate Hazelnut Cookie
description: The fans of this cookie are an elite group. We love them, and we love this cookie. Yes, you can pretend that you are only going to eat half and save the rest for after dinner. There's no judgement here, and there are plenty of roasted hazelnuts for protein.

name: DeLaurenti Peanutbutter Cookie
description: Our most underrated cookie. A cafe classic. Rich peanut butter with the subtle crunch of flaky sea salt on top...enough said.
